description: We are a company specializing in custom plush toy production, working with creators, brands, and communities worldwide. We create unique plush products in collaboration with influencers, fandoms, and companies — and we are looking for a Research Specialist to help us find the best potential partners. ======================================== ROLE OVERVIEW ======================================== Your main task is to research and identify high-quality leads (potential partners) who would be a great fit for custom plush toy collaborations. You will explore the internet, find promising creators/brands, and gather the most important information about them. ======================================== RESPONSIBILITIES ======================================== • Research and identify potential partners: - YouTubers, Twitch streamers, TikTok creators - Bands and musicians - Online communities and fandoms - Video game developers - Brands and companies • Collect and organize key information: - Contact details (email, social media, websites) - Audience size and engagement - Niche relevance and brand fit - Best way to contact (manager, email, DMs, etc.) • Continuously improve research quality and find better opportunities ======================================== IMPORTANT: UNDERSTANDING WHAT MAKES A GOOD LEAD ======================================== We are NOT simply looking for creators with large audiences. We are specifically looking for creators, brands, games, mascots, characters, or communities that can realistically be turned into strong plush products that fans would actually want to buy. A good lead usually has: - Recognizable characters, mascots, avatars, creatures, or visual identities - Strong emotional connection between audience and character - ---------- able, cute, funny, iconic, or collectible visual elements - Existing fandom culture around specific characters or designs Examples of weak leads: - Generic beauty influencers with no recognizable mascot/character - Creators whose content is only their real-life personality without visual branding - Random large gaming communities without a clear character or mascot Examples of strong leads: - Creators with animated personas, mascots, or lore - Games with recognizable creatures or characters - Communities built around iconic designs or ---------- s - Brands with mascots or collectible-style aesthetics The most important question is: “Can this realistically become a plush toy that fans would immediately recognize and want to collect?” ======================================== REQUIREMENTS ======================================== • Good English skills • Good internet research skills • High attention to detail • Good understanding of social media platforms (YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram, etc.) • Ability to understand niche communities and fanbases • Ability to identify trends and promising creators ======================================== WORKING HOURS ======================================== • 3 hours per day • Flexible schedule (please include your availability) ======================================== HOW TO APPLY ======================================== Please include: 1. A short introduction about yourself 2. Your relevant experience 3. Your email and other contact information 5. REQUIRED: Include 3 sample leads you personally researched. For EACH sample lead, you MUST include: - Who the creator/brand/community is - Links/socials - Why you believe they are a strong fit for plush merchandise - WHAT specifically could be turned into a plush product - Why fans would likely buy it Very important: Answers like “they have a big community” or “they are popular in gaming” are NOT enough. We want to see clear thinking about the actual plush potential. Good applications explain things like: - Specific characters or mascots - ---------- s, creatures, avatars, or visual branding - Emotional attachment within the fandom - Why the design would work physically as a plush - Why it would feel collectible or appealing to fans We are looking for someone detail-oriented, curious, and motivated to find great opportunities.

Extract scope requirements, forms, certifications, submittals, deadlines, and compliance requirements. Identify required trades and subcontractors. Research and source qualified subcontractors in the project geography, including unfamiliar markets. Contact subcontractors by phone and email to discuss scope and obtain pricing. Communicate scope requirements, site requirements, payment terms, personnel requirements, and quote deadlines. Collect, organize, compare, and evaluate subcontractor proposals. Identify exclusions, scope gaps, pricing inconsistencies, and items requiring clarification. Follow up persistently with subcontractors to obtain quotes before internal deadlines. Prepare bid schedules, unit-price tables, and required government forms accurately and on time. Phone outreach is a significant part of this position. You must be comfortable speaking directly with U.S. subcontractors and contractors. General Contractor / GC Bids The client also bids self-performed work directly to national and regional general contractors, including: Post-construction cleaning Rough and final cleaning Interior and exterior glass Pressure washing Division 9 and Division 10 scopes Related facility and finishing services You will: Monitor invitations to bid through email and GC bid platforms. Review ITBs, plans, specifications, and project schedules. Identify the complete scope of work, including requirements located in other specification sections. Complete GC bid forms accurately, including alternates, unit prices, allowances, sales tax treatment, bond and insurance requirements, union status, parking requirements, and project-specific exhibits. Prepare and submit proposals to GC estimating and preconstruction contacts. Confirm receipt of submitted bids. Follow up consistently with GCs until the opportunity is awarded or closed. Track bid-date changes, competitiveness, expected award timing, and feedback. Maintain a live log of outstanding GC quotes, including project, GC, contact, value, submission date, last contact, next follow-up date, and status. Support scope clarification and change-order documentation on awarded projects. ESTIMATING & BID COORDINATION Across both workstreams, you will: Review lengthy construction documents and quickly identify critical requirements. Extract and organize information from complex project documents. Build and maintain multi-tab Excel pricing workbooks. Use linked formulas properly rather than hardcoding values where formulas belong. Verify that inputs flow correctly through dependent tabs before submission. Maintain accurate estimating, bid, subcontractor, and quote records. Manage multiple active bids and competing deadlines simultaneously. Communicate professionally with subcontractors, vendors, GCs, contracting officers, and other stakeholders. Use AI and other technology tools to improve document review, research, sourcing, and estimating workflows. CONFIDENTIALITY & DOCUMENT CONTROL Confidentiality is a non-negotiable requirement of this role. Ensure unredacted project details are released only when authorized. Clearly identify documents as internal or external before sending them outside the company. Ensure client-facing documents contain only approved billing information. Never disclose internal cost data, margins, payroll information, or other confidential information to clients, GCs, or subcontractors. Properly communicate and enforce non-circumvention requirements in subcontractor correspondence. REMOTE WORK & HUBSTAFF This is a fully remote position supporting a U.S.-based construction client. Hubstaff will be used for time tracking and work activity monitoring. You must be comfortable working independently in a structured remote environment and maintaining consistent productivity during scheduled U.S. business hours. You are expected to: Accurately track working hours through Hubstaff. Remain available during agreed working hours. Maintain reliable communication with the client and team. Respond promptly to time-sensitive bid and subcontractor matters. Meet deadlines without constant follow-up. Take ownership of assigned bids from start to finish. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 5+ years of experience in construction estimating, bid coordination, construction procurement, or a closely related role. Demonstrated experience reading and interpreting PWS, SOWs, specifications, plans, or other construction documents. Hands-on experience sourcing subcontractors and discussing scope and pricing by phone. Strong Excel skills, particularly multi-tab workbooks with linked formulas. Strong spoken and written English. Professional and confident phone presence. Experience managing multiple bids, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously. Strong organization and follow-through. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. Availability during U.S. business hours across multiple time zones. Ability to make and receive calls through a U.S.-reachable phone number. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS The following are a strong advantage: Experience with federal procurement and ---------- . Familiarity with CLIN structures, set-asides, bid schedules, and wage determinations. Knowledge of Service Contract Act (SCA) and Davis-Bacon requirements. Experience with GC bid invitation platforms. Experience with post-construction cleaning, Division 9/10 trades, or facility services. Experience performing quantity takeoffs from drawings. Familiarity with Bluebeam or construction estimating software. Experience using AI tools for document review, research, sourcing, or estimating. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR We're looking for a construction professional who can hit the ground running. You should be someone who: Understands construction documents rather than simply processing them. Can identify scope gaps and potential issues. Is comfortable speaking directly with U.S. contractors and subcontractors. Can source subcontractors in unfamiliar markets. Can evaluate and normalize competing quotes. Can manage several active bids without losing track of deadlines. Follows up proactively instead of waiting for responses. Takes ownership and keeps the bid pipeline moving. Knows when to make a recommendation and when to escalate a decision. If your experience is primarily administrative or data-entry based, this is not the right role. If you have genuine construction estimating experience and enjoy the challenge of getting bids across the finish line, we want to hear from you. SCOPE OF AUTHORITY You will own the estimating and bid coordination process, but you will not have final authority over pricing or contractual commitments. You will prepare, organize, analyze, and recommend, but you will not: Set final pricing or margins. Make final bid/no-bid decisions. Sign or commit the company to a subcontractor, general contractor, or government agency. The expectation is ownership of the process, not authority over the final number. SELECTION PROCESS Shortlisted candidates will be evaluated through practical work samples, not interview answers alone. Candidates may be asked to complete: 1. Document Extraction Exercise Given a 40–60 page PWS, produce a one-page summary within one hour identifying: Scope Required trades Submittals and forms Site visit date Q&A deadline Bid due date, time, and time zone 2. Subcontractor Outreach Exercise Given a live solicitation, prepare the outreach package you would use to contact subcontractors. 3. Quote Normalization Exercise Given three subcontractor quotes with different inclusions, exclusions, and units, prepare an apples-to-apples comparison and identify the questions you would send back to each subcontractor. 4. Live Call / Role Play Participate in a short scope and pricing call to assess your communication skills and phone presence. APPLICATION QUESTION Please answer this question in your application: Walk us through the most recent federal solicitation or GC bid package you personally worked on. What was the project, what was your role, and what did you personally produce? Please provide specific details about your hands-on work. Generic descriptions of your previous employer's responsibilities will not be sufficient. READY TO TAKE OWNERSHIP OF THE BID PROCESS? If you have real construction estimating experience, strong construction document skills, confidence communicating with U.S. contractors, and the ability to manage multiple bids independently, we'd like to hear from you. To apply: Complete the application form. Upload your updated CV. Submit your short introduction video. Answer the application question about the most recent federal solicitation or GC bid package you personally worked on. Please be specific about your hands-on experience. We are looking for someone who has actually worked on construction bids—not someone who has only provided general administrative support. Apply Here – ----------

Reporting & Business Support Assist with tracking important business metrics and activities. Help prepare reports and structured updates for leadership. Monitor information such as leads, activities, projects, and campaign progress. Keep information organized so leadership and the team have visibility into what is happening. 5. Marketing & Light Creative Support Assist with content organization, research, and basic marketing activities. Support social media updates, analytics tracking, and content planning. Assist with transcription of audio or video content and newsletter preparation when needed. Conduct research on trends, content ideas, and potential marketing opportunities. 6. Customer & Client Administrative Support Assist with collecting client feedback and coordinating review requests. Help identify missing follow-ups or gaps in client communication. Support administrative activities that contribute to an organized and positive client experience. 7. Cross-Team Collaboration & General Support Work collaboratively with leadership and different areas of the business rather than operating independently from the team. Participate in team conversations, meetings, and shared initiatives. Communicate openly about progress, questions, challenges, and opportunities to help. Provide administrative support across recruiting, operations, marketing, and leadership without necessarily owning those functions. Help organize workflows, monitor deliverables, and maintain internal systems. Step in and support teammates when appropriate and when priorities shift. Identify inefficiencies and proactively suggest ways to improve processes and teamwork. What We’re Looking For The ideal candidate is: Highly collaborative and team-oriented – enjoys working with people, contributing to conversations, and being part of a shared goal. Proactive – notices what needs attention and takes initiative instead of always waiting for instructions. Organized and detail-oriented – able to manage multiple moving pieces without losing track of important details. Reliable with follow-through – takes ownership of commitments and closes the loop. Communicative – provides updates, asks questions, and raises concerns early. Adaptable – comfortable supporting different areas of the business as priorities evolve. People-focused – understands that relationships and teamwork are just as important as completing individual tasks. Comfortable with technology – able to learn and work within CRM, project management, communication, and productivity tools. Success in This Role Success is not measured only by how many tasks are completed. We are looking for someone who becomes a trusted and engaged member of the team. The right person will help keep the business organized while also building strong working relationships, communicating consistently, contributing ideas, supporting teammates, and taking shared ownership of the team's success.

Relevant certification (e.g., Google Ads Certification) and a background in marketing, business, communications, or related field are preferred. WHAT YOU WILL DO Own the Google Search book Roughly 17 active Google Ads accounts. Campaign builds and restructures, keyword and search term management, negative keyword hygiene, ad copy testing, bid strategy selection and tuning, and Performance Max where it earns its place. You d ---------- what runs, and you are accountable for what it costs. Own the Local Services Ads book Ten accounts on LSA, including multi-location businesses running LSA across several service areas at once. Budget pacing, lead review and disputes, ranking factors, Google Business Profile alignment, and keeping cost per genuine lead honest rather than cost per charged lead. Callrail Management You are the person who sets up and maintains CallRail for every client: tracking numbers and dynamic number insertion, number pool sizing, routing and call flows, source attribution, spam filtering, and keeping the lead qualification honest. When a client's number pool is too small or their DNI is not swapping, that is yours to catch. Google Tag Manager Setup and Maintenance Container structure, tags, triggers, variables and the data layer. Conversion tracking setup and auditing across Google Ads, GA4 and CallRail, including offline and imported conversions. You are the one who can open a container and say why something fires twice. Meta campaign management and creative direction (not required) Six accounts. Campaign structure, audiences, budget and optimization, plus writing clear creative briefs for our design team and reviewing what comes back. You direct the creative, you do not build it. Client recommendations Explaining performance to non-marketers in plain language, and bringing a recommendation rather than a dashboard. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Real hands-on Google Ads depth. You have personally managed accounts, not directed someone who did. You know why you chose Target CPA over Maximize Conversions in a specific account, and what you did when the learning period went sideways. Genuine LSA experience Hands-on CallRail and GTM. Not "I've seen the dashboard." You should be able to size a number pool, diagnose DNI that is not swapping, and open a GTM container you did not build and work out what fires when. Skepticism about data. Conversion counts inflate for boring reasons: duplicate tags, form-fill double-counting, call tracking misconfiguration, a client's team calling their own tracking number. We want someone whose first instinct on good news is to verify it. Comfort at scale. Managing 28 campaigns means triage. You need a repeatable way to know which accounts need you this week and which do not. Directness. If a client is spending in the wrong place, we would rather hear it from you in week two than in the quarterly review. WHO DOES WELL HERE Someone accountable, because there is no one between you and the spend. Someone organized enough to hold a book this size without things quietly drifting. Someone who is comfortable telling a client something they do not want to hear, and who follows it with a specific alternative. No email or message applications will be accepted. description: Hey! I'm looking for a skilled video editor to create long-form videos for a YouTube channel focused on discovering the best places to live, retire, invest, and explore across different U.S. states. The channel covers topics like the best small towns, underrated hidden gems, retirement destinations, affordable places to live, real estate opportunities, fast-growing areas, and towns worth knowing about before everyone else does. The videos should feel informative, visually engaging, and curiosity-driven — not like a basic slideshow or generic travel video. The goal is to make viewers feel like they are discovering places and opportunities they haven't heard about yet. Look at these chanel for example: ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- ### About this channel This channel is focused on U.S. states, cities, small towns, and emerging destinations. Typical video topics include: * Best towns to live in a specific state * Hidden gems most people don't know about * Best retirement towns * Affordable places to buy a home * Underrated real estate markets * Fast-growing towns and communities * Places people are moving to * Small towns with a great quality of life * Places worth knowing before they become popular * Best places for retirees, families, remote workers, or investors Scripts and voice-over will be provided by me. You will not need to record or direct any voice talent — the finished voice-over track will be delivered to you ready to edit around. Your job is to turn the script and narration into a professional, engaging YouTube video using relevant real-world footage, images, maps, graphics, and other visual material. ### Visual style The visuals should match exactly what is being discussed. For example, if the narration is talking about a specific town, I want to see footage or images of that actual town whenever possible — its downtown, neighborhoods, nature, homes, local attractions, streets, surrounding landscape, and lifestyle. When the script discusses topics such as real estate, cost of living, population growth, location, weather, or nearby cities, you can use: * Real footage of the location * Stock footage * Local photos * Maps and Google Maps-style animations * Aerial/drone footage * Real estate and housing visuals * Charts or simple graphics * Text animations * Screenshots or other relevant visual references when appropriate Please avoid using random stock footage that has nothing to do with the town or location being discussed. Accurate visual sourcing is very important for this channel. ### The job Video length: around 25 minutes I provide: * Complete script * Finished voice-over * Timestamps if needed You provide: * Full video editing * Sourcing relevant footage and images * Town/city/location footage * Maps and location animations * Real estate and housing visuals when relevant * Text animations and motion graphics * Smooth transitions * Background music * Sound effects * Subtitles/captions where appropriate * Final exported video ready for YouTube The editing should keep the viewer engaged throughout the entire video. Every town or location should feel visually different, and the visuals should help tell the story instead of simply filling the screen. Good pacing and visual variety are very important. Pay: $25 per completed video, paid per delivered video Turnaround: 2 days per video, to be discussed once we start working together Revisions: Unlimited revisions until the video is right Volume: I plan to upload 3 videos per week and I'm looking for someone for a long-term working relationship. Consistency is very important. If the first videos perform well and we work well together, there will be ongoing work every week. Before we start, can you make a sample of around 5 minutes for me? This will help me see your editing style, visual selection, pacing, maps, text animations, and how well you can turn the script into an engaging video.

title: ADS MANAGER
description: Paid Ads Manager We are looking for an experienced Paid Ads Manager to join our creative agency, managing advertising campaigns across a varied portfolio of clients in hospitality, events, wellness, professional services and other industries. This role requires someone who can plan, build, monitor and improve campaigns while communicating results clearly. You should be comfortable managing multiple accounts, working to quick deadlines and adapting campaigns as client priorities, budgets and creative assets change. Key Responsibilities Plan, build and manage paid advertising campaigns across Meta Ads and Google Ads. Develop campaign strategies based on each client’s goals, audience and available budget. Manage campaigns focused on lead generation, bookings, sales, website traffic, awareness and event promotion. Build suitable campaign, ad-set and audience structures. Set up prospecting, retargeting and remarketing campaigns. Complete audience, keyword and competitor research. Work with the creative team to identify effective messaging, formats and advertising assets. Write and test clear, persuasive ad copy. Monitor campaign performance, budgets and pacing. Test different creative assets, audiences, placements and campaign objectives. Optimise campaigns based on reliable performance data. Set up and review tracking through Meta Pixel, Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and platform conversion tools. Troubleshoot tracking, attribution, account-access and campaign-delivery issues. Produce clear reports that explain performance, insights and recommended next steps. Manage multiple advertising accounts within a fast-moving agency environment. Respond professionally to feedback and adjust campaigns as client requirements develop. Essential Requirements Minimum of two years’ professional paid advertising experience. Intermediate to advanced knowledge of Meta Ads Manager. Strong working knowledge of Google Ads. Experience managing campaigns across multiple client accounts. Understanding of campaign objectives, audience targeting, bidding, budgets and attribution. Experience with lead-generation, conversion, booking and ecommerce campaigns. Good knowledge of Meta Pixel, Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager. Ability to evaluate key metrics such as CPM, CTR, CPC, CPA, ROAS and conversion rate. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent attention to detail when building, monitoring and reporting on campaigns. Very high standard of written and spoken English. Ability to write clear and effective advertising copy. Strong communication skills and a professional approach to client feedback. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, budgets and campaigns simultaneously. Reliable access to high-speed internet and a suitable remote working environment. The Ideal Candidate You are commercially aware, organised and comfortable taking responsibility for advertising performance. You can move beyond simply launching campaigns and explain what is working, what is not working and what should happen next. You understand the relationship between creative quality, audience targeting, campaign structure and the customer journey. You are confident making decisions based on data while recognising when a campaign needs stronger creative, a better offer or an improved landing page. You communicate clearly, manage budgets carefully and keep accounts structured so campaign activity can be easily reviewed by the wider team. Application Please include: A short introduction outlining your paid advertising experience. Examples of campaigns or accounts you have managed. Relevant results, including budget ranges and key performance improvements. Details of your experience with Meta Ads and Google Ads. Examples of your tracking and analytics experience. Any relevant certifications. Your general availability and typical reporting process.

title: Facebook Ads Video Editor
description: We're looking for a video editor who understands one thing clearly: A good ad doesn't just look nice. It stops the scroll, holds attention, builds desire, and gets people to take action. We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand creating products for sleep, recovery, and natural pain relief, and paid social is one of our main growth channels. That means video creative is not just "content" for us, it's one of the biggest drivers of the business. We're looking for an editor who can help us create high-performing video ads for Facebook, Instagram, and other paid channels. This role is ideal for someone who understands direct-response editing, UGC-style ads, fast testing, strong hooks, emotional storytelling, and conversion-focused creative. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE EDITING --- You'll be working on video ads designed specifically for e-commerce performance, including: - Facebook and Instagram ads: scroll-stopping videos built to grab attention quickly and drive purchases - UGC-style ad creatives: native-feeling videos that look organic, believable, and platform-friendly - Product demonstration videos: clear, benefit-driven edits that show the product in action - Customer testimonial ads: emotional, trust-building edits using reviews, before/after moments, and social proof - VSL-style ads and advertorial videos: longer-form sales videos built around education and direct-response structure - Creative variations for testing: different hooks, openings, captions, CTAs, angles, pacing, and structures --- WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR --- We're not looking for a "cinematic" editor who only cares about pretty visuals. We're looking for someone who understands how ads work. You should know how to edit videos that: - Stop people in the first 1-3 seconds - Make the problem feel real and urgent - Show the product clearly and persuasively - Use captions, cuts, zooms, overlays, and b-roll to maintain attention - Feel native to Facebook and Instagram - Communicate benefits quickly and clearly - Build trust using reviews, testimonials, and social proof - Guide the viewer toward a click or purchase You should be able to take a script, raw footage, UGC clips, product shots, reviews, references, and creative notes... then turn them into a polished ad ready for testing. --- THE KIND OF EDITOR WHO WILL THRIVE HERE --- You'll be a strong fit if you: - Have experience editing video ads for e-commerce brands - Understand direct-response marketing and paid social creative - Can create multiple ad variations quickly - Know how to follow references without copying them blindly - Have a good instinct for hooks, pacing, retention, and emotional flow - Can make simple footage feel compelling and conversion-focused - Are comfortable receiving feedback and iterating fast - Care about whether your videos actually perform, not just whether they look good We care about creative that sells. That doesn't mean ugly or low-quality. It means every editing choice should support the message, the emotion, and the conversion. --- SKILLS & EXPERIENCE --- Ideally, you have experience with: - Meta/Facebook ad creatives - Short-form paid social videos - Long-form VSLs or sales videos - Captioning, motion graphics, overlays, b-roll, sound design, and pacing - Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, DaVinci, or similar tools Bonus if you've worked with sleep, recovery, or natural pain relief. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY --- - Editing new ad creatives from scripts, footage, UGC clips, and references - Creating variations of winning ads for further testing - Improving hooks, pacing, captions, visuals, and CTAs - Adapting creatives for different platforms and aspect ratios - Collaborating with the marketing and creative team to improve performance - Using feedback from ad results to make stronger iterations --- WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU --- - $1,500 per month, full-time (40 hours per week), fully remote - Performance-based bonuses for strong creatives - The opportunity to work on ads that directly drive revenue - Clear creative direction and fast feedback - Long-term growth with a brand aiming to scale aggressively We're building a serious e-commerce brand, and we're looking for an editor who knows how to create ads that get attention, build trust, and convert. If you're an e-commerce ad video editor who understands performance creative, we'd love to hear from you. --- HOW TO APPLY --- All applications go through this form. It's the only way to be considered: ---------- It takes about 10 minutes and requires a short video introduction. Applications sent as a message, without completing the form, will not be reviewed.

title: Data Scientist
description: // The work We make financial research videos. You build the data layer underneath them: pulling the numbers, cleaning them, and turning them into charts and information design that titles, thumbnails, and scripts get built on. Most of this job is code. You'll be scraping SEC filings, hitting APIs, wrangling messy financial data into something structured, and producing charts from it. If you can't write the prompt that gets the data, this role won't work. You don't need to be a finance expert. You need to be fluent with data and fast at learning. We teach you the rest. /// What you'll do Pull data from filings, APIs, and the web — write the scraper, handle the pagination, deal with the garbage formatting. Clean and structure it. Reconcile inconsistencies across sources and periods. Build charts and information design from it. Not screenshots of spreadsheets — designed visuals. Dig into a trend and figure out what's actually in the data. Come back with a finding, not a dump. Help shape the angle: what's the story, and why should anyone care. Chase answers on your own. Come back with progress, not just questions. /// What we need Python and pandas. Comfortable, not "I did a course." You've built things. Real scraping experience — requests/BeautifulSoup/Playwright, whatever you use. You've dealt with sites that don't want to be scraped. You can produce a chart in code (matplotlib, plotly, D3, Observable — your choice) and you have taste about how it looks. SQL is a plus. JavaScript is a plus. Working with financial data is a plus. High agency. You move without being told. You go one layer deeper than asked. Clear written English. We work async. We can teach the domain. We can't teach agency, and we're not teaching you to code. /// Not for you if Your data work stops at Excel. You need a BI tool to make a chart. You need every task fully specified. You go quiet when you get stuck. /// To apply Start with the word CADMIUM so we know you read this far. Then do this, it should take you under an hour: Pick any US-listed company. Pull its last 8 quarters of revenue from its SEC filings — by code, not by hand. Make one chart from it. Send us the code and the chart. We don't care if the chart is beautiful. We care that the data came out of a script you wrote, and that the chart makes one point clearly. Also tell us: one thing you taught yourself recently, and how. We read applications that follow these steps. We skip the ones that don't.

title: Meta Ads Specialist
description: We are seeking an experienced and data-driven Full-Time Meta Ads Specialist to lead the strategy, execution, and optimization of all paid social advertising campaigns across Meta platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger) for a portfolio of diverse agency clients. This is a highly strategic, client-facing role that requires a mastery of performance marketing fundamentals combined with a strong creative intuition and a dedication to staying ahead of platform algorithm shifts. The ideal candidate not only knows how to execute, but is also fluent in the latest AI-driven delivery systems, such as the Andromeda update, and understands the new imperative of creative diversification over hyper-specific audience targeting. Key Responsibilities I. Campaign Strategy & Optimization (The Science) Client Performance Ownership: Plan, launch, manage, and scale high-performing campaigns across multiple client accounts and the entire marketing funnel (TOFU, MOFU, BOFU) to meet aggressive ROAS/CPA targets. Advanced Targeting: Utilize a deep understanding of audience segmentation, including Custom Audiences, Lookalikes (LALs), and Advantage+ Audience parameters, to maximize signal density and conversion efficiency tailored to each client's unique target demographic. Platform Expertise (Post-Andromeda): Structure campaigns for success in Meta’s evolving AI-driven environment. This includes consolidating campaign structures, embracing broad targeting, and leveraging Advantage+ automation tools for budget and placement optimization. Tracking & Data Health: Ensure flawless implementation and maintenance of the Meta Pixel and Conversions API to ensure clean, high-quality data reporting and optimal ad delivery signals for every client property. Budget Management: Rigorously monitor campaign spend, perform daily optimizations, and manage bids and budget allocations (CBO/Advantage+ Budget) to maximize efficiency and scale across your assigned client portfolio. II. Creative Strategy & Storyboarding (The Art) Creative as the New Targeting: Proactively lead the creative strategy, recognizing that ad creative is the primary lever for performance in the current Meta landscape. Storyboarding & Visual Planning: Suggest, plan, and formalize storyboards and visual concepts for new ad creatives, focusing on mobile-first, vertical video (Reels/Stories) formats. A/B Testing Discipline: Implement a rigorous, continuous creative testing framework (e.g., 8-15 distinct creative concepts per campaign) to consistently refresh the ad library and combat ad fatigue. Collaboration: Serve as the critical bridge between the Media Buying team and the Content/Design teams, ensuring all visual and copy assets are briefed correctly, align with platform best practices, and address specific audience angles. III. Reporting & Platform Intelligence Client Analysis & Reporting: Analyze performance data daily, weekly, and monthly, translating complex metrics (e.g., CPM, CTR, ROAS, New Customer Ratio) into clear, actionable insights and strategic recommendations for client presentations and internal stakeholders. Innovation & Updates: Stay current with all major platform updates, policy changes, and algorithmic shifts (e.g., Andromeda, iOS updates). Implement necessary changes immediately to maintain account performance and compliance. Documentation: Maintain comprehensive documentation of all campaign setups, testing results, and optimization protocols. Required Skills & Qualifications 3+ years of dedicated, hands-on experience managing and scaling high-budget paid advertising campaigns on Meta platforms (Facebook and Instagram). Proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple client accounts and diverse campaign objectives simultaneously, ideally within an agency setting. Expert-level proficiency in Meta Ads Manager and Business Manager, including deep knowledge of setting up Conversion Tracking, Catalog Feeds, and Dynamic Ads. Demonstrable understanding of AI-driven ad delivery changes and how to adapt strategy to new automated systems (e.g., the importance of creative density and broad targeting in the current ad auction environment). Proven visual aptitude and creative thinking with experience outlining and briefing impactful ad concepts/storyboards for video and static formats. Exceptional analytical skills, highly proficient in Excel/Google Sheets, and the ability to interpret data beyond surface-level metrics. Strong communication skills, capable of presenting complex performance data and creative rationale to stakeholders. Meta Blueprint certification(s) strongly preferred.

description: IMPORTANT: Start your application with a red apple emoji. Applications without it are not read. WHAT THIS IS We run multiple dropshipping stores across different markets and languages. We need someone to list products and full collections on our Shopify stores, correctly and consistently. You will start with listing. Once you know our process and we know your work, this role grows into launching our Meta ad campaigns as well. That is a real next step, not a maybe. It is the second half of the same job and we would rather grow one person into it than hire twice. Everything runs on a written SOP plus a Loom video that shows the whole process from start to finish. You will not be guessing. WHAT YOU WILL DO Single products: - Get a source product URL from us - Request the import script in our Claude project and run it on your PC through Command Prompt (copy-paste, no coding needed) - Send us the full output, including any errors - Pull the size chart from the source, get it translated and converted to centimetres, then set it up in the Kiwi Sizing app and assign it to the product - Check the live product page against our checklist Full collections: - Same process, but for an entire collection at once - One size chart covers the whole collection, so you build it once and assign it to every product in that collection - Check that the product count matches the source and that nothing was skipped Quality control (this is the important part): - Titles and colour names properly translated, no leftover words from the source language - Correct photo showing for each colour variant - Shoe sizes in EU, not US - Prices and compare-at prices correct - No leftover text from the source store: shipping promises, guarantees, city names, brand stories - Size chart button appears on the product page with the right chart behind it When something is wrong, you send us the product link and describe what you see. You never edit a script yourself. WHAT YOU NEED - Real experience listing products on Shopify. You have done this yourself, on live stores. - Experience launching Meta ads. You will not use it on day one, but this is where the role goes. - Experience with dropshipping stores specifically. - You use Claude or ChatGPT as a working tool, not just occasionally. - A Windows PC. Our import scripts only run on Windows. - Very clear written English. All our communication is written. If we have to read a message twice to understand it, this will not work. - Fast, stable internet. - Flexible availability. You choose when you work your hours, but launches do not always fall inside office hours, so we need someone who can be reached and can pick up a task when it comes in. - Attention to detail, and the discipline to follow a written process exactly instead of doing it your own way. You will get access to our Shopify admin and an API token. We need someone we can trust with that. WHAT WE PROVIDE - Written SOPs and a Loom video walkthrough of the full process - All accounts and tools you need - Direct contact with us. Asking a question is always better than guessing. - A clear path into launching our ad campaigns once you have the listing process down HOW TO APPLY Read this carefully. Applications that miss a step are not reviewed. 1. Start your message with a red apple emoji. 2. List the stores you have worked on. Names or URLs. Tell us what you did on each one: listing, ads, or both. 3. Answer these two questions: - How many products or collections have you listed in a typical week? - Which ad accounts have you worked in, and what did you launch? We reply to everyone who does all three.

title: Motion Designer Figma
description: About the Role We're a boutique branding studio based in the Netherlands. We work at the intersection of brand identity, strategy, and design execution. Our brand and design work is built in Figma, and we're now bringing that work to life in motion for social and beyond. We're looking for a skilled motion designer to join us on a gig basis, with a clear path toward part-time and eventually full-time collaboration for the right person. Our graphic designer and creative lead design everything in Figma. Your job is to take those finished designs and turn them into motion: animated brand content, kinetic typography, logo reveals, and explainer graphics that feel as considered as the brands we build. This is not an entry-level role, and it is NOT for someone who just started animating and is looking to grow into the work. We need someone who has already done this at a high level, repeatedly, and can prove it with published work. What You'll Do - Receive briefs via online meeting, written documentation, and finished Figma design files, then independently own the animation from static design to final motion - Create animated brand content for social: kinetic typography, quote and statement reels, framework and process explainers, announcement and case-study pieces - Produce logo animations, brand reveals, intros, outros, and motion stings from our identity systems - Translate Figma designs faithfully into motion, respecting the original layout, type, and spacing - Build reusable, editable animated templates so our best formats can be repeated across campaigns and clients - Design transitions and motion polish, and add animated graphic layers where needed - Deliver organised, well-structured project files (clean comps, logical naming, reusable pre-comps) and export to the correct specs for social (9:16) and web What This Role Is Not This is not primarily a footage-editing or videography role. We're after animated design, moving type, graphics, and brand motion built from our Figma work, not cutting and grading filmed clips. If you also edit footage, that's a bonus, but it is not the core of this role. It's not for someone who only assembles presets or templates without understanding brand logic. We provide brand deliverables and expect motion that feels intentional, not generic default animation. And it's not for someone who needs constant hand-holding. You receive the brief, ask the right questions upfront, and deliver, with proactive communication if questions come up. What We're Looking For Required: - A strong showreel and portfolio of published motion design work that shows real craft in kinetic type, brand animation, and graphic motion. We will be looking at it critically - Expert-level After Effects. This is the core tool of the role - Excellent kinetic typography. You can animate type in a specific brand typeface so it feels designed, not defaulted - The ability to work from Figma design files and translate static layouts faithfully into motion - A strong sense of timing, easing, and pacing. Your animation should feel premium and considered, never stiff or templated - Clean working habits: organised comps, logical naming, reusable pre-comps, editable project files - Reliable communication in English, written and spoken - Able to work independently from a brief with minimal back-and-forth Nice to have: - A templated, systematic way of working. You structure and document your files so our best formats become repeatable, as we intend to systematise our content - Illustrator experience and comfort preparing or adapting vector assets - Lottie or web-export experience, and familiarity with motion for digital products - A sense for sound, syncing motion to audio - Editing ability (Premiere) for the occasional mixed piece - Prior agency or brand content experience How We Work Together Every project starts with a briefing call where we walk you through the use case, goals, and brand direction. After the call, we provide written documentation and the finished Figma design files. From there, you own the animation. We expect proactive communication if questions come up. No silence until delivery. Compensation This starts as a gig engagement, paid hourly, based on experience and portfolio. We pay well for the right person. Strong collaborators will have the opportunity to move into a structured part-time role, and eventually a full-time position as the relationship grows. How to Apply Send us: - Your showreel and portfolio, links to published, live motion work only. No unlisted mockups or static frames. We want to see what you've actually shipped - A short introduction: your background, the types of projects you've worked on, the tools you're expert in, and your hourly rate expectation Shortlisted applicants will be invited to a paid test project, one short motion piece animated from a real Figma brief, before we move forward. Applications without a showreel will not be reviewed.

title: Senior UI/UX Product Designer (Figma, SaaS + mobile app) — NOT a graphic design role
job_title: Senior UI/UX Product Designer (Figma, SaaS + mobile app) — NOT a graphic design role
description: READ THIS FIRST This is a PRODUCT DESIGN role: screens, flows, and interfaces for a live software platform and a mobile app, designed in Figma and handed to an engineer to build. It is NOT a graphic design role. If your portfolio is logos, branding boards, social media graphics, flyers, invitations, or Canva work, please do not apply — those applications will not be read, no matter how beautiful the work is. If your portfolio shows real software — dashboards, web apps, mobile apps, booking flows — read on. This role was written for you. SENIOR UI/UX PRODUCT DESIGNER — MAKE A LUXURY FAMILY-CARE PLATFORM THE MOST BEAUTIFUL, EFFORTLESS OF ITS KIND Project-based full-time (about 6-9 months), then part-time retainer · Work from home · Flexible hours with a few hours' overlap with US Eastern (New York) time ABOUT US House of Nannies is a boutique, high-end domestic staffing agency in the New York area, founded by a nanny, serving families across Westchester, Manhattan, Greenwich and Fairfield, Bergen County, and the Hamptons. We run two platforms: our placement service (long-term nanny and newborn-care matching) and Little Minders, our membership babysitting service. Behind both sits the Manor — our internal operations platform where our team runs every family's search. We have a strong brand and a defined design language: warm, editorial, premium. We're looking for the product designer who will carry it through every screen. THE ROLE You'll own the UI/UX of our product experience end to end: our internal platform, our family and candidate portals, and our mobile app. You'll redesign existing screens for calm and simplicity, design complete flows with every state (empty, loading, error, success, popups), and hand clean Figma specs to our lead engineer, working a step ahead of him surface by surface. This is a craft-and-ownership role for someone who sweats interface details. SHAPE OF THE ENGAGEMENT (WE'RE UPFRONT ABOUT THIS) Full-time for the initial build — roughly 6 to 9 months — then transitioning to an ongoing part-time retainer for polish and new work as we grow. We name this now because we'd rather be honest about the rhythm than surprise you later. IMPORTANT — ELEVATE, DON'T REINVENT We are not looking for someone to reinvent our brand. We have a brand bible, a design system, and live screens. Your job is to take what exists to its most beautiful, effortless, premium version. If your instinct is to throw it out and start over, we're not the right fit for each other. YOU MUST HAVE - A portfolio of SHIPPED SOFTWARE: web applications, SaaS platforms, or mobile apps that real people use. Landing pages alone do not qualify; print and social graphics do not qualify at all. - Strong flow and interaction design — you design journeys and states, not just pretty screens. - Proven ability to work inside an existing brand system and elevate it respectfully. - Figma fluency and clean developer handoff: components, specs, tokens. - Clear communication with a non-technical founder — you explain design decisions simply. NICE TO HAVE - Marketplaces, booking systems, or membership products. - A warm, editorial, premium aesthetic sensibility — our brand is soft and human, not techy or cold. - Motion and micro-interaction sensibility. HOW WE HIRE A short PAID trial task — redesign one real screen of our platform, working from our brand brief (we pay a flat fee whether or not we continue) — then a portfolio deep-dive and reference check. HOW TO APPLY Start your application with the word ELEVATE, then send exactly three things: 1. A direct link to ONE software screen you personally designed — a dashboard, web app, or mobile app screen you're proudest of. This is the first thing we look at. 2. Your full portfolio link. 3. Your expected monthly salary, and one line: your approach when you inherit an existing brand you love. Applications that don't start with ELEVATE, or whose strongest link is a logo or social media graphic, will not be read.

title: Marketing Operations Manager
description: LEAD THE CREATIVE OPERATION. THEN HELP BUILD WHAT COMES NEXT. Creative Production is the center of this role at the start. You will manage the editors, own the production system, raise the quality of the work, and make sure strong creative moves from brief to final asset without senior leadership having to manage every detail. This is not a coordinator role. It is not a virtual-assistant role. We need a Marketing Operations Manager who can operate the day-to-day work and improve the system at the same time. A NOTE FROM OUR CMO Before applying, watch this short video from our CMO about the role, its expectations, and what success looks like: ---------- /share/9cd974e7c8a848de8b84a4a992df4e45 Once Creative Production is stable and you have demonstrated the judgment, leadership, and capacity required, the role will expand into Social Media Operations. That second phase will include the team, publishing, community, creator, affiliate, and channel systems around the content. Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date. The exact timing will depend on demonstrated readiness and business needs. ABOUT VERITAS Veritas builds complete Starlink Mini deployment setups—mounts, power, cables, cases, and accessories—for consumers, work teams, and government fleets. We are a growing US company with a small, high-output marketing team in the Philippines. Several team members have grown with the company over the long term. We want the same for this role. THE DETAILS • Full-time independent contractor role with fixed monthly compensation of $2,000–$2,500 USD, based on experience, leadership depth, and overall fit—not an hourly position • Approximately 45–50 hours per week, with the regular work schedule fully aligned with Pacific Time • Philippine graveyard shift: roughly 11:00 PM–8:00 AM or 12:00 AM–9:00 AM, depending on U.S. daylight saving time • Fully remote and long-term • This must be your only job. No part-time employment, side hustles, ongoing freelance clients, or subcontracting • Occasional weekend availability when production, launches, or publishing require management coverage • Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna required; no regular onsite office days, but occasional in-person meetings may be scheduled WHAT YOU'LL OWN At full production, the team aims to produce one long-form video and up to 14 supporting creative assets each week. These may include shorts/reels, static graphics, or carousels and are adapted for distribution across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X. PHASE 1: LEAD CREATIVE PRODUCTION • Manage a two-person video-editing team, including their priorities, workload, deadlines, coverage, development, and performance. • Turn approved priorities into clear production plans, briefs, scripts, storytelling direction, B-roll needs, and deliverables. • Own the production pipeline: capacity, assignments, dependencies, revisions, blockers, asset readiness, and delivery visibility. • Review short-form, long-form, ads, thumbnails, static assets, carousels, platform versions, and other creative output. • Evaluate the full story—not only whether one shot matches one line. Check hooks, pacing, B-roll, demonstrations, captions, CTAs, factual accuracy, brand alignment, and viewer flow. • Give editors clear, prioritized, actionable feedback and verify that required revisions were completed correctly. • Use performance findings to identify stronger hooks, packaging, formats, V2/V3 opportunities, and creative tests. • Build and improve SOPs, review standards, production trackers, asset repositories, AI-assisted QA, and backup coverage. • Coordinate minor corrections and urgent production support when needed, without turning the role into a primary editing position. PHASE 2: ADD SOCIAL MEDIA OPERATIONS Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date, once Phase 1 is operating reliably and you have demonstrated readiness for the expanded scope. At that point, you will also: • Manage the current Social Media Moderator and future social media team members. • Own the publishing calendar, content inventory, platform schedules, launch pushes, and publishing verification across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X. • Ensure each platform receives the correct version, copy, CTA, description, tags, products, related content, links, and native-platform setup. • Oversee community, marketing inboxes, important comments and messages, channel presentation, and routine reputation handling. • Manage routine creator-partnership and affiliate operations, including communication, records, deliverables, logistics, and escalation. • Own routine UTM, Bitly, campaign-link, profile-link, and destination-verification workflows. • Review social performance and turn findings into decisions, tests, and coordinated creative recommendations. • Build and maintain the social department’s processes, AI workflows, reporting, and continuity systems. HOW THE ROLE FITS You will report to and work closely with senior marketing leadership. In Phase 1, the video editors report to you. In Phase 2, the Social Media Moderator also reports to you. You will have authority over routine departmental planning, assignments, quality, coaching, corrections, and process improvements within approved standards. Cross-functional, sensitive, contractual, financial, policy, staffing, reputation, and other material decisions remain with senior leadership. HOW WE USE AI Our marketing operation uses AI for context, research, briefs, feedback, quality control, documentation, analysis, automation, and institutional memory. We want someone who uses AI heavily to improve judgment and execution—not someone who accepts raw output. Sources must be checked. Brand and product accuracy must be protected. What the team learns should improve the next workflow. YOU'RE A STRONG FIT IF YOU • Have at least eight years of professional work experience. • Have at least three years managing teams and direct reports. • Have at least two years of experience inside a creative or marketing function. • Have meaningful corporate, in-house, agency, or field-based operating experience—not only freelance, VA, or task-based remote experience. • Have managed a creative-production pipeline and can explain the team size, volume, process, problems, decisions, and results. • Are exceptionally strong at storytelling and can diagnose why an edit is technically correct but still wrong for the overall story. • Hands-on video-editing experience is an advantage, but it is not required. You must be able to direct editors, evaluate their work, and clearly explain what needs to change and why. • Can coach editors, address recurring mistakes, manage underperformance, and maintain accountability without becoming the bottleneck. • Take action without waiting for step-by-step direction and consistently look for ways to improve quality, speed, visibility, and continuity. • Use performance evidence to improve creative work—not only report numbers. • Use AI daily with structured context, validation, human review, reusable systems, and feedback loops. • Communicate clearly in conversational American English. • Can sustain a Philippine graveyard schedule and occasional weekend coverage. • Reside in Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna and be willing to attend occasional in-person meetings. • Have reliable primary internet, a backup connection, and backup power. • Want one company to grow with for the long term. THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR • Someone who waits for detailed instructions before acting. • Someone whose experience is limited to task-based VA work, short freelance engagements, or managing multiple clients. • A strong individual contributor who does not want to manage, coach, and hold people accountable. • Someone who reviews only technical editing details but cannot evaluate the complete story and business goal. • Someone who creates more process without improving output, visibility, quality, or results. • Someone planning to keep another job, freelance clients, or subcontract any part of the work. • Someone testing a graveyard schedule for the first time without a credible plan to sustain it. HOW WE WORK Clear priorities. Direct feedback. Strong ownership. Problems are raised early. Decisions are documented. The goal is not to look busy. The goal is to build work that performs and an operation that improves. Our brand voice follows the same standard: short words, short sentences, confident but never salesy. Like a friend who knows the gear. HOW TO APPLY Use this subject line and at least 20 AP: [INSERT REQUIRED WORD] - [X] years of professional experience - [X] years managing teams Include the following: • Your resume with company names, employment dates, role titles, team sizes, and whether each role was corporate, in-house, agency, freelance, or VA work. • Have you directly managed a creative-production or video-production team? Answer Yes or No. If yes, state the team size. • Can you provide examples of videos, campaigns, or creative projects you directly led if you advance to the next stage? Answer Yes or No. Do not send links or detailed explanations at this stage. • In one short logistics block, confirm that this would be your only job and that you would complete all work personally. Include your city or province, most recent U.S.-hours role and actual schedule, primary and backup internet, backup power, and occasional weekend availability. Note: Applications missing any requirement will not be considered.

title: Experienced Dispute & Chargeback Manager for Fast Growing Health & Beauty Ecommerce Stores
job_title: Experienced Dispute & Chargeback Manager for Fast Growing Health & Beauty Ecommerce Stores
description: We operate international health and beauty dropshipping stores and are looking for an exceptionally intelligent and experienced Dispute, Chargeback Manager & Revenue Recovery Specialist. This is not a beginner position, a general customer support position, or a role for someone who has only occasionally responded to disputes. Your main responsibility will be to protect company revenue by managing active disputes from beginning to end. You will communicate with customers, negotiate dispute closures, assess financial risk, collect evidence, prepare processor submissions, meet deadlines and d ---------- which strategy creates the lowest possible loss for the company. We are looking for someone who already knows how to do this at a high level. There will be no basic dispute-management training and no step-by-step hand-holding. We will explain our internal systems, stores and policies, but you must already understand how disputes work in the health and beauty dropshipping industry. If you do not have a strong and verifiable track record managing Klarna, PayPal and credit card disputes, do not apply. Your main objective: Your performance will be judged by: * Disputes closed directly with customers. * Chargebacks prevented. * Revenue recovered. * Disputes won through strong evidence. * Refunds avoided where possible. * Losses minimized in weak cases. * Evidence submitted correctly and before deadlines. * Follow-ups completed without reminders. * Cases documented and organized properly. * Your ability to work independently. Customer satisfaction is not the primary KPI. Communication must remain professional, but the purpose of the communication is to resolve the dispute, protect revenue and reduce financial damage. What you will do: Manage active disputes You will take ownership of disputes opened through: -Shopify Payments: * Klarna. * Credit Card -PayPal. You will be responsible for: * Investigating each case. * Reviewing the order timeline. * Understanding what the customer is claiming. * Identifying contradictions or weaknesses in the claim. * Determining what evidence is available. * Determining what evidence is still missing. * Contacting suppliers, carriers, warehouses or pickup points when needed. * Communicating directly with the customer. * Persuading customers to close unnecessary disputes. * Negotiating resolutions that minimize losses. * Following up persistently until a final outcome is reached. * Preparing evidence if the customer refuses to cooperate. * Submitting evidence before every deadline. * Recording the result of each case. You must understand that every case requires a different strategy. A copied template, generic apology or automatic refund offer is not dispute management. Negotiate with customers: A major part of this role is getting customers to close disputes voluntarily before they escalate. You must know how to: * Read the customer’s real motivation. * Identify what outcome they actually want. * Challenge inaccurate claims without losing control of the conversation. * Explain policies, delivery information and refund processes clearly. * Use logic, urgency, firmness and reassurance strategically. * Avoid unnecessary admissions that weaken the company’s position. * Avoid offering refunds as much as possible. * Offer calculated alternatives where appropriate. * Keep the customer focused on the resolution you are proposing. * Know when further communication is unlikely to improve the outcome. We use a commercially aggressive approach to dispute recovery. You should be comfortable using persistent follow-up, strong negotiation, precise wording and every procedural advantage available. We need someone aggressive enough to recover revenue, but intelligent enough not to damage the business while doing it. Handle Klarna, PayPal and credit card disputes: You must have direct, hands-on experience managing disputes from beginning to end across Klarna, PayPal and credit card payment processors. This includes investigating the order, communicating with the customer, determining the correct strategy, collecting evidence, submitting the response, meeting every deadline and following the case until a final outcome is reached. You must have experience handling cases involving: * Product not received. * Delivered but not received. * Packages delivered to pickup points. * Uncollected packages. * Returned shipments. * Refund not received. * Incorrect products. * Product-quality complaints. * Cancellation requests. * Opened or used health and beauty products. * Customers refusing to follow return instructions. * Customers keeping disputes open after a solution was offered. * Unauthorized-transaction claims. * Customers claiming the product was significantly different from what was advertised. Across all payment methods, you should understand: * How disputes escalate. * How and when customers can close a dispute. * Evidence and response deadlines. * Tracking and proof-of-delivery requirements. * Order and fulfilment timelines. * Proof of authorization. * Refund and cancellation records. * Customer communication evidence. * Policy acceptance. * When additional evidence should be requested from suppliers, warehouses, carriers or pickup points. * How to identify weaknesses in both the customer’s claim and the company’s position. * When to defend, negotiate, partially refund, fully refund, reship, settle or accept the loss. * The difference between relevant evidence and irrelevant document dumping. * How to organize evidence so the reviewer can understand the case quickly. * How to turn a complicated order history into a clear, convincing and easy-to-review evidence submission. You must know what strengthens a case, what weakens it and when a dispute is commercially worth defending. Klarna disputes You must understand the Klarna dispute process, including: * The different escalation stages. * How customers pause invoices or payments. * How customers can close or update a dispute. * What happens when a dispute is escalated for formal review. * Which evidence Klarna expects for different dispute types. * How to communicate with customers while a Klarna dispute is active. * How to handle customers who refuse to close a dispute after receiving a reasonable solution. * When continued negotiation is more effective than immediately submitting evidence. PayPal disputes and claims You must understand: * PayPal disputes. * PayPal claims. * PayPal chargebacks. * Card-funded PayPal transactions. * Item-not-received claims. * Significantly-not-as-described claims. * Unauthorized-transaction claims. * Appeals and escalations. * PayPal tracking and delivery requirements. * The difference between resolving a case directly with the buyer and defending it through PayPal. * When a PayPal dispute may also become an external credit card chargeback. Credit card chargebacks You must have experience responding to credit card disputes through payment processors, payment gateways, acquiring banks or chargeback-management platforms. You should understand: * Chargeback reason categories and reason codes. * Processor-specific evidence requirements. * Proof of authorization. * Representment. * Pre-arbitration or second-stage disputes where applicable. * How card issuer disputes differ from Klarna and PayPal cases. * How to respond when the payment processor only allows limited evidence or text. * How to select the strongest evidence instead of submitting every available document. * How to prepare a concise case summary that directly addresses the dispute reason. You must be able to turn a complicated case into a clear, convincing and easy-to-review evidence submission. Prepare strong evidence packages: You will collect, organize and submit evidence such as: * Shopify order confirmations. * Order and fulfilment timelines. * Tracking information. * Proof of delivery. * Last-mile carrier tracking. * Pickup-point confirmations. * Customer emails. * Return instructions. * Refund records. * Previous resolution offers. * Store policies. * Screenshots. * Internal notes. * Chronological evidence summaries. *... Every submission must be accurate, relevant, organized and easy for the reviewer to understand. You must know what strengthens a case, what weakens a case and what should not be included. Minimize losses in weak cases: Not every dispute can be won. You must be intelligent enough to recognize when defending a case is no longer the most profitable option. When a case is weak, you should assess: * Order value. * Product cost. * Shipping cost. * Chargeback fees. * Payment processor fees. * Probability of winning. * Probability of escalation. * Whether the product can be recovered. * Whether a partial refund may close the case. * Whether a replacement is cheaper than a refund. * Whether the customer is likely to cooperate. * Whether continuing creates unnecessary processor risk. You must be able to recommend the lowest-cost resolution and explain your reasoning clearly. Intelligence and judgment: This is a mentally demanding role. We need someone who can process incomplete information, recognize patterns, identify contradictions, predict customer behavior and make good decisions without being told exactly what to do. For every case, you should naturally ask: * What is the customer claiming? * What probably happened? * What can we prove? * What can we not prove? * Which parts of the customer’s story are inconsistent? * What evidence is missing? * What will the payment processor care about? * What should be communicated to the customer? * What should be included in the evidence? * What should be excluded? * What is the probability of winning? * What is the cheapest acceptable outcome? * What is the next action? * What deadline cannot be missed? We are specifically looking for someone who is: * Exceptionally intelligent. * Strategically minded. * Commercially focused. * Highly persuasive. * Psychologically perceptive. * Extremely organized. * Creative. * Resourceful. * Calm under pressure. * Detail-oriented. * Punctual. * Proactive. * Reliable. * Comfortable making decisions. * Able to explain and defend their reasoning. * Able to receive feedback without ego. * Capable of working without constant supervision. You must know when to be firm, when to negotiate, when to request more evidence, when to challenge the customer and when to accept a controlled loss. Organization and punctuality: Dispute management is deadline-driven. A strong case submitted after the deadline is worthless. You must maintain a reliable system for: * Active disputes. * Platform deadlines. * Customer follow-ups. * Missing evidence. * Supplier requests. * Carrier investigations. * Return status. * Refund decisions. * Escalation stages. * Final outcomes. * Recovered revenue. * Total losses. You must never rely on memory alone. Every active case must have: * Clear notes. * A current status. * A next action. * A follow-up date. * A final deadline. Being disorganized, late, forgetful, passive or dependent on repeated reminders will result in failure in this role. Required experience: You must have a strong and verifiable track record in: * Klarna dispute management. * PayPal disputes and claims. * Credit card chargebacks. * Shopify order investigations. * Chargeback evidence preparation. * Health and beauty e-commerce. * Dropshipping fulfilment. * International shipping disputes. * Product-not-received claims. * Delivered-but-not-received claims. * Return and refund disputes. * Product complaints. * Opened-product and hygiene-related complaints. * Negotiating dispute closures directly with customers. * Reducing refund and chargeback losses. General customer support experience is not enough. Fashion customer service experience is not enough. Occasionally responding to disputes as part of a support role is not enough. Using a white-label chargeback service without personally choosing the strategy, investigating the case and building the evidence is not enough. We want someone who has personally: * Investigated disputes. * Contacted customers. * Negotiated closures. * Chosen refund and settlement strategies. * Collected missing evidence. * Written evidence summaries. * Submitted processor responses. * Tracked deadlines. * Taken responsibility for the result. Health and beauty dropshipping experience is mandatory You must understand the specific risks connected to health and beauty dropshipping, including: * Customers expecting guaranteed or immediate results. * Product-did-not-work complaints. * Complaints about packaging or product appearance. * Ingredient and instruction questions. * Opened or used products. * Hygiene-related return restrictions. * Product expectation mismatches. * Longer shipping times. * Supplier-side delays. * Overseas fulfilment. * Tracking gaps. * Last-mile carrier handovers. * Returned or uncollected parcels. * Customers opening disputes before contacting support. * Increased payment-processor scrutiny around health-related products and claims. You must understand how these disputes differ from ordinary fashion-store complaints. Independence and working style: We are looking for an expert who can take ownership of daily dispute management. There will be no basic training. At the beginning, we will review your work closely to determine whether your claimed experience is genuine. You will be evaluated through your decisions, organization, communication, evidence quality and results. We expect you to understand the work from day one. If you want you may fill in additional hours by handling daily customer support tasks when dispute volume is lower. However, this is not the main role we are hiring you for. We are hiring a dispute expert first. Customer support experience will never compensate for weak dispute-management ability. AI and templates: You may use AI tools for: * Improving wording. * Translation. * Grammar checks. * Organizing information. * Summarizing timelines. You may not use AI as a replacement for judgment. You must personally understand every case, verify every fact, adapt every message and choose every strategy. If you copy generic responses, upload the same evidence for every case or cannot explain your decisions, you will not succeed in this role. Compensation: Starting with $5 USD per hour. Performance bonuses may be offered based on: * Disputes closed. * Chargebacks prevented. * Cases won. * Revenue recovered. * Refund losses reduced. * Deadline accuracy. * Evidence quality. * Independence and reliability. Exceptional performers may receive higher compensation over time and eventually take full ownership of the dispute-management department. Do not apply unless you are genuinely experienced: No strong dispute-management track record means no interview. No direct experience with Shopify and Shopify Payments (klarna, cc), Paypal and health and beauty dropshipping means no hire. We will not hire based on confidence, impressive language or generic customer support experience. We will test whether you can actually perform the work. Candidates who exaggerate their experience will be identified quickly. How to apply: Provide three real dispute examples that you personally managed. At least one example must involve PayPal. At least one example must involve a Klarna Dispute/Chargeback. At least one example must involve a health, beauty, wellness, cosmetics or personal-care product. For each example, explain: 1. What the customer claimed. 2. Which payment platform was involved. 3. The order value. 4. What evidence was initially available. 5. What evidence was missing. 6. How you obtained the missing evidence. 7. What weaknesses existed in the case. 8. How you communicated with the customer. 9. How you attempted to get the dispute closed. 10. What evidence you submitted. 11. Whether you defended, negotiated, partially refunded, fully refunded, reshipped or accepted the loss. 12. The final outcome. 13. How much revenue was recovered or lost. 14. What you learned from the case. Also answer the following questions: * How many disputes or chargebacks did you manage per month? * Which dispute platforms have you personally used? * What was your approximate dispute win or closure rate? * How much experience do you have in health and beauty dropshipping? * Which credit card dispute categories or reason codes have you handled? * How do you track deadlines and follow-ups? * How do you d ---------- whether to defend or settle a case? * What would you do if tracking shows delivery but the customer denies receiving the parcel? * What would you do if a customer refuses to close a dispute after receiving a reasonable solution? * What is your current availability? Hiring process: Shortlisted candidates will complete a practical dispute-management assessment. You may be asked to: * Review a Shopify order timeline. * Identify weaknesses in the case. * Determine what evidence is missing. * Write a message intended to get the customer to close the dispute. * Prepare an evidence summary. * Select which documents should be submitted. * Identify which documents should not be submitted. * Recommend whether to defend, negotiate, partially refund, fully refund, reship or accept the loss. * Explain your reasoning. * Create a deadline and follow-up plan. We are not interested in theory. We are looking for someone who can think, investigate, negotiate, organize and recover revenue in real situations.
