title: LEAD REACTIVATION & APPOINTMENT SETTER
description: LEAD REACTIVATION & APPOINTMENT SETTER REMOTE | HIGH-TICKET SALES | PERFORMANCE-BASED THE ROLE We are looking for an experienced LEAD REACTIVATION & APPOINTMENT SETTING SPECIALIST to join our sales team. This is NOT a general Virtual Assistant position. We already have a database of prospects who have previously shown interest in our offer. Many of these prospects did not purchase for different reasons: they did not show, cancelled, postponed, had financial or timing concerns, needed more time, or simply stopped responding. Your job is to go back into that pipeline and find the people who are STILL SERIOUS. You will reconnect with prospects, have genuine sales conversations, understand what prevented them from moving forward, determine whether their situation has changed, qualify their current interest, and book qualified sales appointments directly onto Kad's calendar. KAD IS THE CLOSER. Your job is to create the opportunities for her to close. This is a performance-driven sales position for someone who is comfortable making a high volume of calls, handling rejection, overcoming objections, following up consistently, and turning dormant prospects into genuine sales opportunities. AVAILABILITY You must be available during U.S./Canadian Eastern Time (ET). Working hours may be split across morning, afternoon and evening calling windows to maximize contact rates with prospects. Your exact working schedule and required coverage windows will be agreed upon before starting. YOUR MISSION Your mission is simple: KEEP KAD'S CALENDAR FILLED WITH QUALIFIED PROSPECTS WHO HAVE A GENUINE REASON TO SPEAK WITH HER AND ARE COMMITTED TO SHOWING UP. The core workflow is: REACTIVATE → CONVERSE → QUALIFY → BOOK → CRM HANDOFF → PRE-CALL VA → KAD You own the prospect through the BOOKING AND CRM HANDOFF stage. The existing Pre-Call VA takes over after booking and manages appointment confirmation, application completion, preparation and show-up processes. Kad handles the closing conversation. THE LEAD DATABASE You will systematically work through our historical lead database, beginning with leads from: SEPTEMBER 2025 → PRESENT These include prospects who: • Previously expressed interest but did not purchase • Booked an appointment but did not show • Cancelled an appointment • Rescheduled but never returned • Asked to be contacted later • Said they were interested but needed more time • Had financial or timing objections • Stopped responding • Went cold after speaking with the team • Were previously qualified but never moved forward These are NOT traditional cold leads. They have already demonstrated some level of interest. Your responsibility is to discover WHO IS STILL SERIOUS, WHAT HAS CHANGED, and WHETHER THERE IS A LEGITIMATE OPPORTUNITY TO MOVE FORWARD NOW. WHAT YOU WILL DO 1. REACTIVATE OLD LEADS You will systematically work through your assigned pipeline using: • Outbound phone calls • SMS/text • Email • Structured follow-up • CRM tasks • Multiple contact attempts at appropriate times DAILY OUTBOUND EXPECTATION: 80–120+ DIALS PER WORKING DAY, depending on connect rates, active conversations and pipeline volume. This is a SALES ROLE. You will spend a significant part of your working day ON THE PHONE. If making 80–120+ calls feels excessive to you, this is probably not the right position. 2. HAVE REAL SALES CONVERSATIONS We are not looking for someone who simply reads a script. You need to be able to have a natural, intelligent conversation with someone who previously showed interest. You should be comfortable discovering: • Why they originally became interested • What they were hoping to accomplish • What prevented them from moving forward • Whether that obstacle still exists • What has changed since they last spoke with us • What they want now • Why they are considering taking action • What is stopping them from taking action • Whether now is genuinely the right time You should be able to listen carefully, ask intelligent follow-up questions, identify the real objection and move the conversation forward. 3. HANDLE OBJECTIONS You will regularly hear: • "I'm not interested anymore." • "I can't afford it." • "It's not the right time." • "Maybe next year." • "I need to think about it." • "I need to speak with my partner." • "I've already spoken with someone." • "Why are you calling me now?" • "I'm still interested, but things have changed." You must be able to distinguish between: A GENUINE NO AND AN OBJECTION THAT CAN BE EXPLORED. You should never pressure someone who genuinely does not want the offer. But you should also never accept "not now" as the end of the conversation without understanding WHY. 4. QUALIFY BEFORE BOOKING Not everyone who responds should be placed on Kad's calendar. Your responsibility is to determine whether the prospect is genuinely worth Kad's time. Before booking, establish: INTEREST Are they genuinely interested? NEED Do they still have the problem, objective or desire that originally brought them to us? MOTIVATION Why are they considering taking action? TIMING Why are they considering it now? FIT Do they meet the basic qualification criteria for the offer? COMMITMENT Are they genuinely prepared to attend a scheduled appointment? FINANCIAL READINESS If finances were previously the primary reason the prospect did not move forward, has something materially changed? The setter should NOT promise financing, pricing exceptions or payment arrangements. The objective is simply to determine whether the prospect's current circumstances justify another sales conversation. The goal is NOT to maximize the number of appointments. The goal is to maximize the number of QUALIFIED SALES OPPORTUNITIES. 5. BOOK THE APPOINTMENT Once you have established that the prospect is qualified, you will confidently ask for the appointment. You will: • Book directly into Kad's calendar • Select an appropriate appointment time • Confirm the prospect's contact information • Explain what they should expect from the call • Establish commitment to attend • Record the appointment correctly • Complete the required CRM information • Hand the opportunity to the Pre-Call VA A booking is not the end of the job. A QUALITY BOOKING IS. 6. RESPOND FAST TO HOT LEADS Database reactivation is not only about working through a call list. Sometimes a dormant prospect will suddenly respond: "Yes, I'm still interested." When that happens, that lead becomes a PRIORITY. During working hours, actively responding or engaged prospects should be contacted AS QUICKLY AS REASONABLY POSSIBLE. Do not leave a hot reactivation sitting unanswered for hours while continuing routine database dialing. Your priority should be: HOT / RESPONDING LEAD → ACTIVE CONVERSATION → QUALIFICATION → BOOKING Then return to the normal outbound pipeline. 7. FOLLOW UP CONSISTENTLY A prospect saying "not right now" does not necessarily mean "never." You will maintain structured follow-up with prospects who are: • Interested but not ready • Waiting for a specific date • Waiting for finances • Waiting for a partner or decision-maker • Considering their options • Requesting additional information • Temporarily unavailable • Not currently responding Every lead should eventually reach a clear outcome: BOOKED / NOT INTERESTED / NOT QUALIFIED / NOT NOW / LOST No valuable lead should disappear simply because one call was unanswered. DO-NOT-CONTACT & COMMUNICATION COMPLIANCE If a prospect explicitly requests not to be contacted, opts out, unsubscribes, or otherwise indicates that further communication is unwanted, immediately update the CRM and stop outreach through the applicable channel. All outreach must follow company communication policies and applicable calling, texting and email requirements. AUTHORIZATION & REPRESENTING THE COMPANY The setter may NOT make promises, guarantees, pricing changes, financing representations, refunds, discounts, or other commitments on behalf of the company unless specifically authorized. The setter is responsible for qualifying and booking the prospect, not for making unauthorized commercial commitments. 8. CRM OWNERSHIP & ATTRIBUTION Accurate CRM management is part of the job. Every assigned lead must be properly documented. You are expected to: • Record every meaningful interaction • Document objections • Record qualification information • Complete follow-up tasks • Maintain accurate lead status • Record appointments correctly • Provide useful handoff notes LEAD ATTRIBUTION Lead ownership must be documented in the CRM before outreach. Performance credit will only be given according to the company's lead attribution rules. The setter receives credit for leads that are: • Properly assigned to them, OR • Personally reactivated by them in accordance with company attribution rules The following do not qualify for duplicate performance credit: • Existing active opportunities • Appointments already booked by another team member • Leads already actively owned by another salesperson • Duplicate records • Opportunities that cannot reasonably be attributed to the setter THE CRM IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. 9. CRM HANDOFF Once a qualified appointment is booked, your responsibility is to ensure the Pre-Call VA and Kad have the necessary context. The CRM handoff should include: • Previous interaction • Why the prospect originally showed interest • Current situation • Primary motivation • Previous objections • What prevented the original purchase • What has changed • Current level of interest • Qualification information • Questions or concerns raised • Why they agreed to speak with Kad Kad should not have to start the conversation asking: "So, tell me, why did you book?" She should already have the context. IMPORTANT You do NOT own the full post-booking show-up process. The handoff is: YOU → QUALIFIED BOOKING → CRM HANDOFF → PRE-CALL VA → KAD The Pre-Call VA owns: • Appointment confirmation • Application completion • Pre-call material • Preparation • Show-up management You remain responsible for the QUALITY OF THE OPPORTUNITY YOU CREATED. PERFORMANCE SCORECARD This is a PERFORMANCE-DRIVEN SALES POSITION. You will be measured on RESULTS AND SALES ACTIVITY, not simply hours online. INITIAL 30-DAY PERFORMANCE TARGETS: • Outbound dials: 80–120+ per working day • Assigned leads attempted: 100% • CRM documentation: 100% • Follow-up tasks completed: 95%+ • Appointment show rate: TRACKED / 80% TARGET • Qualified shows: PRIMARY KPI • Closed revenue: TRACKED The appointment show rate is a tracked quality metric, not solely a setter-controlled performance requirement, because the Pre-Call VA owns the post-booking confirmation and show-up process. The initial 30-day period will also establish a baseline for the actual reactivation and conversion performance of the database. We will NOT artificially impose a booking quota before understanding the database's real conversion characteristics. QUALITY COMES FIRST. COMPENSATION 30-DAY PERFORMANCE TRIAL $300 USD BASE + PERFORMANCE BONUSES Compensation and continued engagement will be REVIEWED FOLLOWING SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE INITIAL 30-DAY TRIAL. QUALIFIED SHOW BONUS $15 PER QUALIFIED APPOINTMENT THAT ATTENDS A $15 show bonus is earned only when: 1. You personally reactivated the lead. 2. The lead was qualified according to company standards. 3. You personally booked the appointment. 4. The appointment was properly recorded in the CRM. 5. Required qualification and handoff notes were completed. 6. The prospect attended the scheduled sales call with Kad. 7. The opportunity complies with the company's lead-attribution rules. A BOOKING ALONE DOES NOT EARN A BONUS. The purpose of this structure is to reward QUALITY OPPORTUNITIES, not calendar volume. CLOSED SALE BONUS $50 PER CLOSED AND COLLECTED SALE The $50 bonus applies to a sale that: • Originated from a lead personally reactivated by you • Was properly attributed to you in the CRM • Was qualified by you • Resulted in a completed sale with Kad • Has successfully collected the initial payment The $50 closed-sale bonus is earned once the customer's INITIAL PAYMENT HAS SUCCESSFULLY CLEARED. If the payment fails, is reversed, charged back or refunded BEFORE THE BONUS IS PAID, the sale does not qualify for the bonus. Duplicate, pre-existing or improperly attributed opportunities do not qualify. Additional performance bonuses may be introduced based on sustained performance. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR We want a: SALESPERSON WHO HAPPENS TO WORK REMOTELY — NOT AN ADMINISTRATIVE VA WHO IS WILLING TO MAKE SOME CALLS. You should be: • Highly confident on the phone • Persistent without being aggressive • Comfortable with rejection • Naturally conversational • Curious and inquisitive • An excellent listener • Commercially minded • Highly organized • Self-motivated • Competitive • Coachable • Comfortable with measurable targets • Comfortable making 80–120+ outbound calls per day • Able to work independently • Excellent in spoken and written English You must be comfortable calling someone who has not spoken with us in months. You must be comfortable hearing: "NO." And calmly making the next call. REQUIRED EXPERIENCE Previous experience in one or more of the following is required: • Appointment setting • Inside sales • Telesales • Lead generation • Lead reactivation • SDR / BDR • Outbound sales • Consultative sales • Sales development • Customer reactivation • High-ticket sales Strong preference will be given to candidates with experience working with: • Warm leads • Aged leads • Dormant databases • Previously engaged prospects • High-ticket products or services • Sales closers Experience working directly with a closer is a major advantage. WHAT WILL MAKE YOU STAND OUT We want evidence that you can ACTUALLY SELL. Strong candidates will be able to demonstrate: • High outbound call volume • Consistent appointment production • Strong appointment show rates • Experience reactivating old databases • High-ticket sales experience • Strong objection handling • CRM proficiency • Experience working with closers • Consistent target achievement • Measurable sales results If your previous role had numbers attached to it, TELL US THE NUMBERS. For example: • Daily dials • Monthly conversations • Monthly appointments • Show rate • Conversion rate • Revenue generated • Sales target • Target achievement We are far more interested in WHAT YOU ACTUALLY PRODUCED than a list of generic responsibilities. THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF... Do not apply if: • You only want administrative VA work • You dislike making phone calls • You are uncomfortable with outbound sales • You need a script for every conversation • You give up after one unanswered message • You are uncomfortable handling objections • You dislike performance targets • You measure success only by appointments booked • You require constant supervision • You are uncomfortable asking directly for the appointment • You don't enjoy talking to people • You are looking for a low-activity, low-pressure role We are looking for someone who WANTS TO SELL. APPLICATION & SELECTION PROCESS Our application process is designed to identify people who can ACTUALLY SELL, not simply interview well. Through the application portal, you will be asked to provide: • Your CV • Sales experience • Previous appointment-setting or outbound sales experience • Typical daily outbound call volume • Appointments generated • Appointment show rate • Conversion rate, where available • Sales targets and target achievement • Revenue generated, where available • Experience working with warm, aged or dormant leads • Experience handling objections • A short written or recorded introduction • Responses to practical sales scenarios based on real prospect situations SALES EXPERIENCE QUESTION Tell us about an old or "dead" lead you personally brought back to life. Explain: • What had stopped them from moving forward • How you reopened the conversation • What you said or did • How you handled the objection • What the outcome was Please provide actual numbers wherever possible. We are more interested in MEASURABLE RESULTS than generic job descriptions. After applications are submitted, candidates will be reviewed progressively. Strong applicants may be contacted for additional questions, a short sales assessment or a live role-play before a final hiring decision is made. The process is intentionally selective. We are looking for evidence that you can: HAVE THE CONVERSATION → HANDLE THE OBJECTION → QUALIFY THE PROSPECT → ASK FOR THE APPOINTMENT. THE PERSON WE WANT We are looking for someone who can look at a database full of old prospects and think: "THERE IS MONEY IN HERE. LET'S FIND THE PEOPLE WHO ARE STILL SERIOUS." You should enjoy the chase. You should enjoy conversations. You should enjoy figuring out what stopped someone from buying. You should enjoy turning: "NOT NOW." into: "LET'S TALK." You should take pride in putting a genuinely qualified prospect in front of a closer. Because when you do your job properly, Kad doesn't spend her time hunting for opportunities. SHE SPENDS HER TIME CLOSING THEM. If you are an exceptional appointment setter, SDR, telesales professional, sales development specialist or lead reactivation specialist who wants to work with a real pipeline and be measured on meaningful results: WE WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU.

I'm looking for one editor to take ownership of the editing work alongside me, long term. Success in this role comes down to two things above all else: editing quality and English comprehension. Because of that, this posting is specific about what the work requires, and the application asks for more than a résumé. I'd rather be clear upfront than have either of us discover a mismatch a month in. THE WORK Daily short-form vertical content — mostly talking heads with occasional voiceover/b-roll: Cutting dead space so videos stay paced and never drag Stitching the strongest takes into one seamless piece Adding image overlays on screen to support what's being said Zooms, crops, and reframes to keep the frame dynamic B-roll builds: I provide a voiceover and footage, you find the visual that matches each line Sourcing your own overlay assets — reading the script and independently finding the images it calls for The last two items are the core of the role. The rest is technical work most editors can learn. Choosing the right visual for the right sentence is what separates a video that reaches 4,000 people from one that reaches 4,000,000. I'll give you background and direction, but I want you fully self-sufficient at finding the visuals a script needs. You should be able to take the script and go find what it needs. This requires genuinely understanding English — hearing a sentence and catching the humor, the tone, the reference — because you can't source the right image for a line you don't fully understand. Your English does not need to be perfect. It needs to be strong enough that you follow everything being said and that we can communicate quickly and clearly. Familiarity with internet and pop culture is a significant advantage here, and it's rewarded. EXAMPLES OF THE WORK Please watch all three before applying so you know exactly what you'd be producing. This is the most important quality in the role. Self-sufficiency with assets. You can take a script and go find the images it needs without being handed a folder. This is weighted as heavily as your editing. Willingness to go the extra step. Reviewing your own export once more and fixing what wasn't flagged. Strong English comprehension. Understanding is essential; polished speaking and writing is a bonus. Responsive communication. When I message during working hours, I need a reply promptly rather than the following day. This role likely isn't the right fit if you're applying broadly today, prefer briefs explained in detail more than once, or intend to use AI to write your application answers — I'm looking for your own thinking. You'd be working directly with me each day on videos that have proven to get millions of views. title: Email Support Expert — Shopify DTC brand
job_title: Email Support Expert — Shopify DTC brand
description: We're looking for a customer service specialist who understands one thing clearly: A good reply doesn't just sound polite. It answers the real question, solves the problem before it grows, and turns a frustrated customer into one who orders again. We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand selling K-beauty skincare products to women over 40. We currently sell in Italy, Spain, UK and we're actively expanding across Europe, with new markets launching soon. Paid social is one of our main growth channels — which means most customers meet us through an ad, arrive with questions, and write to us in their own language. Support is not a cost center for us, it's one of the biggest drivers of trust, retention, and repeat revenue. We're looking for someone who can own that inbox across several languages — and who can do it using a modern, AI-driven workflow that lets us answer fast, absorb volume, and open new markets without the quality dropping. This role is ideal for someone who understands e-commerce support, multilingual communication, courier problems, refunds and disputes, AI-assisted workflows, and the difference between closing a ticket and keeping a customer. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE HANDLING --- You'll be working the inbox of a DTC brand running paid traffic, which means: — "Where is my order": stalled tracking, parcels stuck at a hub, deliveries marked complete but never received — Pre-purchase questions: people who saw the ad and want to know if it works and if we're real — Product and skin questions: ingredients, how to use it, what to expect and when, sensitive skin, pregnancy — Reactions and complaints: rare, serious, handled carefully and escalated properly — Refunds, returns and withdrawal: EU consumer rules, our guarantee, and knowing when to say yes — Disputes and chargebacks: PayPal and card cases, caught early enough to resolve instead of lose — Comments and DMs under our ads: public, and often a cold audience's first impression of us — Win-back conversations: the ones that turn a solved problem into another order --- WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR --- We're not looking for someone who writes beautiful, polite emails and nothing else. Anyone can do that now. AI made good prose free, which means good prose is no longer the job. We're looking for someone who works the ticket before writing it. You should: — Read the real carrier events, not the tracking link the customer already saw — Check whether this person wrote before, and what was promised last time — Notice the payment method — PayPal and card have different dispute clocks — Tell a policy abuser apart from someone genuinely upset and about to leave one star — Chase the courier yourself instead of telling the customer to keep waiting — D ---------- within your limits instead of escalating everything and slowing the queue — Close the conversation, so the same person doesn't write three more times You should be able to take a Shopify order, a tracking page that hasn't moved in five days and an angry customer, and turn it into a resolved ticket and a customer who stays. --- LANGUAGES (NON-NEGOTIABLE) --- Our customers write from all over Europe, and every email is answered in the language it arrived in — never in English, and never in something that reads like it came out of a translator. A customer can tell within one sentence. — English at a top level, written and spoken. It's our working language and the one you translate through — You don't need to be native in every market. You do need replies a native reader wouldn't flag as translated — Which means catching what translation tools get wrong: formality in German, politeness register in French, warmth in Italian and Spanish — Any European language you genuinely have is a strong plus, not a requirement — Written level is what counts. You'll be judged on the emails you write, not on a certificate If your English isn't strong enough to move quickly and accurately in both directions, this role isn't the right fit. --- HOW WE USE AI (AND HOW WE DON'T) --- We assume you use AI. Everyone does, and we'd be concerned if you didn't. What matters is how. You should be confident in: — Drafting and translating with it, and holding one consistent tone across every language — Building your own prompts, macros and saved replies, so the same answer isn't rewritten fifty times — Checking every fact first: AI invents shipping dates and policies, and the customer holds us to them — Knowing which tickets it never touches alone: reactions, legal threats, disputes, anyone on their third email — Spotting the answer that is technically correct and still wrong, because it missed the problem underneath — Keeping the result human: a reply that reads as generated costs more trust than a slower one would have If your workflow is pasting the customer's email into ChatGPT and sending back whatever comes out, this role isn't the right fit. --- THE KIND OF PERSON WHO WILL THRIVE HERE --- You'll be a strong fit if you: — Have handled real volume for an e-commerce brand, and know your daily ticket count — Know your own numbers: response time, refund rate, chargeback rate, contact rate — Are comfortable inside Shopify: orders, fulfillments, refunds, customer history — Know what macros, tags and SLAs are actually for — Chase people internally when something is stuck, without being asked twice — Write short: six clear lines beat three paragraphs, in every language — Stay calm with someone being unfair to you, and calm again the third time — Have judgment about money: a partial refund today often beats a chargeback next week — Notice patterns: thirty emails about one thing means something upstream is broken — Care whether the customer comes back, not just whether the ticket is closed We care about support that protects revenue. That doesn't mean saying no to customers. It means every reply — and every refund decision — should support the relationship, the trust, and the next order. --- SKILLS & EXPERIENCE --- Ideally, you have experience with: — Customer service for an e-commerce or DTC brand running paid social — Shopify: orders, refunds, fulfillments, customer history — A helpdesk: Gorgias, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Front, Intercom, or similar — Email, WhatsApp, live chat, and Instagram and Facebook ---------- and comments — Carrier tracking and claims, and dealing with couriers on missing parcels — Refunds, returns and EU consumer rules, including the right of withdrawal — PayPal and card disputes, resolved before they become chargebacks — ChatGPT, Claude, DeepL, or an AI agent inside the helpdesk Bonus if you've worked with beauty, skincare, or K-beauty brands targeting a female audience over 40. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY --- — Answering emails in the language they arrived in, inside our response time targets — Working each ticket properly: order, tracking, history and payment checked before you reply — Chasing couriers on stuck parcels, and d ---------- when to reship — Handling refunds, returns and withdrawal requests within your limits — Catching disputes early, before they become chargebacks — Replying to comments and DMs under our ads, where a cold audience is watching — Improving macros, saved replies and prompts so the whole queue gets faster — Flagging patterns: the product page that causes tickets, the courier that keeps failing — Adapting tone and templates as each new European market opens --- WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU --- — Competitive compensation based on experience — Performance-based bonuses tied to real numbers: response time, satisfaction, refund rate — Access to premium AI and support tools — fully covered by us — Real autonomy: a spending limit you can d ---------- within, from early on — Owning the customer relationship for a brand growing across multiple European markets — Long-term growth with a fast-scaling D2C brand expanding internationally We're building a serious e-commerce brand, and we're looking for someone who knows that support is where trust is either built or lost — using both real judgment about customers and money, and the AI tools that make modern support possible at scale. If you're a multilingual customer service specialist who works the ticket AND lives in the AI workflow, we'd love to hear from you. --- READY TO APPLY? --- If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd love to hear from you. Apply here: ----------

title: Operations & Delivery Manager (Client Systems)
description: About Us Bolder Digital is an Australian-based recruitment agency committed to connecting top Filipino talent with leading businesses globally. We are looking for an individual to join our team and work remotely from the Philippines as we are based in Australia (Remote, based in the Philippines, working on Australian Eastern Time Zone 8/9 AM – 5 PM). Job Type Full-Time – Long term/Gig Start Date: ASAP Compensation: Negotiable — based on proven expertise 1. Purpose of the Role The Operations & Delivery Manager is responsible for turning The Event Engineer methodology into working systems inside client accounts, and for keeping those systems running through every event cycle. This role owns the build, the delivery and the client relationship at an operational level. It is the bridge between what is sold on a strategy call and what actually exists inside GoHighLevel on event day. When a client's funnel, automation, portal or event works, this role built it. When it breaks, this role fixes it. The role is accountable for client outcomes at the delivery layer: events that launch on time, funnels that convert, automations that fire correctly, and clients who feel supported without the Founder having to intervene. 2. Scope Client portfolio: Full operational responsibility for all active equity and retained client accounts, plus incoming Event Engineer beta clients. Typical portfolio size is three to six concurrent accounts, each running its own event cycle. Event volume: Multiple live client events per quarter, each on a recurring turnover cycle of roughly four to six weeks, plus The Event Engineer's own events. Systems: GoHighLevel (all client sub-accounts and the master account), ClickUp, the Event Engineer Studio platform, Canva, Zoom, Facebook Groups, Skool, Circle, Stripe payment configuration within GHL, Replit, and Loom. 3. Key Responsibility Areas 3.1 Client Delivery Management Own the day to day operational relationship with each assigned client. Act as the primary operational point of contact for clients in their dedicated channels, responding to build requests, technical questions and delivery issues. Translate client requests into scoped, prioritised tasks, and push back or escalate where a request falls outside agreed scope. Maintain a prioritised task list per client and keep the client visible on status, blockers and timelines. Run proactive check-ins on an agreed cadence: more frequently in the lead up to an event, weekly at baseline. Send pre-event support messages, event turnover checklists and event reflection forms, and chase the inputs needed to close each cycle. Record walkthrough videos and short training clips so clients can self-serve on recurring tasks. Attend client calls where technical input is required, and convert call outcomes into actioned tasks. Flag client risk early: unmet expectations, scope creep, delivery slippage, or a client going quiet. 3.2 GoHighLevel Build & Automation Design, build, test and maintain the full technical stack inside client sub-accounts. Build and maintain workflows, triggers, conditions, tags, dynamic tags and custom values. Build and maintain email and SMS sequences across every funnel phase: registration, launch, nurture, stick, live day, replay, VIP upsell, retargeting, sales and onboarding. Build funnel pages: landing, registration, thank you, VIP upsell, order, sales, sign in, event portal, replay, waitlist and feedback pages, including mobile views. Configure products, pricing, payment plans, coupons, order bumps and refund processes. Configure calendars, booking flows, forms, surveys and pre-session intake. Manage domains, sub-domains, email deliverability, sender reputation, phone number provisioning and A2P registration. Build and maintain pipelines, opportunity stages and follow-up automations. Set up communities and course delivery inside GHL, and build integrations to external platforms such as Skool and Circle where required. Own snapshot management: creation, versioning, cleanup and deployment across client accounts. Test everything end to end before it goes live. No sequence, page or automation goes to a client without a full test pass. 3.3 Event Delivery Lifecycle Run the full operational cycle for every client event, from set up through to turnover. Pre-event set up Branding board, domain, email, phone integration and account configuration. Build or update the event funnel, portal, community group and all supporting assets. Configure the event calendar invite builder, timezone handling and countdown timers. Schedule the pre-event social, email and SMS sequences. Live event Monitor systems throughout the event and resolve faults in real time. Confirm Zoom links, sign in flows, attendance tracking and portal access are live across all comms before day one. Update replay pages, post daily group content and manage attendance workflows day by day. Post-event turnover Run the standard turnover checklist against every client account: dates in email and SMS copy, automation date triggers, tag names, workflow triggers and conditions, product prices, money-off codes, email and SMS links, pipelines, registration and sign in pages, waitlist updates. Manage refunds, group closure, member removal and the reset of social assets. Set up the next event cycle and confirm the new dates are live everywhere. Progressively automate steps of the turnover so the cycle gets faster each time. 3.4 Gamification & Interactive Builds Design and build instant-feedback gamification systems layered on top of GHL event portals, including chains, hearts, badges, progress trackers and unlockable rewards. Produce the supporting graphics, unlock logic, webhooks and external services required. Build the client-facing explanation assets: how-to-play videos, onboarding emails and walkthrough recordings. Test gamification against real audience conditions and resolve display or trigger failures. 3.5 Event Engineer Product & Systems Support Work alongside the development team on the Event Engineer Studio platform: custom fields, login and access automation, onboarding webhooks, snapshot logic and sub-account provisioning. Participate in structured platform testing cycles and report defects with clear reproduction steps. Maintain the master Event Engineer GHL account: whitelabelling, branding consistency, disclaimers, workflow hygiene and removal of unused sub-accounts. Build internal tools that reduce manual delivery load, including reporting and analysis applications. Confirm build logic with developers where the platform and the delivery methodology intersect. 3.6 Systems Integrity, Documentation & SOPs Run a regular systems health check across GoHighLevel and ClickUp, and report anything breaking or at risk of breaking. Maintain and improve delivery SOPs: event turnover, Zoom configuration, testing checklists, backend event running, gamification builds and client change requests. Document every build so another tea ---------- mber can pick it up. Nothing critical sits only in one person's head. Maintain credential and access hygiene across all platforms, including rotation when a tea ---------- mber or contractor exits. Build and maintain the client change-request process so scope is captured, priced and tracked. 3.7 Delivery Coordination Maintain the ClickUp structure for delivery: lists, statuses, deadlines and priorities across all client accounts. Add realistic duration estimates to build tasks and hold the delivery timeline. Coordinate contractors and developers assigned to delivery work, including briefing, handover and quality review of their output. Schedule client calls and delivery meetings, and manage the meeting cadence per client. Report weekly on delivery status, blockers and upcoming event dates. 4. Success Measures Performance in this role is assessed against: Measure Target On-time event delivery 100% of client events launch on their agreed date with all funnels, automations and portals live and tested Live event fault rate Zero critical faults during a live event. Any fault resolved within the session it occurs in Event turnover completion Full turnover checklist closed within five business days of an event ending Client responsiveness Client operational requests acknowledged same business day, with a clear timeline given Build quality No client-facing build goes live without a documented end to end test pass Documentation coverage Every recurring delivery process has a current SOP that another tea ---------- mber can execute Founder escalation rate Declining volume of delivery issues requiring Founder intervention Continuity A named, briefed backup exists for every client account and every critical system 5. Skills & Experience Required Essential Advanced, hands-on GoHighLevel expertise across workflows, funnels, custom values, snapshots, products, calendars, communities and deliverability. This is the single most important technical requirement. Demonstrated experience building and running online event funnels end to end. Strong automation logic: able to reason about triggers, conditions, tags, timing and re-entry, and to debug why something did not fire. Comfortable with HTML, CSS and JavaScript at the level needed for custom page elements and embedded widgets. Experience with webhooks, APIs and connecting third-party services. Confident client-facing written communication. Able to explain a technical problem to a non-technical business owner without jargon or defensiveness. Project management discipline: able to hold multiple client accounts, multiple event cycles and competing deadlines at once without dropping items. High standard of testing and quality assurance. Checks work before it ships. Desirable Experience with Zapier, Make or n8n. Experience with Skool, Circle, Zoom configuration and Facebook Group management at scale. Experience building lightweight internal tools or apps. Canva and basic design capability for event assets. Prior exposure to equity or revenue-share client models where delivery quality directly drives the fee. 6. Attributes Ownership. Takes a problem to resolution rather than reporting it and waiting. Integrity. Says what is actually true about status and timelines, including when something has slipped. Calm under event pressure. Live events do not allow for panic. Faults get diagnosed and fixed. Systems thinking. Solves the class of problem, not just the instance. Automates repeated work. Boundaried. Supports clients generously without letting client urgency override agreed priorities and scope. Documents by default. Builds so that someone else could take over tomorrow. 7. Working Arrangements Full time, remote, with core overlap to Melbourne business hours. Availability outside standard hours during live client event windows, with time back in lieu. Event weeks are known and blocked in advance. Planned leave to be flagged at least two weeks ahead where possible, with handover notes and a named cover for each active client. Weekly one to one with the Founder, plus participation in team check-ins. 8. Continuity Requirement Because this role holds the technical and operational knowledge for every client account, continuity is a formal part of the job, not an optional extra. The incumbent is required to: Maintain current written SOPs for all recurring delivery processes. Record walkthrough videos for any build that is non-obvious. Keep a live handover document per client covering status, credentials location, open items and known quirks. Brief a nominated backup before any planned absence. How to Apply Submit the following: - Resume - Short cover letter explaining how you are fit to work in this role mentioning the experience you have and how it would help you complete this role at a high level. - A portfolio with any examples - Use the application code WOWZA so we know you’ve read the full role description. IMPORTANT: This is an expert-only position. You will be skills-tested. If you’re not proven, not fast, or not world-class — this isn’t for you.

title: Customer Service Expert — E-Commerce Support at Scale
job_title: Customer Service Expert — E-Commerce Support at Scale
description: We're looking for a customer service specialist who understands one thing clearly: A good reply doesn't just sound polite. It answers the real question, solves the problem before it grows, and turns a frustrated customer into one who orders again. We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand selling K-beauty skincare products to women over 40. We currently sell in Italy, Spain, UK and we're actively expanding across Europe, with new markets launching soon. Paid social is one of our main growth channels — which means most customers meet us through an ad, arrive with questions, and write to us in their own language. Support is not a cost center for us, it's one of the biggest drivers of trust, retention, and repeat revenue. We're looking for someone who can own that inbox across several languages — and who can do it using a modern, AI-driven workflow that lets us answer fast, absorb volume, and open new markets without the quality dropping. This role is ideal for someone who understands e-commerce support, multilingual communication, courier problems, refunds and disputes, AI-assisted workflows, and the difference between closing a ticket and keeping a customer. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE HANDLING --- You'll be working the inbox of a DTC brand running paid traffic, which means: — "Where is my order": stalled tracking, parcels stuck at a hub, deliveries marked complete but never received — Pre-purchase questions: people who saw the ad and want to know if it works and if we're real — Product and skin questions: ingredients, how to use it, what to expect and when, sensitive skin, pregnancy — Reactions and complaints: rare, serious, handled carefully and escalated properly — Refunds, returns and withdrawal: EU consumer rules, our guarantee, and knowing when to say yes — Disputes and chargebacks: PayPal and card cases, caught early enough to resolve instead of lose — Comments and DMs under our ads: public, and often a cold audience's first impression of us — Win-back conversations: the ones that turn a solved problem into another order --- WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR --- We're not looking for someone who writes beautiful, polite emails and nothing else. Anyone can do that now. AI made good prose free, which means good prose is no longer the job. We're looking for someone who works the ticket before writing it. You should: — Read the real carrier events, not the tracking link the customer already saw — Check whether this person wrote before, and what was promised last time — Notice the payment method — PayPal and card have different dispute clocks — Tell a policy abuser apart from someone genuinely upset and about to leave one star — Chase the courier yourself instead of telling the customer to keep waiting — D ---------- within your limits instead of escalating everything and slowing the queue — Close the conversation, so the same person doesn't write three more times You should be able to take a Shopify order, a tracking page that hasn't moved in five days and an angry customer, and turn it into a resolved ticket and a customer who stays. --- LANGUAGES (NON-NEGOTIABLE) --- Our customers write from all over Europe, and every email is answered in the language it arrived in — never in English, and never in something that reads like it came out of a translator. A customer can tell within one sentence. — English at a top level, written and spoken. It's our working language and the one you translate through — You don't need to be native in every market. You do need replies a native reader wouldn't flag as translated — Which means catching what translation tools get wrong: formality in German, politeness register in French, warmth in Italian and Spanish — Any European language you genuinely have is a strong plus, not a requirement — Written level is what counts. You'll be judged on the emails you write, not on a certificate If your English isn't strong enough to move quickly and accurately in both directions, this role isn't the right fit. --- HOW WE USE AI (AND HOW WE DON'T) --- We assume you use AI. Everyone does, and we'd be concerned if you didn't. What matters is how. You should be confident in: — Drafting and translating with it, and holding one consistent tone across every language — Building your own prompts, macros and saved replies, so the same answer isn't rewritten fifty times — Checking every fact first: AI invents shipping dates and policies, and the customer holds us to them — Knowing which tickets it never touches alone: reactions, legal threats, disputes, anyone on their third email — Spotting the answer that is technically correct and still wrong, because it missed the problem underneath — Keeping the result human: a reply that reads as generated costs more trust than a slower one would have If your workflow is pasting the customer's email into ChatGPT and sending back whatever comes out, this role isn't the right fit. --- THE KIND OF PERSON WHO WILL THRIVE HERE --- You'll be a strong fit if you: — Have handled real volume for an e-commerce brand, and know your daily ticket count — Know your own numbers: response time, refund rate, chargeback rate, contact rate — Are comfortable inside Shopify: orders, fulfillments, refunds, customer history — Know what macros, tags and SLAs are actually for — Chase people internally when something is stuck, without being asked twice — Write short: six clear lines beat three paragraphs, in every language — Stay calm with someone being unfair to you, and calm again the third time — Have judgment about money: a partial refund today often beats a chargeback next week — Notice patterns: thirty emails about one thing means something upstream is broken — Care whether the customer comes back, not just whether the ticket is closed We care about support that protects revenue. That doesn't mean saying no to customers. It means every reply — and every refund decision — should support the relationship, the trust, and the next order. --- SKILLS & EXPERIENCE --- Ideally, you have experience with: — Customer service for an e-commerce or DTC brand running paid social — Shopify: orders, refunds, fulfillments, customer history — A helpdesk: Gorgias, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Front, Intercom, or similar — Email, WhatsApp, live chat, and Instagram and Facebook ---------- and comments — Carrier tracking and claims, and dealing with couriers on missing parcels — Refunds, returns and EU consumer rules, including the right of withdrawal — PayPal and card disputes, resolved before they become chargebacks — ChatGPT, Claude, DeepL, or an AI agent inside the helpdesk Bonus if you've worked with beauty, skincare, or K-beauty brands targeting a female audience over 40. --- WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY --- — Answering emails in the language they arrived in, inside our response time targets — Working each ticket properly: order, tracking, history and payment checked before you reply — Chasing couriers on stuck parcels, and d ---------- when to reship — Handling refunds, returns and withdrawal requests within your limits — Catching disputes early, before they become chargebacks — Replying to comments and DMs under our ads, where a cold audience is watching — Improving macros, saved replies and prompts so the whole queue gets faster — Flagging patterns: the product page that causes tickets, the courier that keeps failing — Adapting tone and templates as each new European market opens --- WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU --- — Competitive compensation based on experience — Performance-based bonuses tied to real numbers: response time, satisfaction, refund rate — Access to premium AI and support tools — fully covered by us — Real autonomy: a spending limit you can d ---------- within, from early on — Owning the customer relationship for a brand growing across multiple European markets — Long-term growth with a fast-scaling D2C brand expanding internationally We're building a serious e-commerce brand, and we're looking for someone who knows that support is where trust is either built or lost — using both real judgment about customers and money, and the AI tools that make modern support possible at scale. If you're a multilingual customer service specialist who works the ticket AND lives in the AI workflow, we'd love to hear from you. --- READY TO APPLY? --- If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd love to hear from you. Apply here: ----------

title: Marketing Operations Manager
description: LEAD THE CREATIVE OPERATION. THEN HELP BUILD WHAT COMES NEXT. Creative Production is the center of this role at the start. You will manage the editors, own the production system, raise the quality of the work, and make sure strong creative moves from brief to final asset without senior leadership having to manage every detail. This is not a coordinator role. It is not a virtual-assistant role. We need a Marketing Operations Manager who can operate the day-to-day work and improve the system at the same time. A NOTE FROM OUR CMO Before applying, watch this short video from our CMO about the role, its expectations, and what success looks like: ---------- /share/9cd974e7c8a848de8b84a4a992df4e45 Once Creative Production is stable and you have demonstrated the judgment, leadership, and capacity required, the role will expand into Social Media Operations. That second phase will include the team, publishing, community, creator, affiliate, and channel systems around the content. Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date. The exact timing will depend on demonstrated readiness and business needs. ABOUT VERITAS Veritas builds complete Starlink Mini deployment setups—mounts, power, cables, cases, and accessories—for consumers, work teams, and government fleets. We are a growing US company with a small, high-output marketing team in the Philippines. Several team members have grown with the company over the long term. We want the same for this role. THE DETAILS • Full-time independent contractor role with fixed monthly compensation of $2,000–$2,500 USD, based on experience, leadership depth, and overall fit—not an hourly position • Approximately 45–50 hours per week, with the regular work schedule fully aligned with Pacific Time • Philippine graveyard shift: roughly 11:00 PM–8:00 AM or 12:00 AM–9:00 AM, depending on U.S. daylight saving time • Fully remote and long-term • This must be your only job. No part-time employment, side hustles, ongoing freelance clients, or subcontracting • Occasional weekend availability when production, launches, or publishing require management coverage • Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna required; no regular onsite office days, but occasional in-person meetings may be scheduled WHAT YOU'LL OWN At full production, the team aims to produce one long-form video and up to 14 supporting creative assets each week. These may include shorts/reels, static graphics, or carousels and are adapted for distribution across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X. PHASE 1: LEAD CREATIVE PRODUCTION • Manage a two-person video-editing team, including their priorities, workload, deadlines, coverage, development, and performance. • Turn approved priorities into clear production plans, briefs, scripts, storytelling direction, B-roll needs, and deliverables. • Own the production pipeline: capacity, assignments, dependencies, revisions, blockers, asset readiness, and delivery visibility. • Review short-form, long-form, ads, thumbnails, static assets, carousels, platform versions, and other creative output. • Evaluate the full story—not only whether one shot matches one line. Check hooks, pacing, B-roll, demonstrations, captions, CTAs, factual accuracy, brand alignment, and viewer flow. • Give editors clear, prioritized, actionable feedback and verify that required revisions were completed correctly. • Use performance findings to identify stronger hooks, packaging, formats, V2/V3 opportunities, and creative tests. • Build and improve SOPs, review standards, production trackers, asset repositories, AI-assisted QA, and backup coverage. • Coordinate minor corrections and urgent production support when needed, without turning the role into a primary editing position. PHASE 2: ADD SOCIAL MEDIA OPERATIONS Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date, once Phase 1 is operating reliably and you have demonstrated readiness for the expanded scope. At that point, you will also: • Manage the current Social Media Moderator and future social media team members. • Own the publishing calendar, content inventory, platform schedules, launch pushes, and publishing verification across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X. • Ensure each platform receives the correct version, copy, CTA, description, tags, products, related content, links, and native-platform setup. • Oversee community, marketing inboxes, important comments and messages, channel presentation, and routine reputation handling. • Manage routine creator-partnership and affiliate operations, including communication, records, deliverables, logistics, and escalation. • Own routine UTM, Bitly, campaign-link, profile-link, and destination-verification workflows. • Review social performance and turn findings into decisions, tests, and coordinated creative recommendations. • Build and maintain the social department’s processes, AI workflows, reporting, and continuity systems. HOW THE ROLE FITS You will report to and work closely with senior marketing leadership. In Phase 1, the video editors report to you. In Phase 2, the Social Media Moderator also reports to you. You will have authority over routine departmental planning, assignments, quality, coaching, corrections, and process improvements within approved standards. Cross-functional, sensitive, contractual, financial, policy, staffing, reputation, and other material decisions remain with senior leadership. HOW WE USE AI Our marketing operation uses AI for context, research, briefs, feedback, quality control, documentation, analysis, automation, and institutional memory. We want someone who uses AI heavily to improve judgment and execution—not someone who accepts raw output. Sources must be checked. Brand and product accuracy must be protected. What the team learns should improve the next workflow. YOU'RE A STRONG FIT IF YOU • Have at least eight years of professional work experience. • Have at least three years managing teams and direct reports. • Have at least two years of experience inside a creative or marketing function. • Have meaningful corporate, in-house, agency, or field-based operating experience—not only freelance, VA, or task-based remote experience. • Have managed a creative-production pipeline and can explain the team size, volume, process, problems, decisions, and results. • Are exceptionally strong at storytelling and can diagnose why an edit is technically correct but still wrong for the overall story. • Hands-on video-editing experience is an advantage, but it is not required. You must be able to direct editors, evaluate their work, and clearly explain what needs to change and why. • Can coach editors, address recurring mistakes, manage underperformance, and maintain accountability without becoming the bottleneck. • Take action without waiting for step-by-step direction and consistently look for ways to improve quality, speed, visibility, and continuity. • Use performance evidence to improve creative work—not only report numbers. • Use AI daily with structured context, validation, human review, reusable systems, and feedback loops. • Communicate clearly in conversational American English. • Can sustain a Philippine graveyard schedule and occasional weekend coverage. • Reside in Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna and be willing to attend occasional in-person meetings. • Have reliable primary internet, a backup connection, and backup power. • Want one company to grow with for the long term. THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR • Someone who waits for detailed instructions before acting. • Someone whose experience is limited to task-based VA work, short freelance engagements, or managing multiple clients. • A strong individual contributor who does not want to manage, coach, and hold people accountable. • Someone who reviews only technical editing details but cannot evaluate the complete story and business goal. • Someone who creates more process without improving output, visibility, quality, or results. • Someone planning to keep another job, freelance clients, or subcontract any part of the work. • Someone testing a graveyard schedule for the first time without a credible plan to sustain it. HOW WE WORK Clear priorities. Direct feedback. Strong ownership. Problems are raised early. Decisions are documented. The goal is not to look busy. The goal is to build work that performs and an operation that improves. Our brand voice follows the same standard: short words, short sentences, confident but never salesy. Like a friend who knows the gear. HOW TO APPLY Use this subject line and at least 20 AP: [INSERT REQUIRED WORD] - [X] years of professional experience - [X] years managing teams Include the following: • Your resume with company names, employment dates, role titles, team sizes, and whether each role was corporate, in-house, agency, freelance, or VA work. • Have you directly managed a creative-production or video-production team? Answer Yes or No. If yes, state the team size. • Can you provide examples of videos, campaigns, or creative projects you directly led if you advance to the next stage? Answer Yes or No. Do not send links or detailed explanations at this stage. • In one short logistics block, confirm that this would be your only job and that you would complete all work personally. Include your city or province, most recent U.S.-hours role and actual schedule, primary and backup internet, backup power, and occasional weekend availability. Note: Applications missing any requirement will not be considered.

CREATOR RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT Getting a creator to say yes is only the beginning. You will be responsible for managing the relationship from initial outreach through to receiving the final content. WHAT WE VALUE We are looking for someone who: Is extremely proactive and resourceful Is confident reaching out to strangers Has excellent communication skills Has strong negotiation skills Has good emotional intelligence Can build genuine relationships with creators Is organised and detail-oriented Can manage many creator relationships simultaneously Is comfortable with rejection Can follow up consistently Doesn’t need to be constantly told what to do Can identify opportunities independently Moves quickly Understands social media and online creators Has good creative instincts Understands what makes UGC content engaging Most importantly, we want someone who can get things done. KPIs This is a performance-based role. What You Will Create You will help us produce: Social media graphics and carousels Instagram/Facebook/LinkedIn content Reels and short-form videos Video editing and subtitles/captions Patient education content Diagnostic imaging educational content Referrer/GP communication material Clinic promotional material Flyers, brochures and posters Website and landing-page content Email/newsletter content Recruitment and employer-branding material Clinic announcements and campaigns Presentation graphics and internal communication material Content calendars and campaign ideas Graphic Design Skills You should be highly capable with tools such as: Adobe Photoshop Adobe Illustrator Canva Pro Adobe InDesign or equivalent You must understand branding, typography, visual hierarchy, layout and consistency. description: Company: CareWell Diagnostix Location: Philippines – Remote / Work From Home Employment: Full-Time Working Hours: Melbourne, Australia business hours About CareWell Diagnostix CareWell Diagnostix is a growing diagnostic imaging organisation operating multiple clinics across Melbourne, Australia. We are looking for an experienced Senior Radiology Receptionist to join our remote team. This is a senior position for someone who understands that radiology reception is much more than answering phones. Correct bookings, examination preparation, referral handling and accurate patient information directly affect patient care, clinical workflow and the efficiency of our imaging teams. Key Responsibilities You will assist with: Answering high-volume inbound patient and referrer calls Booking and rescheduling radiology appointments Correctly identifying examinations from referrals Understanding appropriate appointment durations Providing patients with correct examination preparation instructions Managing appointments across different clinics, rooms and modalities Checking referral information before booking Uploading and processing referrals and documents Responding to patient enquiries professionally and empathetically Communicating with GP clinics, specialists and other referrers Managing emails, online enquiries and administrative tasks Following up missing information where required Understanding Medicare/private billing requirements relevant to bookings Escalating clinical or booking questions appropriately rather than guessing Supporting urgent appointment requests Maintaining patient confidentiality and privacy Following CareWell SOPs and approved booking procedures Assisting with training and supporting junior reception team members Identifying recurring booking errors and helping management improve processes Radiology Knowledge We strongly prefer candidates with previous experience working for an Australian radiology/diagnostic imaging provider. Are you available to work Melbourne business hours, including changes associated with Australian daylight saving? title: Client Success Manager / Operations Coordinator
description: The role You are the single point of contact for our clients and the person who keeps delivery moving internally. Half the job is client success: onboarding, weekly comms, reporting, and keeping accounts happy and renewing. The other half is ops: making sure every client request becomes a tracked task, gets QA'd, launches on time, and nothing goes stale. What you'll own Client success (~50%) Own client relationships end-to-end: onboarding calls, weekly/bi-weekly check-ins, monthly performance reviews. Translate performance data (leads, appointments kept, cost per kept appointment) into plain-English updates clients actually understand. Spot churn risk early — slow lead flow, low show rates, quiet clients — and escalate with a fix, not just a flag. Collect creative assets, offers, approvals and account access without being chased. Ops / project coordination (~50%) Run the ClickUp board: every client request becomes a task with owner, due date, and status. No orphan requests. Traffic the creative → QA → launch → optimization loop; chase blockers and keep QA from becoming a bottleneck. Own the Slack request pipeline: intake, prioritization, daily standup of what's due, end-of-day recap of what shipped. Maintain and improve SOPs so the process survives without heroics. Keep trackers, reporting sheets, and dashboards accurate and current. You're a fit if you have 2+ years in client success, account management, or agency project coordination (paid media / marketing agency strongly preferred). Excellent written English — clear, calm, professional under pressure. Comfort with performance numbers: CPL, show rate, cost per kept appointment. You don't need to build ads, but you must read a report and know what's off. Hands-on with ClickUp (or Asana/Monday), Slack, Google Sheets; HighLevel and Meta Ads Manager experience is a big plus. Ruthless follow-through. You close loops without reminders. Nice to have: experience with home-services or local lead-gen clients, appointment-setting funnels, light copy/creative brief writing. Success in the first 90 days Days 1–30: know every client, their offer and their numbers; own the ClickUp board and daily standup. Days 31–60: run all client comms and monthly reporting independently; QA-to-launch cycle time down measurably. Days 61–90: zero stale tasks >7 days, no missed client check-ins, documented SOPs for intake → launch → report. How to apply Send a short note with: (1) an agency/client-facing role you've held and how many accounts, (2) the PM tool you ran and how

description: Full-Time Dispatcher (Remote) Company: Eveready Express Engagement Type: Independent Contractor (Full-Time) Location: Remote About the Role Eveready Express is seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented, and experienced Dispatcher to join our growing logistics team. The ideal candidate must have at least two (2) years of experience working in the U.S. logistics or transportation industry and possess strong dispatching, route planning, and load coordination skills. You should thrive in a fast-paced environment, be able to effectively multitask, possess intermediate English communication skills, demonstrate expert computer skills, and have a growth mindset with a willingness to continuously learn and improve. As a Dispatcher, you will be responsible for coordinating daily transportation operations, negotiating rates, assigning drivers, monitoring shipments, communicating with customers, and ensuring deliveries are completed safely, efficiently, and on time while maintaining compliance with DOT and ELD regulations. Vehicles Being Dispatched 26-Foot Box Trucks (10,000 lb. weight capacity) – Dock-high with lift gate Sprinter Vans Cargo Vans Ram ProMaster (High Roof) About Eveready Express Founded in 1984, Eveready Express is a trusted leader in trucking, courier, logistics, and distribution services. We proudly serve businesses throughout the Northeast by providing dependable transportation solutions backed by honesty, integrity, urgency, teamwork, and exceptional customer service. Key Responsibilities Dispatch Operations Dispatch vehicles based on customer orders, schedules, and driver availability. Negotiate rates with drivers while maintaining a target minimum 40% gross margin. Assign loads efficiently to maximize profitability and operational performance. Coordinate pickups and deliveries to ensure customer service expectations are met. Driver Communication Maintain continuous communication with drivers throughout their routes. Provide dispatch instructions, updates, route changes, and operational support. Ensure drivers follow company procedures and customer requirements. Routing & Scheduling Plan efficient delivery routes to minimize transit time, fuel consumption, and operating costs. Adjust schedules quickly as operational needs or unforeseen circumstances arise. Proactively identify delays and coordinate solutions to minimize service disruptions. Provide timely shipment updates to customers and internal teams. Customer Service Serve as the primary point of contact for customers after dispatch. Respond professionally to customer inquiries. Resolve delivery concerns while maintaining exceptional customer service. Documentation & Compliance Maintain accurate dispatch records, driver logs, shipment notes, Bills of Lading (BOLs), and Proofs of Delivery (PODs). Ensure compliance with DOT regulations, ELD requirements, Hours of Service (HOS), company policies, and customer-specific procedures. Problem Solving Resolve logistical challenges including traffic delays, vehicle breakdowns, weather disruptions, missed appointments, and last-minute schedule changes. Safety & Regulatory Compliance Verify driver qualifications, vehicle readiness, insurance, and compliance with company safety standards. Work closely with HR and Operations to ensure all regulatory requirements are met. Team Collaboration Collaborate with Customer Service, Operations, Billing, Sales, HR, Warehouse, and Drivers to ensure seamless daily operations. Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities to improve dispatch efficiency, operational workflows, and customer satisfaction. Recommend process improvements and innovative solutions to management. Qualifications Required: Minimum of 2 years of experience in the U.S. logistics or transportation industry. Previous experience dispatching 26-foot box trucks, cargo vans, sprinter vans, or final-mile delivery vehicles is required. Strong understanding of DOT regulations, ELD compliance, and Hours of Service (HOS) requirements. Experience negotiating driver rates while maintaining profitability and service quality. Expert computer skills, including the ability to quickly navigate multiple applications, browser tabs, spreadsheets, dispatch platforms, and communication tools simultaneously. Proficiency with Transportation Management Systems (TMS), dispatch software, GPS tracking platforms, load boards, CRM systems, Microsoft Office (especially Excel), Google Workspace, and web-based applications. Strong ability to multitask and manage multiple drivers, customers, deliveries, and priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced environment. Intermediate English communication skills (written and verbal). Excellent organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail. Comfortable communicating professionally with drivers, customers, brokers, and internal teams. Strong critical-thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities. Dependable, self-motivated, highly organized, and capable of working independently with minimal supervision. job_title: GoHighLevel Design Specialist - Websites, Funnels, CSS (PHP 35k)
description: ABOUT US We are an Australian digital marketing agency. We build lead generation systems for construction, trade and home service businesses: solar, electrical, air conditioning, plumbing, bathrooms and builders. We run the ads, we build the pages, and we wire the whole thing into GoHighLevel so every lead is tracked from the ad click through to the booked job. We are small, fast and AI first. You will work directly with the founder. We have not named the company in this ad on purpose. If your application gets through the first screen, we tell you exactly who we are by email, before any interview. THE ROLE, AND WHICH OF OUR TWO GOHIGHLEVEL ADS YOU SHOULD APPLY FOR We are hiring two GoHighLevel specialists at the same time, and we are running two ads so the right person lands in the right seat. This ad is the design seat. You build the websites, the funnels and the pages inside GoHighLevel, and you make them look like they were never built in GoHighLevel. You are the person who makes the system look right. The other ad is the automation and AI seat. Workflows, pipelines, webhooks and the AI features. That person makes the system behave. The two of you will work side by side every day, in the same sub-accounts. So each of you needs a working knowledge of the other half. They will build a page sometimes. You will wire a workflow sometimes. But we are hiring each of you for your strong side, and we will screen you on your strong side. If making pages look great on a phone is what you are best at, this is your ad. If what you are best at is workflows, integrations and AI, apply for the automation ad instead, not this one. Please do not apply for both. Pick the seat that is actually you and we will read it properly. One more thing worth saying plainly, because it saves everybody time. You are not the copywriter. We write the words. You lay them out, and you tell us when the layout is fighting the message. WHAT YOU WILL DO Design and build inside GoHighLevel. This is the seat. - Client websites and funnels in the builder: home, service, about, gallery, opt-in, sales, booking and thank you pages, multi step forms and surveys - Make it not look like GoHighLevel. This is the part almost nobody does well and it is the reason this job exists. Custom CSS and code blocks when the drag and drop builder runs out of road, which is often - Genuinely mobile responsive. The builder fights you on mobile. You win that fight - Sound layout judgement: spacing, hierarchy, type, contrast, and a call to action that is actually findable on a phone in sunlight - Work with real client photography, which is often badly lit and the wrong aspect ratio, and make it look deliberate - Page speed and image handling, so a tradesman's site does not take nine seconds to load - Landing pages for specific ad campaigns, built fast, matched to the ad that points at them - Email and SMS templates, calendars, booking pages and forms that look like the client's brand, not like the platform - Reusable snapshots and templates so a new sub-account is stood up fast rather than rebuilt from zero Make it convert - Every page we build has ads pointed at it, so the page has a job. Forms above the fold on mobile, obvious phone numbers, trust signals where they get seen - Forms that actually submit and actually create the contact. You test the form yourself and keep the proof. We have been burned by a form that showed a success message and quietly discarded every lead Automations. The half you support. - Wire the automation behind your own pages: form submitted, booking confirmed, thank you page redirect, internal notification, the first speed to lead text. Competent, not exceptional. The automation seat owns the complex builds - Read a workflow well enough to see why your form is not triggering it, and fix the simple cases yourself Measurement - Meta Pixel and Google Tag Manager installed on the pages you build, verified as firing - Test every form, trigger link, calendar and redirect before it goes live, and keep the screenshot that proves it fired Domains - Point client domains confidently: A records, CNAMEs, root versus subdomain, SSL, redirects - You know the difference between a DNS change that is safe and one that takes a client's email offline, and you check before you change Documentation - Document what you build so someone else can pick it up THE MONEY, PLAINLY PHP 35,000 per month to start. That is the number on the card and it is what this seat pays from day one. Separately, and honestly: there is more available for someone genuinely exceptional who can prove it. If your number is above 35,000, do not skip this ad. Apply, name your number, and send the live URLs that justify it. We would rather have that conversation than never see your application. On day one you get a written standard describing exactly what good delivery looks like in this seat. At 60 days we review your delivery against that written standard. You will know before you start what you are being measured against. THE ARRANGEMENT, IN PLAIN TERMS Please read this section properly. We would rather you d ---------- it is not for you today than discover something you did not expect in week three. - This is an independent contractor engagement. It is not employment. You invoice us each pay period and we pay the invoice. - You are responsible for your own tax and any local statutory contributions. We do not withhold tax. We do not pay SSS, PhilHealth or Pag-IBIG. - There is no paid annual leave. There is no paid sick leave. There is no 13th month pay. We are telling you this in the ad rather than letting you find it out later. - You are paid twice a month, in PHP, by Wise. - Hours are 7:00am to 3:30pm Philippine time, Monday to Friday. 40 hours a week. - Full time and exclusive for the engagement. Exclusive means what it says: while you are engaged with us you do not hold other retained clients and you do not work for another agency, evenings and weekends included. If you have existing commitments, tell us at application stage. - 3 month probation. - There is a PAID test task before any offer, and for this seat it is a real page build in a sandbox sub-account. We pay you for the time you spend on it, whether or not we make you an offer. - Your equipment and your internet are yours: your own computer, a reliable connection at 25 Mbps or better, a backup connection, and a plan for power outages. - Either side can end the engagement with two weeks written notice. That runs both ways. - We provide and pay for a Claude account. You will use it every day. - You will be inside client CRMs, ad accounts and domain settings. Confidentiality is taken seriously, and you sign a contractor agreement and an NDA before you get access to anything. - Real ownership of the build side of the agency, not a ticket queue. HOW THE INTERVIEW WORKS, SO THERE ARE NO SURPRISES - If you get through the first screen we email you, tell you who we are, and offer you one interview time. One fixed slot, not a range. - Reply and confirm that time in writing. If you do not confirm, we do not hold the slot. - If something comes up, tell us before the slot and we will rebook you once. That happens and it is fine. - If you do not turn up and you did not tell us, your application is closed. In our last round more than half the people we booked did not attend. It cost us an afternoon we could have spent on the people who did. - The interview is a screen share. Add the client type or industry. - READ = I understand what it is and could learn it, but I have never shipped it. - NEVER = I have never touched it, or I do not know what it is. Read this next paragraph carefully because it is part of the test. We expect most applicants to have a lot of NEVERs on this list. Nine NEVERs with five honest DONEs beats eighteen DONEs every time, and an application with no NEVERs will be trusted less, not more. We open the DONEs on a screen share. There is no penalty for NEVER. 1. A client website built in the GHL builder with custom CSS so it does not look like GHL 2. A funnel built in GHL: opt-in, sales, booking and thank you pages 3. A GHL page rebuilt because it broke on mobile, and made genuinely responsive 4. A multi step form or survey with conditional logic 5. Custom CSS written to do something the GHL builder would not do on its own 6. A code block or custom JavaScript added to a GHL page to make something behave 7.
