We've been around since 2012 and are now in an exciting stage of growth: building new technology, training programs, internal systems, and infrastructure to support where the company is going next. We're a lean team with ambitious plans, and we care about doing things well: clean systems, clear communication, strong design, and thoughtful execution. We're not trying to become a huge corporate machine. We want to stay lean, move quickly, and have really capable people doing meaningful work. About the Role: We're looking for a Strategic Executive Assistant to work closely with our COO across creative, operational, and strategic projects. This isn't a traditional VA role where you'll simply be handed a checklist every morning and told what to do. Sometimes you'll get a clear assignment. Other times, you'll get a rough idea, a voice note, or a half-formed concept and need to help turn it into something useful, organized, and polished. That's a big part of the job. This will start as a part-time role, with the opportunity to transition into a full-time position after the first few months if it's a strong mutual fit. Ideally, we're looking for someone who wants to grow with us long-term. One other thing, you don't need to come from finance, although you should be interested in learning it. This is an industry where expertise matters, and the better you understand our business, our advisors, and our clients, the better you'll become at this role. We'll help you learn, but you should genuinely want to. What You'll Do: Project Support: - Organize projects, priorities, meetings, and follow-ups - Coordinate with team members, contractors, and developers - Help make sure things don't quietly fall through the cracks Creative & Communication: - Create beautifully designed presentations, one-pagers, training materials, internal communications, and visual assets - Turn rough notes or concepts into polished outputs - Help maintain consistency across our brand and internal tools - Look at something we've created and tell us, honestly, "this could be better" Systems & Operations: - Maintain daily spreadsheets, trackers, dashboards, and project pipelines - Test new internal tools and identify improvements - Find ways to simplify or automate repetitive work AI & Technology: - Use tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Canva, and Google Workspace to research, create, and improve work - Experiment with new tools and figure things out quickly - Help us find smarter ways to work as new technology becomes available You don't need to know every tool already. Being resourceful and learning quickly matters much more. Who We're Looking For: You'll probably thrive here if you: - Have excellent written English - Are highly organized and dependable - Have strong visual/design taste (this is more important than I'm probably letting on in this posting) - Can work independently without needing constant direction - Learn new tools quickly - Can manage multiple projects without losing the details - Are comfortable receiving direct feedback - Naturally look for better ways to do things - Have high integrity and are comfortable being transparent (this is also more important than I’m probably letting on in this posting) Above everything else, we're looking for judgment, initiative, and ownership. Why Work With Us? - Direct exposure to company leadership and decision-making - Meaningful projects alongside the more traditional VA work - Creative freedom; good ideas are genuinely encouraged - Opportunity to learn AI, technology, operations, and business - Increasing responsibility as your capabilities grow - A real pathway from part-time into a full-time role - A stable company with ambitious long-term growth plans - A predominantly Filipino team and client community (99% of the company and clients come from a Filipino background) - The chance to actually see your work shape how a company operates (for real) How to Apply: If you've made it this far, include the word "builder" somewhere in the first sentence of your application so we know you actually read the posting. title: QA Engineer
description: We are looking for a Mid-Level QA Engineer with strong manual testing experience to join our team and help ensure the quality, usability, and reliability of our web-based products. This role is ideal for someone with 3–5 years of QA experience, particularly within a web development agency, SaaS company, or fast-paced product environment. We are looking for a QA professional who goes beyond simply following test cases. You should be naturally curious, able to think like a real user, identify edge cases and unexpected behaviors, and proactively raise issues and improvements before they reach customers. As our QA workflow continues to evolve, you will also be expected to work comfortably with AI-assisted testing tools and modern QA practices. Automation experience is not required for this position. Key Responsibilities 1. Manual & Exploratory Testing • Perform comprehensive manual testing of web applications and features. • Conduct exploratory testing to identify unexpected behaviors, usability issues, and edge cases. • Test beyond the expected "happy path" to identify scenarios that may not have been considered during development. • Validate new features, bug fixes, integrations, workflows, and system changes. • Perform regression testing to ensure existing functionality remains stable after updates. • Test across different browsers, devices, and screen sizes. • Identify issues from both a functional and user-experience perspective. 2. Web & Mobile Application Testing • Test responsive web applications across desktop, tablet, and mobile environments. • Participate in testing upcoming mobile applications and mobile-specific workflows. • Validate functionality across different devices, browsers, operating systems, and screen sizes. • Identify UI inconsistencies, usability concerns, navigation issues, and device-specific problems. 3. Test Planning & Quality Assurance • Review requirements, specifications, designs, and user stories to identify potential testing risks. • Create and maintain test scenarios, test cases, checklists, and testing documentation where appropriate. • Determine what areas require deeper testing based on the complexity and risk of a change. • Conduct regression testing before releases. • Verify reported bugs and confirm fixes. • Help establish practical QA standards and processes as the team continues to improve its development workflow. 4. Bug Identification & Reporting • Identify, document, prioritize, and communicate software defects clearly. • Provide detailed reproduction steps, expected results, actual results, and supporting evidence. • Work closely with developers to investigate and resolve issues. • Retest fixes and ensure issues are properly resolved before release. • Distinguish between critical defects, functional issues, usability concerns, and minor improvements. 5. AI-Assisted QA • Use AI tools to improve testing efficiency, test coverage, documentation, and analysis. • Be open to incorporating AI into day-to-day QA workflows. • Work alongside emerging AI-assisted and Playwright-based testing processes. • Identify opportunities where AI can improve testing without compromising quality or critical thinking. • Maintain ownership of QA decisions rather than relying blindly on automated or AI-generated results. 6. Collaboration & Continuous Improvement • Work closely with developers, product stakeholders, and other team members throughout the development lifecycle. • Communicate issues and risks clearly and constructively. • Ask questions when requirements or expected behavior are unclear. • Proactively suggest improvements to product quality, testing processes, and user experience. • Follow through on identified issues until they are appropriately resolved. • Contribute to a collaborative, communicative, and quality-focused team environment. What We're Looking For Required Qualifications • 3–5 years of professional QA/testing experience. • Strong experience in manual software testing. • Experience testing web applications. • Experience in a web development agency, SaaS company, or similar fast-paced technology environment. • Experience with functional, regression, exploratory, and cross-browser testing. • Experience testing responsive web applications across different devices and screen sizes. • Strong ability to identify edge cases and unexpected user scenarios. • Strong attention to detail without losing sight of the overall user experience. • Ability to work independently and manage testing priorities with limited supervision. • Strong written and verbal communication skills. • Comfortable working with developers and other technical team members. • Willingness to learn and use AI-assisted QA tools and modern testing workflows. Nice to Have • Experience testing mobile applications. • Experience working with SaaS products. • Understanding of common SaaS concepts such as: - User roles and permissions - Multi-tenancy - User workflows - Integrations - Authentication and authorization - Data dependencies • Basic understanding of APIs and API testing. • Familiarity with browser developer tools. • Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Linear, ClickUp, GitHub, or similar project/issue-tracking platforms. • Exposure to Playwright or other test automation frameworks. • Basic understanding of SQL/database validation. job_title: VIDEO EDITOR, SHORT-FORM REELS (Remote · PHP & SA)
description: WHO WE ARE We're a small creator-management agency (Portugal HQ) that builds handmade brands for a tiny roster of creators. The founder works on every account. We're hiring our first dedicated editor for one flagship creator: a cozy homemaker lifestyle brand (warm home, garden, cooking, comfort) with a retro-gaming thread woven through it. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY EDIT Instagram Reels (15 to 30s) for a warm domestic-lifestyle brand. Think lamp-lit rooms, cooking and garden moments, soft-spoken voiceover, a retro game paused on the TV in the background. Warm and cozy, but never slow or boring. Our editing style: - 2-3s pacing rule - Something must happen every 2 to 3 seconds: a sound effect, a subtle zoom, a cut, a text pop, an on-screen detail. Micro-events keep retention high. The trick is doing this while the reel still FEELS calm and warm, not chaotic. Gentle movement, not zoom-punch spam. - Optimal trimming - Tight cuts, no dead air, no wasted frames. Every clip trimmed to its best moment. - Sound design as a core skill - Domestic texture (kettle, chopping, rain on the window, keyboard clicks) layered with retro game SFX accents and a whisper-register voice. You'll integrate sound effects constantly. Our audience recognizes the brand by sound in 3 seconds. - Simple, clean transitions and effects - Smooth and purposeful. No flashy transition packs, no trend-chasing effects that fight the cozy vibe. - Nostalgia-literate accents - You don't need to be a Nintendo expert. You'll work from our reference bank of era-correct sounds and visuals, and you'll learn why a 1998 chest-opening sound outperforms any trending audio for our audience. You'll get a full style bible, hook templates, banned-elements list, and direct feedback from the founder. We want an editor who becomes THE voice of this brand's edit, not a gig-worker juggling 30 clients. WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU - Some experience with short-form vertical content (Reels, Shorts, TikTok). Show us, don't tell us. - Strong pacing instincts: you know how to keep a reel alive every 2 to 3 seconds without making it feel loud - Clean audio mixing and confident sound-effect work. This brand lives and dies on sound. - Solid color grading fundamentals (warm grades, skin tones) - CapCut, Premiere Pro, or DaVinci Resolve all welcome. We judge the output, not the software. - A good laptop that can handle raw vertical footage and deliver on deadline - Fluent written English. Feedback loops are async and fast. - Reliable internet Bonus points: you've edited cozy-lifestyle, cooking, home, or ASMR-adjacent content · you understand parasocial audiences · you grew up on PlayStation, Nintendo, or Sega · you've worked with creator brands before.

title: Deep-Research Investigator — Skip Tracing, Public Records & Property Title (Real Estate)
job_title: Deep-Research Investigator — Skip Tracing, Public Records & Property Title (Real Estate)
description: Read this first: Most "research" jobs are box-checking. This one isn't. We buy distressed, tax-delinquent, and inherited (probate) real estate in Minnesota, and before we can help a homeowner or an heir, we first have to find the right human being — often someone who has died, moved five times, or never wanted to be found in the first place. That's your job: take a property and a half-dead trail of information and figure out who legally owns it, who inherited it, and how to reach them. You are the detective at the very front of everything we do. If you get it right, a family gets helped and we do a deal. If you get it wrong, everything downstream breaks. We are looking for one exceptional person. Not five average ones. What the work actually looks like: A few real examples of the thinking we need: 1. The obituary nugget. The owner died. You find the obituary — and instead of skimming it, you read every single line. Buried in paragraph four is "she is survived by her daughter, Maria (Robert) Thompson of Bloomington." That one line just gave you a married daughter, a son-in-law's name, and a city. Most people miss it. You don't. 2. The dead end that isn't. The phone is disconnected. The address is vacant. The person is deceased. A box-checker stops here and writes "unable to locate." You think: okay, who are their people? You find their Facebook, you see who comments "love you mom" every year on the memorial post, you trace the daughter, you find the daughter's spouse, you build the path. You treat a dead end as a puzzle, not a stop sign. 3. The messy title. Grandpa died without a will. He had four kids; one of them died before him and left two kids of her own. There's an old mortgage and a lien. You don't just report that — you can reason about who actually has to sign to sell this property and what fraction each person owns, because you understand how title and inheritance work. If reading those three scenarios made you a little excited, keep reading. If they sounded tedious, this role will make you miserable — please don't apply. Who you are: You think like an investigator, not a clerk. You are genuinely intelligent and you love connecting scattered pieces into a picture nobody else could see -- the entire role is essentially like stalking a scummy boyfriend who you suspect might be messing around -- same mindset, really. You get a small thrill from finding the thread everyone else walked past. You are relentlessly detail-oriented. You read the whole document. You notice the middle initial, the maiden name, the second address, the neighbor's last name. You assume the one clue you need is hiding in the part everyone else skips. You are resourceful and creative under a dead end. When the obvious path fails, you already have three more. You know your way around public records, county sites, genealogy and obituary sources, social media, and open-source research (OSINT) techniques. You understand property and legal structure. You can read a deed, follow a chain of title, and reason about heirs and ownership shares. We keep everything ethical and above-board, but you need to actually understand the machinery. You are fluent with AI, and you use it every day. This is non-negotiable. We run our research with AI tools — especially Claude (Cowork) — and you'll be expected to work alongside it fluently: prompting it well, checking its work, and using it to move faster without ever letting it think for you. If you're not already comfortable living inside AI tools daily, this isn't the role for you. Hands-on experience with DataSift / ReiSift (our CRM) is a strong plus. Backgrounds we especially want (any one of these moves you to the top of the pile): Private investigation, skip tracing, or asset/people location OSINT / open-source intelligence research Intelligence, law-enforcement, or government investigative service (e.g., NBI, NICA, PNP intelligence, military intelligence) Title abstracting or work at a title company, title insurance, or a real estate law office Paralegal / legal research, especially anything touching estates, probate, or property You do not need all of these. One of them, done well, plus the right mind, is what we want. What you'll do day to day: Run deep research on specific properties and people using Claude Co-Work, public records, county assessor/recorder data, court and probate records, obituaries, genealogy tools, and social media Determine the correct legal owner, confirm whether they're living or deceased, and map out heirs and decision-makers Trace and verify current contact paths for the right people Document everything with sources, so the next person can trust and re-check your work Flag the messy title situations that need extra legal thinking, and reason through them with us This is a research-focused, low-phone role. You'll rarely be on live calls. If you love the hunt and hate cold-calling, that's a feature, not a bug. A note on our team: ARCH is a women-led company, and right now our whole team is women. We're proud of the supportive, collaborative, drama-free culture we've built, and to keep that going we're prioritizing female applicants for this role. Availability: To start: ~30 hours/week, with a clear path to full-time for the right person Core hours overlap with U.S. Central Time (Monday–Friday); occasional Saturday if a deal is hot Ideally ~6 hours/day, 5 days/week Compensation: Up to $10 USD/HR with $ ---------- bonus/closed transaction (averaging 3-5 transactions/month), total monthly income to be around (10*30HRS*4 weeks) + (300 per file bonus * 3-5 bonuses/month) = $2100-$3000USD/month. If you're truly exceptional, bonuses may become even larger. – Up to $10 USD/hour based on experience -- lower hourly rate if low experience, plus performance bonuses for hard-to-find location wins. Compensation will be reviewed and raised as you prove yourself. We pay more for people who are genuinely great, and we keep them. How to apply — read carefully, this is part of the test: We screen hard, on purpose. Follow these instructions exactly — attention to detail is the job, so this is your first audition. Applying takes two steps, and you must do both. ⚠️ READ THIS: If you do not follow every single instruction below, exactly — the subject line, both personality tests, the PrinciplesYou PDF attached, the screen-recording, and both application steps — your application will be immediately rejected and will not be reviewed at all. No exceptions, no follow-up, no second chances. This is not us being harsh; following precise instructions is the job. If that already sounds like too much, this role is not for you. Step 1 — Email your full application Email everything to ---------- with the exact subject line "REAL ESTATE RESEARCHER" (applications without this exact subject line are deleted unread). Include all of the following: 1. Your resume. 2. A short note (5–8 sentences): Tell us about the single hardest person or piece of information you ever had to track down — what made it hard, and how you cracked it. Be specific. Two personality tests (complete both): 3. DISC — free at ---------- (attach or paste your results) 4. PrinciplesYou — free at ---------- . After you finish the assessment, click "Invite and Share" in the left menu, then under "Download as PDF" click DOWNLOAD, and attach that PDF to your email. 5. A 5-10 minute screen-recording (or however long you need -- the more thorough and better your research is -- great!) where you complete a small test search and talk out loud through your thinking the entire time. We care far more about how you think than whether you get the "right" answer. Your test task: Using free public information and any other tools & websites you want, find out everything you can about the current owner of this property: 1235 Thomas Ave N, Minneapolis, MN ---------- Who owns it? Are they living or deceased? If deceased, who are the likely heirs and how would you try to reach them? Any thoughts about the property? Any information you found in public records? Show us your screen and narrate every step, every source, and every dead end and how you got around it. One-line answer: In the test research above, what was the single most useful piece of information you found, and where exactly did you find it? Step 2 — Message me here on OnlineJobs.ph After you email, also send me a direct message right here through OnlineJobs.ph letting me know your application is in your inbox. Doing both steps is itself part of the test — it tells us you can follow a multi-part instruction exactly. Applicants who skip either step, leave out any of the five items, or ignore the subject-line instruction will not be considered. We read every complete application carefully. If you're the person we're describing, you'll enjoy this — and we'd love to meet you.

description: Senior Accountant Accounting & Bookkeeping · DDM Properties Ltd. · Sunset Reef St. Kitts Position Summary The Senior Accountant is responsible for the full-cycle accounting and bookkeeping function of DDM Properties Ltd., operating Sunset Reef St. Kitts. Sunset Reef is a luxury boutique resort with seven suites, a restaurant, and a beach bar. The role maintains accurate books in QuickBooks Desktop, produces management and owner/shareholder reporting, and ensures all statutory tax and payroll filings are prepared on time. Corporate tax returns are filed by BDO; this position prepares complete, audit-ready packages, meets every internal and statutory deadline, and is the primary day-to-day liaison with BDO for filings and consultation. Key Details Company: DDM Properties Ltd. (Sunset Reef St. Kitts) Location: St. Kitts (on-island preferred; remote/hybrid may be considered for an exceptional candidate) Reports to: Owners / Directors and General Management Department: Finance & Administration Employment type: Full-time Core Responsibilities Bookkeeping & General Ledger • Own the complete general ledger in QuickBooks Desktop, including chart of accounts maintenance, journal entries, accruals, prepayments, and month-end close. • Process accounts payable and receivable; match invoices to purchase orders and guest/vendor records; manage vendor statements and payment runs. • Reconcile all bank, credit card, merchant (Airbnb and other OTA), and cash accounts monthly; investigate and clear reconciling items promptly. • Record revenue by unit, channel, and period; track deposits, refunds, owner draws, and intercompany or related-party transactions. • Maintain fixed-asset register, depreciation, and capital expenditure records for resort buildings, plant, vehicles, marine assets, and equipment. • Enforce coding standards, supporting documentation, and internal controls so books are always audit-ready. Excel Reporting & Analysis • Build and maintain Excel workbooks using PivotTables, Power Query, lookup functions, and structured tables for operational and financial analysis. • Produce monthly management packs: P&L vs. budget, cash position, occupancy/revenue by unit, payroll cost, utilities, maintenance, and food & beverage where applicable. • Prepare owner and shareholder reports with clear commentary on variances, cash flow, and material issues. • Support annual budget and rolling forecast processes with source data and scenario analysis. Tax Compliance, Deadlines & BDO Liaison • Own the tax calendar. Ensure every statutory deadline is met. Escalate risks early to management and owners. • Prepare and file (or coordinate filing of) recurring St. Kitts & Nevis obligations as applicable, including VAT returns, Social Security (C3) and related payroll remittances, Hotel & Restaurant Tax, withholding tax, and any other IRD or Social Security Board filings. • Prepare complete year-end packages for corporate income tax (CIT-101 / CIT-100 as applicable): trial balance, financial statements, supporting schedules, fixed-asset and capital-allowance workings, and reconciling items. • Coordinate with BDO as the firm that files corporate taxes and provides consultation. Supply BDO with accurate, timely information; track open queries; implement BDO recommendations once approved by owners. • Monitor corporate tax installment dates and year-end filing (typically 3½ months after fiscal year-end) so BDO can file on time. • Maintain tax working papers and correspondence so any IRD or Social Security review can be answered quickly. Payroll, People Costs & Controls • Support or own payroll processing, statutory deductions, and remittances in line with St. Kitts labour and Social Security rules. • Track staff entitlements relevant to accounting (leave accruals, severance provisions where required) and keep payroll records complete. • Assist management with cash-flow planning so tax, payroll, and vendor obligations are funded before due dates. Stakeholder Reporting • Report clearly and on schedule to management, owners, and shareholders. • Flag cash shortfalls, unusual transactions, control gaps, and tax exposure without delay. • Support ad hoc owner requests, lender or insurance information packs, and due-diligence data rooms as needed. Required Qualifications & Skills • QuickBooks Desktop: Proven, hands-on experience as a power user (company file maintenance, banking, A/P, A/R, inventory or job costing if used, custom reporting, year-end close). QuickBooks Online alone is not sufficient. • Excel: Advanced skills required. Must be fluent with PivotTables and PivotCharts, filters and slicers, SUMIFS/INDEX-MATCH or XLOOKUP, data validation, and clean workbook design. Ability to turn QuickBooks exports into owner-ready analysis. • Experience: Minimum 5 years of progressive accounting or bookkeeping experience, including at least 2 years at a senior or sole-charge level. Hospitality, vacation rental, multi-unit property, or multi-entity experience is a strong advantage. • Education / designation: Diploma or degree in Accounting, Finance, or equivalent. ACCA, CPA, CMA, or similar designation preferred but not mandatory if experience is strong. • Tax literacy: Working knowledge of corporate tax packages, VAT or sales-tax returns, and payroll/statutory remittances. Experience with St. Kitts & Nevis IRD and Social Security Board processes is highly desirable. • Communication: Clear written reporting to non-accountants (owners and operations). Professional liaison with external accountants (BDO) and government agencies. • Work style: Deadline-driven, discreet with owner financial information, comfortable in a small-team resort environment, and able to work with incomplete handoffs and operational data from multiple sources. Preferred Experience • St. Kitts & Nevis statutory filings: VAT, CIT, Social Security C3, Hotel & Restaurant Tax, withholding tax. • Multi-currency books (XCD / USD / CAD) and related-party or owner-operated structures. • Airbnb, VRBO, or other OTA payout reconciliation. • Working with an external firm (such as BDO) that signs and files the corporate return. • IFRS-style financial statements or year-end packages suitable for IRD filing. Success Measures • Month-end close completed on an agreed timetable with reconciled banks and a clean trial balance. • Zero missed statutory or BDO handoff deadlines. • Owner/shareholder packs delivered on schedule, with explanations that can be acted on. • BDO receives complete, consistent working papers with minimal rework. • Books remain current, coded consistently, and support operational decisions at the resort.

title: Social Media & Paid Ads Assistant — Long-Term Position
job_title: Social Media & Paid Ads Assistant — Long-Term Position
description: Social Media & Paid Ads Assistant — Long-Term Position AP Rollerskating is looking for a reliable, detail-oriented Social Media & Paid Ads Assistant to help us grow our roller skating academy. We offer programs for both children and adults. Our goal is not simply to post more content. We want to build an upbeat, engaged online presence that helps more people discover our programs and ultimately become students. This is a long-term position with stable hours. We are looking for someone who wants to learn our business, become part of our team, and take genuine ownership of their responsibilities. ## What You Will Do Your primary responsibility will be making sure our social media content is organized, prepared, and published consistently. Your regular responsibilities will include: * Pulling photos and short video clips from our media folders * Scheduling daily Facebook and Instagram content * Publishing 3–7 Facebook and Instagram Stories each day * Editing short videos into simple Reels using CapCut, VN, or Canva * Writing and adapting captions using the examples and guidelines we provide * Responding to comments and messages using approved scripts * Keeping our content calendar organized and up to date * Tracking inquiries and leads accurately * Providing a simple weekly report showing what was posted, engagement, leads generated, and work completed Training will be provided for our systems and processes. Paid Advertising Responsibilities We plan to run Facebook and Instagram lead-generation campaigns for our roller skating programs. Experience with Meta Ads Manager is strongly preferred. Depending on your experience, you may also help with: * Setting up Facebook and Instagram lead-generation campaigns * Creating and testing ad images, videos, copy, headlines, and calls to action * Setting up and managing Meta lead forms * Checking campaigns regularly to make sure they are working correctly * Tracking leads, cost per lead, and basic campaign results * Preparing simple weekly performance reports * Making approved adjustments to improve campaign performance You will not be permitted to launch campaigns, change budgets, or increase advertising spend without approval. If you have strong social media skills but limited paid ads experience, you may still apply. Please be honest about what you have personally done inside Meta Ads Manager. What We Are Looking For The right person will have: * Strong written English * Reliable internet and a dependable computer * Excellent organization and attention to detail * Consistent work habits and the ability to meet daily deadlines * The ability to follow documented systems and instructions * Comfort learning new software * A positive, friendly, and professional attitude * The confidence to ask questions when something is unclear * The ability to complete work without being constantly reminded We do not expect you to know everything on your first day. We do expect you to be dependable, honest, willing to learn, and committed to doing high-quality work. Preferred Experience Experience with any of the following is helpful: * Facebook and Instagram content management * Meta Business Suite * Meta Ads Manager * Facebook lead-generation campaigns * Canva * CapCut, VN, or similar video-editing software * Social media reporting and lead tracking Work Schedule * Approximately 10–20 hours per week, depending on experience and speed * Flexible working hours, provided daily responsibilities are completed on time * Availability to check messages and campaign activity twice each workday * Some overlap with U.S. Eastern Time may occasionally be required for training or team meetings Compensation * Competitive monthly salary based on experience and demonstrated ability * Stable, long-term work * Training, clear expectations, and ongoing support * The opportunity to take on greater responsibility as you learn our business and produce results How to Apply Use this exact subject line: **AP Social Media Assistant — Consistency Matters** Please include all of the following: 1. A short introduction about yourself 2. A link to your OnlineJobs.ph profile 3. Links to social media pages you have personally worked on, if available 4. Your expected monthly salary in U.S. dollars 5. The number of hours you would like to work each week 6. A description of your experience with Meta Ads Manager and Facebook lead-generation campaigns 7. An example of a paid campaign you worked on, including what you personally handled and the results, if available 8. One sentence explaining why consistency matters in social media 9. The words **“Wheels Up”** at the very end of your application Please do not claim that you “managed” an account if you only created posts for it. We appreciate applicants who are clear and honest about exactly what they have done. Applications missing any of the requested information will not be considered. Attention to detail is an important part of this position, and the application instructions are the first opportunity to demonstrate it. We are excited to find someone who wants a stable, positive, long-term working relationship and gets real satisfaction from dependable, high-quality work.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
job_title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description: READ THIS FIRST We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California. This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment. This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here. On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here. If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work. THIS IS A SALES ROLE. YOU NEED AT LEAST 6 MONTHS OF EXPERIENCE PERSUADING PEOPLE AND MOVING THEM TOWARD A BOOKED APPOINTMENT OR A SALE. OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses). 13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top. --- ABOUT THE COMPANY You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years. The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market. You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked. A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time. We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't. --- WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support. Daily: - Call new Facebook/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day) - Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time. - Respond to inbound SMS, Facebook ---------- , and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them - Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel - Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar - Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs - Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM) - Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers Weekly: - One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min) - Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings - Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them During training (first 2–4 weeks): We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence. --- A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY) We use a script. We also need you to think. Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words. Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment. This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you. Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works. If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well. --- SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES) All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning. - US workdays: Monday through Friday - US days off: Saturday and Sunday - Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call) - Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March): Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT - A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time - A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time - Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night) Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November): - Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT - Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit. Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying. --- COMPENSATION Base pay: $900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month. 13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000. Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly): - $3 per new client showed appointment - $2 per existing client showed appointment - $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon) Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly): - +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month - +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month - +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month Worked examples: Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 (midpoint) - Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90) - Threshold bonus: $75 - Total: ~$1,250/month Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 - Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120) - Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150) - Total: ~$1,475/month Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked): - Base: $1,000 - Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking) - Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350) - Total: ~$2,025/month This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role. --- OTHER BENEFITS 1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year 2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can. 3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation. To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form --- TARGET KPIs - Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+ - Show Rate: 90%+ - Bookings per day: 4–9 - Showed appointments per month: 100–160 - Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit. --- WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Background: - Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders. - Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required. Non-negotiable skills: The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for: - Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role. - Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings. - Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going. - Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe. - Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists. Everything else: - ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier. - STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work. - Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application. - Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind. - Script discipline for the structured parts of the call. - Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused. - Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified. - Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising. - Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance. - CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred. - High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one. - Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing. - Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load. Preferred: - Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry - Personal interest in beauty or self-care - Experience working with older female clientele (35–65) - Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster) Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT): We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean: - Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout. - Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words. - Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat. - Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down. - Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses. - KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them. --- TECH REQUIREMENTS Non-negotiable: - Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire. - Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application. - Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop - Mouse - Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods. - Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls. - Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients. Preferred: - Second monitor - You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster) --- DO NOT APPLY IF: - You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait. - You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it. - You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next. - You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking. - You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale. - Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker - You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast. - You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure - You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating" - You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it" - You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term - You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation --- HIRING PROCESS 1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions 2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner 3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay 4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion 5. Offer — targeting hires between August 28 – September 7 6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance --- HOW TO APPLY Submit your application through this Tally form: | ---------- | IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience. The form will ask for: - A screenshot of your typing test results ( ---------- ) - A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net) - A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor) - A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages - A few short questions to gauge fit - A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar) - A short Loom video introducing yourself Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form. --- Looking forward to meeting the right person. Ethan Founder, Midnight Siren --- Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning. - US workdays: Monday through Friday - US days off: Saturday and Sunday - Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call) - Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March): Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT - A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time - A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time - Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night) Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November): - Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT - Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit. Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying. --- COMPENSATION Base pay: $900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month. 13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000. Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly): - $3 per new client showed appointment - $2 per existing client showed appointment - $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon) Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly): - +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month - +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month - +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month Worked examples: Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 (midpoint) - Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90) - Threshold bonus: $75 - Total: ~$1,250/month Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month: - Base: $950 - Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120) - Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150) - Total: ~$1,475/month Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked): - Base: $1,000 - Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking) - Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350) - Total: ~$2,025/month This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role. --- OTHER BENEFITS 1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year 2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can. 3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation. To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form --- TARGET KPIs - Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+ - Show Rate: 90%+ - Bookings per day: 4–9 - Showed appointments per month: 100–160 - Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit. --- WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Background: - Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders. - Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required. Non-negotiable skills: The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for: - Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role. - Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings. - Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going. - Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe. - Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists. Everything else: - ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier. - STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work. - Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application. - Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind. - Script discipline for the structured parts of the call. - Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused. - Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified. - Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising. - Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance. - CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred. - High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one. - Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing. - Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load. Preferred: - Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry - Personal interest in beauty or self-care - Experience working with older female clientele (35–65) - Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster) Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT): We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean: - Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout. - Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words. - Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat. - Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down. - Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses. - KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them. --- TECH REQUIREMENTS Non-negotiable: - Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire. - Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application. - Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop - Mouse - Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods. - Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls. - Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients. Preferred: - Second monitor - You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster) --- DO NOT APPLY IF: - You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait. - You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it. - You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next. - You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking. - You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale. - Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker - You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast. - You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure - You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating" - You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it" - You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term - You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation --- HIRING PROCESS 1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions 2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner 3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay 4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion 5. Offer — targeting hires between August 28 – September 7 6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance --- HOW TO APPLY Submit your application through this Tally form: | ---------- | IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience. The form will ask for: - A screenshot of your typing test results ( ---------- ) - A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net) - A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor) - A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages - A few short questions to gauge fit - A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar) - A short Loom video introducing yourself Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form. --- Looking forward to meeting the right person. Ethan Founder, Midnight Siren --- Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

Demonstrate success managing full site backups, staging environments, and seamless site transfers/migrations with minimal downtime. Track record of optimizing WordPress sites to hit PageSpeed Insights (PSI) scores of 80+ (Mobile & Desktop) and top GTmetrix grades. Experience deploying security plugins/firewalls (Wordfence, Solid Security, etc.), monitoring brute-force attacks, patching backend vulnerabilities, and cleaning malware. Skill in verifying and troubleshooting custom JavaScript snippets, event pixels (Meta, GA4), call tracking (CallRail), and conversion tags using Browser Developer Tools (Console/Network tab). Familiarity with setting up, reading, and managing performance alerts or similar auditing tools. Experience configuring and managing automated uptime monitoring and escalating downtime alerts outside standard hours. Ability to establish baseline testing protocols before monthly maintenance workflows, including safe plugin updates, vulnerability scanning, and post-update QA testing. What We Are Looking For This role is a great fit if you want to grow your technical hard skills. Ideal candidates: Enjoy solving complex technical puzzles and critical thinking. Have a strong problem-solving mindset. Feel comfortable explaining technical issues clearly. Are eager to learn, take ownership, and step up to urgent site issues. Are forward-thinking problem solvers. They see where an issue is heading and plan two steps ahead to prevent downstream issues. This team works across time zones with limited real-time overlap, so updates can't wait for someone to come ask. Documents as they go: time logs, ticket notes, and QA steps live in the system. Takes ownership through to verification: Uses critical thinking skills to assess if the root cause is confirmed fixed, not just the symptom. Escalates early when something's outside their depth, rather than quietly guessing on a live client site. Works well independently and asynchronously, while staying looped in with the maintenance and migration teams during handoffs. ==================== TO APPLY: Incomplete applications will not be considered. ==================== If you’re ready to join a team where you can make a lasting impact, follow the instructions below to apply: Your Response Must Include: - A resume or detailed work history showcasing your relevant experience. Complete, thoughtful answers to the following questions: 1. Senior Ownership, Decision-making, and Communication As a senior escalation point for the Web Maintenance team, you’d be solving complex technical puzzles independently. How do you document your troubleshooting steps for the rest of the team, and how do you d ---------- when to solve a problem yourself versus when to escalate? 2. Performance Optimization and Conversion/Tracking Priority Can you walk me through your process for speeding up a slow website while ensuring that background scripts, analytics, and marketing integrations continue to function properly? 3. DNS, Domains, & Basic Networking Skills When managing website migrations or launches, how do you handle DNS updates (like A records, CNAMEs, and MX records) to ensure the site launches seamlessly without breaking the client’s email or triggering downtime? 4. WordPress Security Best Practices With over 150 client sites under our care, keeping sites secure and updated without causing downtime is a daily priority. WHAT YOU WILL DO 1) Claim jobs fast, and only the right ones - Monitor multiple WhatsApp groups where transportation jobs are posted all day. - Before accepting a job, immediately check our drivers' live locations, current assignments and upcoming schedules to confirm we can cover it. - Accept and claim jobs within seconds when we can cover them. 2) Assign and confirm - Assign or pre-book the appropriate driver for each accepted job. - Send the complete trip information to the driver and confirm the driver received and acknowledged it. - Check for scheduling conflicts and prevent double bookings. 3) Monitor every active trip - Track each trip in real time: driver on location, passenger on board, trip completed. - If a driver is late, unresponsive or has an issue, act immediately: contact the driver, update the appropriate person, and arrange backup coverage when needed. - Handle airport pickups, flight delays and last-minute schedule changes calmly. 4) Keep the tracking sheet perfect Every job must be entered into our Google Sheets tracker with: - Trip date and time - Pickup and drop-off locations - Passenger information - Assigned driver - Company that provided the job, and the specific dispatcher who sent it - Total job amount, driver pay, expected profit - Payment terms, due date, and payment status (paid, pending or late) This is how we know exactly who gave us each job and who we need to follow up with for payment, so accuracy is not optional. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR Required - Previous dispatch or live-operations experience in a fast-paced, last-mile environment. - Excellent spoken and written English; you will be communicating with drivers, affiliates and clients constantly. - Strong internet connection (minimum 25 Mbps download / 10 Mbps upload) with a backup connection, plus a backup power source. You must be reachable at all times during your shift. - Comfortable working U.S. Eastern Time hours, including early mornings, evenings or weekends depending on the shift assigned. - Confident with WhatsApp (groups, voice notes, quick replies) and Google Sheets (data entry, filters, formulas at a basic level). - Calm under pressure, extremely organized, and able to make quick decisions without waiting to be told. Strongly preferred - Experience in limousine, black-car, taxi/rideshare, NEMT, airport transportation, courier, or food-delivery dispatch. - Working knowledge of the New York Tri-State area: JFK, LGA, EWR, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, Westchester, Long Island, New Jersey and Connecticut - including typical drive times and traffic patterns. - Experience dispatching from affiliate networks or job-posting groups where trips are claimed first-come, first-served. - Familiarity with limo/black-car software or booking platforms. Please note: 3PL trucking, truckload scheduling and HVAC dispatch experience can be helpful, but those industries operate very differently from limousine and taxi dispatch. If your background is only in those areas, please explain clearly in your application how you would handle live passenger transportation, airport pickups and jobs that must be claimed within seconds. HOW TO APPLY Apply with the subject line: BLACK CAR DISPATCHER - [YOUR NAME] In your application, answer all of the following. Applications that do not answer every question will not be reviewed. 1. Describe your dispatch experience. What industry, how many drivers/trips per day, and what tools did you use? 2. Have you dispatched passenger transportation (limo, black car, taxi, NEMT, airport)? Give one specific example of a problem trip and how you solved it. 3. A trip is posted in a WhatsApp group: JFK pickup at 6:00 PM today, drop-off in Midtown Manhattan. Walk us through, step by step, exactly what you check and do in the first 60 seconds. 4. Attach a screenshot of a speed test (speedtest.net) taken on the connection you would use for work, and tell us your backup internet and backup power setup. 5. What hours are you available in U.S. Eastern Time? 6. How familiar are you with the NYC Tri-State area? Roughly how long is JFK to Midtown at 5:00 PM on a weekday? Shortlisted candidates will complete a short paid live-dispatch trial (WhatsApp + Google Sheets) before hiring.

title: Part-Time Customer Experience Representative
description: About Teton Teton creates dependable outdoor gear designed to help people enjoy life outside.
