description: We are an Australian metalwork company seeking an experienced Senior AutoCAD Drafter and Project Coordinator to join our team remotely on a full-time basis. The primary responsibility of this role is producing accurate and practical AutoCAD 2D shop drawings for architectural and structural metalwork. The successful applicant must also be capable of independently coordinating projects and communicating professionally with clients, architects, engineers, builders and other consultants. Our typical scope includes: * Balustrades and handrails * Privacy and decorative screens * Louvres and sunshades * Gates and fences * Awnings and pergolas * Façade elements and architectural metalwork * General structural steel and aluminium components Key responsibilities: * Prepare general arrangement, fabrication and installation drawings using AutoCAD 2D * Interpret architectural, structural and consultant drawings * Develop practical connection, fixing, fabrication and installation details * Identify clashes, discrepancies, constructability issues and missing information * Prepare and manage RFIs, drawing registers, material schedules and transmittals * Revise drawings promptly based on client and consultant comments * Coordinate shop-drawing submissions, reviews and approvals * Communicate professionally with clients, architects, engineers and builders * Attend and actively participate in online design and coordination meetings * Prepare meeting minutes and follow up outstanding actions * Resolve design and coordination matters independently wherever possible * Manage assigned projects from initial documentation through to shop-drawing approval * Maintain organised project records and correspondence * Assist with general project administration * Occasionally assist with quantity take-offs and estimating when drafting workloads are lighter The successful applicant must not simply copy information from architectural or structural drawings. You must be able to review the entire design, identify potential problems and produce coordinated drawings that can be practically manufactured and installed. Mandatory qualifications and experience: * Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Architecture or another relevant discipline * Strong professional experience using AutoCAD 2D * Previous drafting experience in architectural metalwork, façades, balustrades, louvres, screens, aluminium or structural steel * Good understanding of fabrication, connections and installation requirements * Ability to work with Bluebeam Revu * Professional written and spoken English * Confidence communicating directly with clients, architects, engineers and builders * Ability to attend and actively participate in online coordination meetings * Ability to manage assigned projects and resolve issues with minimal supervision * Strong organisational and project administration skills * Exceptional attention to detail and a high level of accuracy * Ability to produce drawings quickly without compromising quality * Excellent responsiveness during agreed working hours * Ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines and priorities * Reliable computer and high-speed internet connection * Availability to work hours that provide reasonable overlap with Sydney business hours Software requirements: The successful applicant must have their own computer and access to a recent, properly licensed version of AutoCAD. AutoCAD software and licensing will not be provided by the company. Applicants must also be able to use Bluebeam Revu confidently. A Bluebeam licence may be provided if required. Experience with Revit, SketchUp and estimating will be considered an advantage but is not essential. This is a long-term, full-time remote position. The right person will be trusted to manage assigned projects independently and will have opportunities to take on greater project coordination and estimating responsibilities based on their performance and capability. To apply, please provide: 1. Your CV 2. Details of your university degree 3. Examples of relevant shop drawings or a portfolio 4. Details of your metalwork or façade drafting experience 5. Examples of projects you have coordinated directly with clients and consultants 6. Your level of AutoCAD, Bluebeam, Revit and SketchUp experience 7. Your project administration and estimating experience 8. Confirmation that you have access to a recent licensed version of AutoCAD 9. Your expected monthly salary 10. Your availability to commence Shortlisted applicants will be given a drafting and coordination assessment to demonstrate their technical understanding, speed, accuracy, drawing quality, attention to detail and communication skills.

title: Proofreader & KDP Formatting Specialist
description: # Job Posting: Proofreader & KDP Formatting Specialist **Project:** Beauty Reimagined Spiritual Productivity Planner **Type:** Freelance / Contract (Project-Based) **Format:** Remote --- ## About the Project Beauty Reimagined (BR) is a faith-lifestyle brand publishing a 12-month, faith-based spiritual productivity planner for women of faith. The manuscript is a large, image-rich Word document (600+ pages) built with a consistent monthly structure — devotionals, declarations, scripture reflections, goal-setting pages, weekly schedules, daily intention grids, and reflection sections — wrapped in a custom deep-plum-and-gold design. We're looking for a detail-oriented freelancer to take the manuscript through its final two steps before it goes live on Amazon: a full proofread, and conversion into a fully KDP-compliant, print-ready file. --- ## Scope of Work **1. Proofreading** - Read through the full manuscript for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and typographical errors - Check consistency of scripture references, quotation formatting, and recurring phrases across all 12 months - Flag any repeated or missing content (e.g., duplicated pages, inconsistent section structure between months) - Verify dates, headers, and labels are accurate and consistent throughout - Deliver a marked-up list of corrections (tracked changes or a separate issues log — your preference) **2. KDP Formatting & Conversion** - Convert the corrected manuscript into a print-ready file that meets Amazon KDP's current paperback specifications, including: - Correct trim size, margins, and gutter for an 8.5" x 11" trim at the book's final page count - Proper bleed setup if any full-bleed images are present (uniform page size across the entire interior file — no mixed bleed/non-bleed pages) - Embedded fonts, flattened transparency, no crop marks/metadata/placeholder text - Correct, sequential pagination - Export to a KDP-compliant PDF - Run the file through KDP's online previewer (or equivalent QA) and resolve any flagged issues before final delivery - Confirm final page count is even and within KDP's allowed range for the trim size --- ## Deliverables - Proofread manuscript with all corrections applied (Word .docx) - Final print-ready, KDP-compliant interior PDF - A short summary of any formatting decisions made or issues encountered --- ## Requirements **Core Skills** - Proven experience proofreading long-form manuscripts (books, planners, workbooks, or similar) - Hands-on experience formatting interiors for Amazon KDP specifically (not just general PDF/Word design) - Comfortable working with Microsoft Word at scale (300+ page documents, styles, section breaks, mirrored margins) - Strong attention to detail and consistency across repetitive, templated content **Technical / Software** - Adobe Acrobat (or equivalent) for final PDF quality checks — embedded fonts, flattened transparency, no stray metadata before upload - Working knowledge of font embedding — this manuscript uses custom fonts (Playfair Display, Cormorant Garamond), and KDP will reject a file if fonts aren't properly embedded - Comfortable working with large, image-heavy Word files (600+ pages, dozens of embedded images) — this is a different scale than a typical manuscript - Basic image/DPI literacy — able to identify a low-resolution image before it becomes a print problem **Process & Reliability** - Version control discipline — this manuscript has gone through 25+ revisions, so tracking changes without silently overwriting prior fixes is essential - Ability to follow an established style guide and preserve locked-in phrasing choices, rather than "correcting" them to personal preference - Willingness to sign a simple confidentiality agreement, as this is unpublished original content **Content-Specific** - Care and precision verifying quoted scripture references match the cited translation exactly - Sensitivity to devotional/spiritual tone — this is not a project for aggressive line-editing or rewriting of voice **Practical** - A realistic turnaround estimate provided upfront, given the file size and scope - Willingness to complete one month as a paid test/sample before taking on the full 12-month project ## Nice to Have - Experience with tools like Vellum, Atticus, InDesign, or Affinity Publisher for print layout - Portfolio or samples of previously formatted KDP paperbacks - Familiarity with faith-based or lifestyle publishing content --- ## How to Apply Please include: 1. A brief note on your relevant proofreading and KDP formatting experience 2. Links or samples of at least one KDP paperback you've formatted (interior file or published listing) 3. Your estimated turnaround time and rate for a project of this scope --- *Beauty Reimagined / Beauty Powerhouse Chicago — faith-lifestyle brand and boutique salon based on Chicago's South Side.*

title: MICROSOFT AUTOMATION ENGINEER
description: MICROSOFT AUTOMATION ENGINEER Employment Type: Full-Time Work Arrangement: Remote / Offshore Department: Automation & Business Systems Reports To: AI & Business Systems Manager / Senior Management ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Microsoft Automation Engineer who can design, build, integrate, and maintain business automation solutions using the Microsoft ecosystem. This role is for someone who enjoys turning manual and repetitive business processes into reliable, scalable, and intelligent automated systems. You will work across Microsoft Power Automate, Power Apps, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Dataverse, Power BI, Copilot Studio, APIs, and AI-powered workflows. The ideal candidate is not simply a workflow builder. You should understand how systems connect, how data moves between platforms, how APIs work, and how to build automations that are reliable enough for real business operations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES • Design and develop automated business processes using Microsoft Power Automate. • Build cloud flows, approvals, scheduled workflows, event-driven automations, and integrations. • Develop AI-powered agents and workflows using Microsoft Copilot Studio. • Connect Microsoft services, third-party applications, and internal systems using APIs and connectors. • Work with REST APIs, HTTP requests, JSON, webhooks, authentication, and data transformation. • Build solutions using SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Dataverse, Excel, Teams, Outlook, and other Microsoft services. • Develop Power Apps when a user interface is required for an automation. • Integrate automation with Power BI and business reporting workflows when appropriate. • Design automated document-processing and data-extraction workflows. • Implement AI-assisted processes using Copilot, Copilot Studio, AI Builder, Azure AI, or related Microsoft AI services. • Troubleshoot failed flows, API errors, authentication issues, data problems, and integration failures. • Implement error handling, logging, notifications, retries, and monitoring. • Follow proper development, testing, deployment, and production practices. • Document automation architecture, workflows, dependencies, and technical processes. • Identify manual processes that can be eliminated, simplified, or automated. • Work with business stakeholders to translate operational requirements into technical automation solutions. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Technical Skills • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Power Automate. • Strong understanding of Power Platform. • Experience with Microsoft 365 services such as SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, and Excel. • Experience working with APIs and HTTP requests. • Understanding of REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, authentication, and data structures. • Experience with Power Automate expressions and dynamic content. • Ability to troubleshoot and debug complex workflows. • Understanding of automation architecture and integration patterns. • Experience handling errors, retries, exceptions, and failed automation runs. • Experience working with data from multiple systems. • Understanding of environment management and deployment practices. AI & Agent Skills • Experience with Microsoft Copilot Studio is highly preferred. • Understanding of AI agents, prompts, tools, knowledge sources, and agent workflows. • Experience integrating AI into business processes. • Familiarity with AI Builder, Azure AI, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or similar Microsoft AI technologies is an advantage. • Ability to identify practical business use cases for AI automation. DEVELOPMENT & INTEGRATION SKILLS Candidates should be comfortable working with: • REST APIs • HTTP / HTTP actions • JSON • Webhooks • OAuth / API authentication • Power Automate expressions • Microsoft Graph API • JavaScript or Python is a strong advantage • SQL or database concepts are an advantage • Git / version control is an advantage PRODUCTION & ENGINEERING MINDSET The successful candidate should understand that automation is software used by real people and businesses. You should be able to: • Build automations that are reliable and maintainable. • Design proper error handling and recovery. • Prevent duplicate processing. • Validate data before performing actions. • Handle API failures and rate limits. • Create reusable components and standardized patterns. • Test automations before deployment. • Maintain clear documentation. • Understand the difference between development, testing, and production environments. • Safely deploy changes without disrupting existing business processes. PORTFOLIO REQUIREMENT A portfolio or personal website is REQUIRED. Your portfolio must demonstrate actual automation, integration, AI, Power Platform, or software projects that you have built. Examples may include: • Power Automate workflows • Microsoft Copilot Studio agents • Power Apps • API integrations • AI automation • Document automation • Business process automation • Microsoft 365 integrations • Dashboards and reporting automation • Custom applications or tools Applications without a portfolio or personal website may not be considered. IMPORTANT APPLICATION INSTRUCTION To demonstrate attention to detail, candidates MUST add the exact word: PROD_ACTIVE immediately before their email application when submitting their application. Example: Applications that do not follow this instruction may be automatically rejected. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR We are looking for someone who: • Thinks in systems and processes. • Can understand a business problem and design the technical solution. • Does not rely solely on templates or tutorials. • Can troubleshoot when an automation breaks. • Understands APIs and integrations. • Can work independently. • Takes ownership of automation projects from requirements through deployment. • Is curious about AI and emerging Microsoft technologies. • Builds solutions with reliability and maintainability in mind. • Can explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS • Microsoft Power Platform certifications. • Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Functional Consultant Associate. • Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Developer Associate. • Microsoft Certified: Power Automate RPA Developer Associate. • Experience with Microsoft Copilot Studio. • Experience with Azure. • Experience with Microsoft Graph. • Experience with Dataverse. • Experience with Power BI. • Experience with Azure AI or Microsoft Foundry. • Experience building enterprise-grade automation solutions. • Experience working with CI/CD or deployment pipelines. • Experience with governance, security, and Power Platform environments. EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Technology, or a related field is preferred but not mandatory. • 2+ years of hands-on experience in automation, software development, Power Platform, systems integration, or a related technical field. • Demonstrated project experience may substitute for formal education or years of experience. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE Within this role, you will be expected to identify inefficient processes, design automation solutions, build and test them, integrate them with existing systems, and continuously improve them. The goal is not simply to create more workflows. The goal is to build reliable systems that reduce manual work, minimize errors, improve operational visibility, and allow the business to scale more efficiently.

title: Executive Assistant / OBM / Operations Manager
description: About the Role Our client is a compliance consulting and internal audit firm. They implement international management system standards and run internal audits for companies in electronics recycling, IT asset disposition, and manufacturing across North America. Their clients use that work to prepare for and hold third-party certifications. The team is small and senior, and they hold their own operations to the same standard they hold their clients to: documented, repeatable, and not dependent on one person's memory. Right now a large volume of daily operational work sits on the founder's desk. Around 45 recurring administrative and IT tasks are documented, along with a long tail of requests that have never been written down at all. This role takes them over. The business is also part way through replacing a stack of spreadsheets, email threads, and automations with custom software, with the first phase going live shortly. A lot of what you learn manually in your first months will be automated in your later ones. They need someone who understands why the current process works the way it does, so that when the new system takes over, someone there can still tell when it is producing the wrong answer. Some context on what it is like to work here. The team is small and growing, and there is no department to hand something to. If you spot a problem, you either own it or you flag it, and both are fine. Priorities move, several things run at once, and you will report directly to the Managing Director with no layer in between. As the company grows this role will change shape more than once. That suits some people and frustrates others, and it is worth knowing which one you are before you apply. This is not a role where you wait to be told the same thing twice. You learn a process, run it correctly, write down what the instructions were missing, and then help make it faster. What You'll Own Workflow, Automation and Documentation (about 40%) Learn each recurring process by running it manually and correctly before proposing to change it Write and update standard operating procedures as you go, flagging what is missing, outdated, or wrong Build automations and AI-assisted workflows for repetitive work, stored in portable form the company owns rather than locked inside one platform Maintain existing automations across the connected tools: diagnose failures, find where a handoff broke, fix or escalate Review automated output on a defined cycle rather than assuming it stays correct. An automation that quietly produces the wrong result is worse than a manual step, and catching that is part of this role. Support the rollout of the new operating platform: test workflows, migrate and clean data, own the approval steps the system routes to a person, and report what is not working Complete the outstanding data migration work, including backfilling historical engagement records that were never entered into the system of record Maintain the SOP library and the automation library side by side, with consistent naming and version control Keep a running log of every task you are asked to do and every question you had to ask to complete it Report monthly on which tasks were automated and how many hours of manual work that removed. This is the primary measure of the role. Operations Execution (about 40%) Run the new-engagement launch sequence, two to three times a week, across four connected systems Act as the operational glue: keep projects moving, chase what is stuck, and handle the daily requests that keep the firm running Take on work delegated directly by the Managing Director, ranging from research and follow-up to standing responsibilities that move off her desk permanently as you demonstrate you can hold them Quality check the output of the processes you run and the automations you build: verify results against the source, catch errors before they reach a client or a report, and correct the process rather than only the instance Support the quality review process: upload and format audit reports, run and check an AI-assisted first-pass review, track what is waiting on whom, and keep reports from stalling between reviewer and auditor. (You will not perform the review or make audit judgments — you keep the queue moving.) Handle certificate of insurance requests, vendor onboarding packets, and W-9 issuance Maintain the vendor and subcontractor register and the supporting documentation set Calendar and inbox support for leadership, including meeting notes, action item tracking, and follow-through to completion Systems Administration and Records (about 20%) Provision accounts and access for new team members across Google Workspace and eight other platforms, and support onboarding and offboarding Maintain the Google Drive structure, permissions, naming conventions, and file cleanup Maintain the software subscription register: what renews when, what nobody uses, what should be cancelled Maintain email marketing list hygiene: before every send, confirm no unsubscribed contacts remain on the active mailing list Support hiring logistics, credential tracking, and HR administration Bookkeeping and finance are a separate role. You will work alongside the bookkeeper, and there are handoff points between you, but you do not own the finance cycle. What You Bring Six or more years in an operations, executive assistant, business management, or process coordination role supporting leadership directly Experience in a company where processes were not fully documented, and you were part of fixing that Demonstrated experience building or maintaining workflows and automations, in any tool Excellent written English. You will draft internal and occasional external communications. Proven ability to follow a written procedure exactly, and to notice and report when the procedure is wrong Real working use of AI tools. You should be able to tell us about a specific repetitive task you handed to an AI tool, which tool you used, how you set it up, and how you check that its output is correct. title: Bookkeeper
description: About the Role Our client is a compliance consulting and internal audit firm. They implement international management system standards and run internal audits for companies in electronics recycling, IT asset disposition, and manufacturing across North America. Their clients use that work to prepare for and hold third-party certifications. The team is small and senior, and they hold their own operations to the same standard they hold their clients to: documented, repeatable, and not dependent on one person's memory. They are looking for a Bookkeeper to own the day to day accuracy of their financial records — transaction processing, coding, reconciliation, and the disciplined execution of the payables, receivables, and payroll cycles. This role carries more weight than the title usually implies. Most bookkeeping roles are volume roles. This one is a judgment role with volume attached. Multi-phase engagements bill on milestones, subcontractor invoices have to be matched against agreed rates before anything moves, and expense submissions get checked against policy rather than waved through. The hard part is not entering the transaction, it is knowing where it belongs and saying so when you are not sure. Expect 25 to 30 hours a week during onboarding and training, settling to around 20 once you are running the cycle independently. Hours grow from there: transaction volume is rising, the second company is just launching, and the more of the repetitive work you systematise and take on, the faster the role moves toward full time. You would support two companies under the same ownership. The second is newly launching as an extension of the services the first provides, which means you will be setting up its finance processes rather than inheriting them, and keeping the records for the two entities cleanly separated as it grows. Some context on what it is like to work here. The team is small and growing, and there is no finance department behind you. You will report directly to the Managing Director with no layer in between, and the volume of transactions is rising as both companies grow. Priorities move and several things run at once, but the finance cycle still has to close on time and correctly every month. Holding both of those at once is the job. The business is also part way through replacing a stack of spreadsheets, email threads, and automations with custom software. A meaningful part of this role is learning how the finance processes work today, documenting them properly, and automating the parts that should not need a person at all. We want someone who reaches for a system before they reach for a repetitive workaround. What You'll Own Accounts Payable and Contractor Payment Process vendor bills daily, coding each to the correct account, customer, class, and billable flag in QuickBooks Online Match subcontractor invoices against project records, agreed rates, and time tracking before anything is queued for payment Review contractor expense submissions against the travel and expense policy, and flag exceptions rather than processing them Prepare the semi-monthly payment run and produce the run summary for approval Maintain vendor records, W-9s, and the onboarding documentation set Billing and Accounts Receivable Run the monthly invoicing cycle from time tracking into QuickBooks, ensuring every completed engagement is billed accurately and completely, including recoverable expenses Apply milestone and deposit billing terms correctly for multi-phase engagements Maintain the collections log on a weekly cycle: refresh status, issue past-due notices, and track follow-up dates Report debtor ageing and escalate anything past the defined threshold rather than carrying it quietly Reconciliation and Record Integrity Perform monthly bank, credit card, and inter-system reconciliations on the defined cycle Investigate and resolve reconciling items rather than carrying them forward Maintain expense categorization consistency and flag coding that does not fit the existing chart of accounts Prepare the month-end close file and supporting schedules for review Payroll and Statutory Support Own the payroll change cycle: enter approved new hires, approved terminations, and approved rate or salary changes into the payroll system Verify that every approved change has been entered before the cutoff, and prepare the payroll change summary for review Prepare the monthly payroll run, ensuring deductions, classifications, and filings are correct and on time. (Approval of the underlying changes, review of the change report, and final approval and submission of payroll all sit with the Managing Director.) Maintain a clean distinction between payroll and contractor payment per engagement classification Prepare annual contractor tax forms Assemble the underlying numbers for state tax filings, workers' compensation premium audits, and annual insurance renewals You prepare and support these. You do not own the filing decision or the external relationships. Systems, Documentation and Automation Run each finance process manually and correctly before proposing to change it Write and update the procedure for every recurring task you own, flagging what is missing, outdated, or wrong Build automations and AI-assisted workflows for the repetitive, rules-based work, and store them in a form the company owns rather than locked inside one platform Quality check automated output on a defined cycle rather than assuming it stays correct Support the migration of finance data and workflows into the new operating platform, and own the approval steps it routes to a person Keep a running log of every task you are asked to do and every question you had to ask to complete it Report monthly on which tasks were automated and how many hours of manual work that removed What You Bring Six or more years of hands-on bookkeeping experience, ideally in a professional or technical services environment Demonstrable QuickBooks Online experience: coding, reconciling, invoicing, and closing. Not familiarity — this has been your actual job. Accuracy under volume, and the discipline to resolve a reconciling item rather than carry it The judgment to reason about where a transaction belongs, and the honesty to say "I am not sure about this one" instead of guessing Real working use of AI tools. You should be able to describe a specific repetitive task you handed to an AI tool, which tool you used, how you set it up, and how you verify the output. Experience building or maintaining a workflow or automation in any tool, or clear evidence you look for the systemic fix rather than repeating the workaround Strong written English Ability to record your screen and narrate what you are doing clearly Strong advantages CPA, or an equivalent national professional accountancy qualification A degree in accounting, finance, or a related field Experience maintaining books for more than one entity under common ownership Experience with time tracking systems, relational database tools, expense and card management platforms, payroll providers, or workflow automation platforms Experience through a finance system migration or accounting software implementation Exposure to a regulated, audited, or ISO-certified environment Experience supporting a US-based firm How Success Is Measured 100% of completed engagements invoiced within the defined period Debtor days within agreed target 100% of reconciliations completed on cycle, with no unresolved items carried forward Month-end close file delivered within the agreed timetable Zero payments released against unmatched or unverified documentation Coding accuracy verified on review sample A written procedure exists for every recurring task in the role, and each one is reviewed and updated on a defined cycle rather than written once and left Procedures updated promptly as processes change, including the full rewrite required when the new platform replaces a manual workflow Both entities closed cleanly and separately, with no cross-coding between them Documented reduction in manual hours through automation, reported monthly How to Apply Complete our application form here: ---------- It takes about ten minutes. To confirm you have read this posting in full, include the code BK-2026-READ where the application asks for it. We will respond to every applicant who completes the form.

Our target is under 2 minutes on live chat, and you'll be moving between Intercom, Slack, email, phone, and partner channels all shift. If you go quiet, this role won't work Comfortable using a support platform. We use Intercom (very similar to Zendesk) inbox, macros, tagging, help center articles Comfortable working with AI tools. Joven and our team leads run daily stand-ups and are available on Slack throughout your shift WORKLOAD & DAYS/TIMES OF WORK We'll start on a 1-month fully paid trial (we both see how we work together) ~45 hours per week to start We staff support 7 days a week across multiple shifts, including overnight. Hot Tanks manages the content strategy, planning, approvals, scheduling, and publishing. ## What You Will Edit Content may include: * Educational and expert videos * Client testimonials and review videos * Short testimonial clips * Installation and project footage * Before-and-after videos * Field B-roll * Technician and TEAM introductions * Service-quality and Signature Standard videos * Client journey and “what to expect” videos * Community content * Behind-the-scenes and TEAM culture content ## Core Responsibilities You will: * Review raw footage provided by Hot Tanks. * Select the strongest usable moments. * Remove mistakes, long pauses, repeated takes, and unusable footage. * Create clean, natural edits with strong pacing. * Keep speakers sounding natural and human. * Add approved: * Logos * Lower thirds * Captions * Text overlays * Service labels * Transition cards * End frames * Calls to action * Make basic adjustments to: * Audio * Exposure * Colour * Framing * Add B-roll when it improves the story or explanation. * Create vertical and horizontal versions when required. * Create thumbnails when required. * Export videos in the correct dimensions, resolution, and file format. * Keep project files and finished exports organized. * Complete reasonable revisions based on consolidated Hot Tanks feedback. ## Common Video Formats Typical work may include: ### 9:16 Vertical Video * Instagram Reels * Facebook Reels * YouTube Shorts ### 16:9 Horizontal Video * YouTube Main Videos * Website videos * Facebook native video ### Other Common Deliverables * 15–30 second clips * 30–60 second short-form videos * 1–3 minute videos * Thumbnails * Occasional longer-form videos when required Some source footage may require more than one finished format. For example, the same source footage may be edited into both a vertical and horizontal version. ## Editing Style Hot Tanks content should feel: * Professional * Clear * Warm * Trustworthy * Clean * Calm * Natural * Consistent The goal is not to make every video flashy or heavily produced. The finished video should help the viewer feel: * “I understand what they are explaining.” * “These people know what they are doing.” * “They seem professional.” * “I would feel comfortable having them in my home.” ## We Prefer * Clean cuts * Natural pacing * Easy-to-read captions * Simple graphics * Consistent branding * Strong opening moments * Useful B-roll * Minimal unnecessary effects * Clear endings and calls to action ## Please Avoid * Excessive animation * Distracting transitions * Aggressive zooming * Overused sound effects * Excessive text * Meme-style editing unless specifically requested * Trend-heavy editing that weakens the Hot Tanks brand * Editing that changes the meaning of what someone said ## Brand Protection The Video Editor must follow approved Hot Tanks brand assets, templates, and editing standards. Do not independently: * Change logos. * Change brand colours. * Rewrite approved company promises or standards. * Create new company claims. * Change the meaning of a client testimonial. * Add pricing, guarantees, technical claims, or promotional language that was not provided or approved. * Publish content directly unless specifically authorized. Hot Tanks controls final approval and publishing. ## Monthly Work Structure Work will normally be provided in organized batches rather than as isolated one-off videos. The monthly workload may include a mix of: * Short-form videos * Simple edits * Alternate versions of the same source footage * Testimonial edits * Educational videos * Mid-length videos * Occasional longer-form pieces * Thumbnails The mix and volume of work may vary slightly from month to month within the agreed scope. The agreed monthly flat rate covers the regular editing workload established between Hot Tanks and the selected editor. One consolidated revision round per assignment is normally expected. ## What Hot Tanks Provides Hot Tanks will provide: * Raw footage * Content direction * Required dimensions * Brand assets * Reference examples when needed * Required text, labels, or end frames * Editing instructions * Consolidated feedback The editor is not expected to independently create the overall content strategy. ## What We Are Looking For The right person should have: * Strong short-form video editing skills. * Good pacing and storytelling judgement. * Experience editing vertical and horizontal video. * Experience preparing social-media-ready content. * Strong attention to detail. * Reliable file organization. * Strong written English for captions and on-screen text. * Ability to follow templates, instructions, and standards consistently. * Ability to receive feedback and apply it without repeatedly making the same corrections. * Reliable communication. * Reliable turnaround. * Good judgement about when to cut and when to let a moment breathe. Experience with home services, trades, testimonials, educational content, or local-business marketing is helpful but not required. ## Software You may use professional editing software such as: * Adobe Premiere Pro * DaVinci Resolve * Final Cut Pro * CapCut * Similar professional editing software We care more about the quality and consistency of the finished work than the specific software used. ## What Success Looks Like A successful Video Editor: * Learns the Hot Tanks editing style. * Delivers clean, publication-ready videos. * Requires fewer corrections over time. * Keeps branding consistent. * Meets agreed deadlines. * Keeps files organized. * Communicates clearly. * Handles repeatable monthly production reliably. * Turns raw footage into useful finished assets the Hot Tanks TEAM can publish confidently. ## Compensation **Monthly Compensation Range: $500–$1,000 CAD** This is an ongoing freelance/contract editing role. The final monthly rate will be agreed upon based on: * Experience * Editing quality * Efficiency * Ability to follow the Hot Tanks editing standard * Communication and reliability * Agreed monthly workload We are looking for a flat monthly arrangement that reflects the agreed workload rather than pricing every individual video separately. ## Paid Test Project Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a paid test editing project using actual Hot Tanks footage. The purpose of the test is to allow both Hot Tanks and the editor to determine whether the working relationship is a good fit before entering into an ongoing monthly arrangement. The paid test will evaluate: * Editing quality * Pacing and storytelling * Ability to follow instructions * Brand consistency * Caption and on-screen text accuracy * Attention to detail * Communication * Turnaround time and reliability * Ability to apply feedback The test project will be compensated at an agreed project rate before the work begins. Completion of the paid test does not guarantee an ongoing contract. Candidates whose work is a strong fit may be offered the monthly freelance editing role. This role is focused on turning approved Hot Tanks footage into strong, consistent, publication-ready video content.

title: YouTube Documentary Video Editor – Long-Form Faceless Channel

description: # YouTube Documentary Video Editor – Long-Form Faceless Channel We are looking for a talented **YouTube Documentary Video Editor** to join a growing faceless YouTube channel. Our videos are story-driven documentaries focused on **Canada, cities, regional identity, history, culture, politics, economics, rivalries, and major events**. Typical videos will be approximately **20–40 minutes long**. This is not a simple “put stock footage over a voiceover” editing job. We are looking for an editor who understands **storytelling, pacing, viewer retention, visual variety, and documentary-style editing**. ## WHAT YOU WILL RECEIVE For each video, you will generally receive: * Final voiceover * Completed script * Organized visual assets * Archival photographs and footage * B-roll * Maps, charts, screenshots and other supporting materials * Source information where relevant * Editing instructions for important sequences You will **not normally be expected to research the entire video from scratch**. However, a strong editor should be capable of finding additional appropriate visuals when something is missing or when a better visual would significantly improve the scene. ## YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES You will turn the supplied materials into a polished, engaging YouTube documentary. This includes: * Editing the complete video around the voiceover * Selecting the strongest available visuals for each narration beat * Creating strong visual pacing * Using archival photographs and footage effectively * Adding maps, headlines, screenshots, documents and graphics where appropriate * Creating simple motion graphics and animations * Adding tasteful zooms, pans and movement to still photographs * Using text and on-screen information when it strengthens the story * Adding appropriate music and sound design * Mixing audio properly * Creating smooth transitions between sections * Maintaining visual continuity and a consistent documentary style * Finding supplementary visuals when necessary * Delivering a finished video ready for YouTube ## THE EDITING STYLE The editing should feel like a **modern YouTube documentary**, not a corporate presentation and not an over-edited TikTok video. We value: **Storytelling over effects.** Every visual should help explain the story, establish a location or period, provide evidence, create emotion, or maintain viewer attention. We do NOT want random stock footage inserted simply because something needs to appear on screen. We also do not want excessive transitions, constant sound effects, unnecessary animation, or distracting editing tricks. Good judgment matters. ## WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR You should have experience editing long-form YouTube videos, documentaries, video essays, history content, geography content, or similar storytelling formats. You should understand: * YouTube audience retention * Documentary pacing * Visual storytelling * B-roll selection * Archival imagery * Music and sound design * Motion graphics * Maps and basic data visualization * How to keep a 20–40 minute video visually interesting without making it exhausting You should also be comfortable receiving detailed feedback and making revisions. ## SOFTWARE Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, or another professional editing platform is acceptable. After Effects or similar motion-graphics capability is an advantage. ## VERY IMPORTANT: COPYRIGHT You must understand basic copyright and licensing requirements. Do not download random images or footage from Google, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook or other websites and insert them into our videos without authorization. Any additional assets you source must have appropriate licensing or usage rights, and the source must be documented. ## PAID TEST Shortlisted applicants may be asked to complete a **small paid editing test of approximately 2–3 minutes**. The same voiceover, script and asset package will be provided to shortlisted candidates so that editing quality can be compared fairly. The test will evaluate: * Storytelling * Pacing * Visual selection * Music * Sound design * Graphics * Attention to detail * Ability to follow instructions * Overall professional quality ## LONG-TERM OPPORTUNITY This is intended to become an ongoing position. We are building a library of documentary videos and expect to publish consistently. If your work is excellent, there will be regular projects available. We value editors who become familiar with the channel's visual language and improve with each video. ## TO APPLY Please send: 1. A short introduction about yourself. 2. Links to **2–3 of your best long-form YouTube edits**. 3. At least one example involving documentary, history, geography, politics, economics, video essay, or similar storytelling content if available. 4. Tell us exactly what parts of those videos you personally edited. 5. Tell us what editing software you use. 6. Tell us approximately how long you would need to edit a polished 25–30 minute documentary when the voiceover, script and most visual assets are supplied. 7. Tell us your expected rate for a 25–30 minute finished video. 8. Confirm whether you are willing to complete a paid 2–3 minute editing test. **To show that you read the entire job post, begin your application with the words:** **“DOCUMENTARY EDITOR”** Applications that do not include these words may not be reviewed. Please do not send 15–20 portfolio links. Send only your strongest and most relevant work. We are looking for someone who wants to build a **long-term working relationship**, not simply complete one video.

title: Social Media Content Manager
description: Facebook • Instagram • LinkedIn | Two Personal Brands | Long-Term Opportunity We are looking for an exceptional Social Media Content Manager to help manage the personal brands of two U.S.-based insurance and financial-services professionals: a mother and daughter who work together in business. This is not a generic VA posting job. We will provide you with the raw ingredients: Photos Videos Personal stories Business activities Travel Speaking engagements Community involvement Podcast content Industry information Ideas and thoughts Context about what is happening in our lives and businesses THE TWO PERSONAL BRANDS You will be creating content for Kelly and Hailey, a mother-daughter team in the U.S. insurance and financial-services industry. They work together but have different voices, personalities and audiences. Your job is to learn both. Kelly Kelly is an experienced business owner, insurance professional, advocate, public speaker and community leader. Her content includes: Business and entrepreneurship Insurance and financial education Advocacy and public policy Leadership Community Travel Personal reflections Family Lifestyle Speaking Behind-the-scenes life Podcast content Her voice is thoughtful, confident, conversational and occasionally provocative. Hailey Hailey represents a different generation and perspective. Her content should have its own voice and should NEVER simply be a rewritten version of Kelly's content. Part of your job will be learning what makes each woman sound distinctly like herself. YOUR PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY Each day, you will receive or have access to photos, videos, ideas and context from Kelly and Hailey. You will transform those materials into platform-appropriate content for: Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Our initial content framework provides for up to: 3 content opportunities per platform, per person, per day. That means you must be capable of managing a high-volume content pipeline across six social profiles. However: We value quality over filling a quota. Not every content opportunity must become a feed post. Depending on the content and platform, you should recommend whether something belongs as: Feed post Story Reel Carousel Professional insight Personal post Short-form thought Engagement post Or should NOT be posted at all We are looking for judgment, not just output. PLATFORM DIFFERENTIATION IS REQUIRED If Kelly gives you one photograph and tells you: "I had coffee this morning with an insurance agent who reminded me how important mentorship is in our industry." We do NOT want you to write one caption and copy it three times. You should understand how to turn that ONE moment into: LinkedIn A professional thought about mentorship, leadership or developing the next generation of insurance professionals. Facebook A warmer personal story about the conversation and relationship. Instagram A shorter, visually driven caption with an engaging hook. Same person. Same photograph. Same underlying story. Three different pieces of content. That ability is central to this job. CONTENT SCHEDULE Content will generally be distributed across three U.S. audience windows: Morning: approximately 6:30–7:30 AM Pacific Time Afternoon: approximately 11:00 AM–12:30 PM Pacific Time Evening: approximately 4:30–6:00 PM Pacific Time You do NOT need to be awake at those hours. We expect you to use scheduling tools once direct publishing privileges have been granted. Over time, you will also be expected to review analytics and recommend better posting times based on OUR actual audience behavior. FIRST 30 DAYS You will NOT initially receive direct access to our social media accounts. During the training period: We provide content → You create posts → We review → We approve or revise. We will teach you our voices through feedback. Your responsibility is to learn from that feedback so the number of revisions steadily decreases. We are specifically looking for someone who can eventually reach the point where we read a post and say: "Yes. That's exactly how I would have said it." Once that trust has been established, we will provide appropriate access so you can schedule and publish approved content directly. Eventually, the right person will independently manage much of the daily publishing calendar. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE At the beginning: We correct you. Then: We occasionally correct you. Eventually: You know what we're going to say before we say it. Our ideal Social Media Content Manager learns: What Kelly will post What Kelly will NOT post What Hailey will post What Hailey will NOT post Their vocabulary Their humor Their opinions Their professional boundaries Their audiences Their preferred content styles We want someone interested in becoming part of our long-term media team. RESPONSIBILITIES You will: Create platform-specific social media copy Organize provided photos and videos Maintain a weekly content calendar Recommend content formats Create simple Canva graphics when appropriate Schedule approved content Maintain consistent personal-brand voices Repurpose podcast and business content Track published content Monitor basic performance analytics Identify which topics and formats perform best Recommend improvements monthly Maintain organized content archives Avoid repetitive posts Fact-check professional claims before submitting content Flag anything you are unsure about rather than guessing IMPORTANT: AI USE You may use AI tools to assist your work. However: We do not want AI-generated personalities. If every caption sounds polished, generic, inspirational and interchangeable, this will not work. AI can help you work faster. It cannot replace learning Kelly and Hailey's voices. We will recognize generic AI copy immediately. REQUIREMENTS You must have: Excellent written American English Strong understanding of Facebook Strong understanding of Instagram Strong understanding of LinkedIn Experience managing personal brands Excellent attention to detail Strong organizational skills Canva proficiency Experience with social scheduling tools Ability to work independently Reliable internet Ability to meet weekly deadlines Excellent judgment and discretion Experience with insurance, financial services, professional services or executive personal brands is helpful but not required. Writing ability and judgment matter more. COMPENSATION Starting compensation: $250 USD per week This is an independent contractor position. The initial engagement will include a paid two-week trial period. Compensation and responsibilities may increase as trust, independence and responsibility increase. We are interested in a long-term relationship with the right person. HOW TO APPLY: Email applications to: ---------- Begin your application with: POUR IT OVER ICE Applications that do not begin with those words will not be considered. Then answer the following: 1. Tell us about the personal brands you currently manage or have previously managed. 2. Provide examples of Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn content YOU personally wrote. 3. Tell us how you would make one story sound different on Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn. 4. How do you learn a client's writing voice? 5. What do you think is the biggest mistake business professionals make on social media? 6. What social media scheduling and analytics tools have you used? 7. How do you use AI in your content-creation process? 8. How many hours per week would you expect this role to require? 9. Are you currently working for other clients? If yes, approximately how many hours per week? 10. Why are you interested in a long-term role rather than project work? FINALIST TEST Selected finalists will receive the same: Photograph Short video Background information Personal context You will be asked to create social content from that material. The test will evaluate: Writing quality American English Kelly vs. Hailey voice differentiation Facebook vs. Instagram vs. LinkedIn differentiation Hooks Judgment Creativity Accuracy Attention to instructions We are not looking for the person who creates the most content. We're looking for the person we can eventually trust to speak in our voices.

title: Client Ops Associate
description: Client Ops Associate (Path to Key Account Manager) Full Time | Remote | Reports to Head of Ops/Delivery About the company CivSav is a digital marketing agency built specifically for agriculture and heavy machinery companies across the USA. We run SEO, Google Ads, Meta advertising, and email/lifecycle marketing (Klaviyo) for a growing roster of ag clients. We're a lean, fast-moving team — not a big-agency bureaucracy — and we're scaling from a strong client base toward 100+ accounts without losing the quality that got us here. About the role We're hiring a Client Ops Associate to be the operational backbone of our client relationships. This is not a call-center support role and it's not a senior strategist role — it's the seat where someone proves they can be trusted with a client relationship, and grows from there. You'll start by making sure nothing falls through the cracks: onboarding new clients, keeping tabs on what's been delivered versus what's been promised, and handling the day-to-day questions clients have. If you're good at this — organized, calm under pressure, and someone clients trust — this role is the direct path to owning a full book of clients as a Key Account Manager. We are deliberately hiring this as an assistant-level role with a real growth path, not a dead-end support job. The person we hire in twelve months should look nothing like the person we hire today. What success looks like - New clients are onboarded smoothly: accounts and access collected without chasing, kickoff calls run on time, nothing missed. - Clients get fast, clear answers to routine questions, and you know exactly when something needs to go to a specialist or to leadership instead of you handling it yourself. - Nothing executed for a client goes untracked. If someone asks "where are we on X client," you have the answer in under a minute. - You build a track record of good judgment — knowing what you can decide on your own and what needs a second opinion — that earns you more client ownership over time. Key responsibilities Customer support - First point of contact for routine client questions and requests. - Follow a clear escalation path: technical issues to the relevant specialist, anything involving expectations, money, or a frustrated client to your manager. - Keep client communication professional, timely, and honest — we do not overpromise to make a moment easier. Onboarding - Run new clients through our onboarding process: collecting domain, ad account,Klaviyo, and analytics access.Onboarding clients on meta and GHL. - Schedule and run kickoff calls using our onboarding playbook. - Make sure every new client is fully set up and hands off cleanly to the delivery team. Project management assistance - Track what's been executed for each client across SEO, ads, email, and web — using our shared tracking system. - Flag work that's stalled or at risk before it becomes a client complaint. - Keep a clear, current record any manager can check without needing to ask you directly. Growth path - Months 0–3: support, onboarding, and tracking, fully trained on our systems, all client-facing work reviewed before it goes out. - Months 3–6: independently own a small group of standard-tier clients — ongoing check-ins, reporting, routine decisions — with regular check-ins with your manager. - Months 6–12+: full ownership of an assigned client roster as a Key Account Manager, with review shifting to spot-checks and true escalations only. Progression is based on demonstrated judgment and reliability, not just time served. About you — required - Excellent written and verbal English communication. - Highly organized — you naturally track details without being told twice. - Comfortable talking to clients directly, including when a conversation is a little uncomfortable. - Genuinely ambitious about growing into a client-ownership role, not just looking for a support job. - Reliable internet, quiet workspace for client calls, and availability during US business hours. About you — preferred - Prior experience in an agency, customer success, or account coordination role. - Familiarity with basic digital marketing concepts (you don't need to run SEO or ads, but you should be able to follow a conversation about them). - Familiarity with GHL, Meta Business Suite - Experience with a task-tracking tool (ClickUp, Jira, spreadsheets, or similar). How to apply We read every application carefully, and we pay close attention to how instructions are followed — it tells us a lot before we ever get on a call. Subject line: "Hi, I'm YOUR NAME from CITY/COUNTRY and I'm applying for the Client Ops Associate role." In the body of your email, include: 1. A two-sentence opening: your name, where you're from, and that you're applying. 2. Three sentences on the most relevant experience you have for this specific role. 3. Three sentences on a time you had to stay organized while juggling multiple people's expectations at once — what happened, and how you kept it from falling apart. 4. Three sentences on where you want to be in two years, and why this role is a step toward that. 5. A closing line with your name, email, and phone number. Attach your current resume or CV. Candidates who follow these instructions completely move to the next stage, which includes a short scenario exercise designed to show us how you think under a bit of pressure — not to trick you, but to make sure we're both confident before we ever put you in a room with a client.

title: Creator Sourcing & Outreach VA
description: Real Mad Honey is a premium DTC brand selling wild Himalayan mad honey, sourced by hand at 3,500+ meters and third-party tested for purity. We've served 50,000+ customers and we're growing fast. We're hiring a VA who will report directly to the Creator Partnerships Manager — owning creator sourcing, outreach, and keeping our whole partnerships operation organized and easy to navigate. This is a hands-on assisting role, not just task execution: you'll be the person who makes sure nothing falls through the cracks. RESPONSIBILITIES Finding Creators • Look online for creators who make content we could work with. • Check if each one is really a good fit for our brand — not just how many followers they have. • Write down why each one is a good pick, so a decision can be made fast. • Be the first point of contact, and inform the manager on rates for negotiation. Organizing Our Files & Content • Keep our files and folders neat, so anyone on the team can find what they need in seconds. • When videos or photos come in from a creator, save, label, and keep track of them the right way — so nothing gets lost, and no one has to dig through a mess to find a clip later. • Keep a simple, up-to-date list of every deal: who it's with, what stage it's at, when it's due, and whether it's paid. • Make sure product gets shipped and creators get their tracking info. Helping the Manager • Tell the manager right away if a creator is doing great work — they might be worth a bigger deal. • Tell the manager right away if something's going wrong. Don't wait and hope it fixes itself. • Help build our creator community across our programs — seeding, ambassadors, and more. • Help with other small tasks as they come up. This role grows as you do. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE First 30 Days • You know the kind of creators and personas that fit our brand. • You've sourced your first few creators. • You understand our budget and know how to lock in a deal — rate, contract, all of it. • You know how our database works and how we keep it clean and organized. • You understand the different creator programs we run, the tools we use to source, and how our whole system fits together. First 60 Days • You're finding and vetting creators without needing much guidance. • Our files and content are organized well enough that someone else could jump in and understand everything. • You're catching problems early and flagging them before they get bigger. • You're starting to spot creators who could grow into bigger roles — ambassadors, repeat collaborators — and flagging them to the manager. First 120 Days • You're running the sourcing and organizing side of this role on your own. • The manager trusts your picks and your organization without double-checking. • You're already suggesting ways to make the process better. • You're helping the manager grow our creator community across all our programs — seeding, ambassadors, Trybe, and beyond. SKILLS & EXPERIENCE • Hands-on experience with UGC sourcing or creator management, ideally in a DTC or e-commerce context. • Comfortable finding and vetting talent across sourcing platforms. • Experience supporting paid ads teams and understanding how UGC feeds into performance creative. • Strong eye for creator quality — you can tell who fits the brand and who'll actually perform, before you ever send an outreach message. • Excellent written English for outreach, negotiations, and creator briefs. • Organized across multiple timelines, multiple creators, and multiple campaigns simultaneously. • Comfortable with spreadsheets/trackers and general workspace tools. MUST HAVES • Straight to the point communicator. No long, confusing instructions needed either direction. • Proactive. You don't wait to be told. • Integrity. We're remote and run on trust. • Reliable, deadline-driven, and comfortable managing your own time without needing constant check-ins. • This must be your only job. Full commitment, full presence. WHO WILL THRIVE HERE Someone organized enough that a manager can hand off a messy pile of creator info and trust it comes back usable — clear, honest, and dependable. HOW TO APPLY Send us your resume (CV) and a short intro video telling us about yourself and your motivation — we want to see your energy and how you communicate, not just read about it. If you're shortlisted, we'll send you the test assignment as the next step. Start your application with the words “Honey Hive” so we know you actually read this whole posting. We read everything. Real applications only — copy-paste responses will be ignored.

title: 🔥 HIRING: Performance Video Editor + AI Creative Specialist
job_title: 🔥 HIRING: Performance Video Editor + AI Creative Specialist
description: Help us build one of the leading kids health brands in Europe. Remote · Full-Time · Strong Base + Uncapped Performance Bonuses We’re not looking for someone who just wants another video editing job. We’re looking for one person who wants to become world-class at performance creative - and wants their income to grow with their performance. Wunderwell is a fast-growing German DTC brand building health products specifically for children. But we’re not here to build another supplement company. Our goal is to build the brand parents think of when it comes to supporting their children through the different stages and moments of growing up. And creative is going to be one of the biggest reasons we get there. That’s where you come in. This is NOT a normal editing role. We don't need someone who can make videos look pretty. We need someone who understands why people buy. You should care about: Hooks. Retention. Pacing. Emotional triggers. Buyer psychology. Direct response. UGC. Storytelling. AI. And ultimately: sales. Your creatives won't disappear into some client folder. They go live. They get real ad spend. We see exactly what happens. If they lose, we learn. If they win, we scale them. And when your creatives win, you win financially too. That feedback loop will allow you to become a much better marketer than someone who spends years editing videos without ever knowing whether they actually sold anything. What you'll actually do You'll work closely with one of our Founders and turn ideas, scripts and raw footage into ads that sell. You do not need to speak German. We provide the German scripts, copy and strategic direction. Your job is to turn them into creatives that perform. This is also not just a cut-and-caption job. A major part of this role is creating content yourself with AI - and then turning it into finished performance ads. That includes: - Cutting raw footage from our real UGC creators into high-converting Meta ads - Finding and layering the right B-roll to strengthen every line of the script - Creating strong hooks and maintaining attention throughout the video - Understanding the marketing idea behind a brief instead of blindly executing it - Studying our winning ads and understanding why they worked - Iterating winners quickly with new hooks, openings, B-roll and structures - Using AI to create footage we couldn't produce traditionally - Creating AI B-roll and AI-generated scenes - Creating realistic AI talking heads / avatars - Creating AI animations and visualizations - Using AI voiceovers and other AI-native creative formats - Constantly testing new tools and workflows that make our creatives better or faster - Looking at performance feedback and applying those learnings to your next edit We already have creators producing real footage. Your job is to turn those raw ingredients into something people stop scrolling for and eventually buy from. We want someone OBSESSED with getting better. You don't need to know every AI tool on day one. But you do need to already be an excellent editor and you need to learn insanely fast. You should be the type of person who sees a great ad and immediately wonders: "Why does this work?" Someone who saves winning ads. Studies competitors. Experiments with new AI tools before being asked. Tries a different opening because you think it could perform better. And actually shares ideas with the team. We don't want someone waiting all day for the next task. If you see an opportunity, say it. If you think our brief could be better, tell us. If you discover a new AI workflow that could change how we produce creatives, show us. You start as an editor. But editing does not have to be your ceiling. The path Performance Video Editor → Senior Editor → Creative Strategist → Creative Lead How quickly you move through that path is largely up to you. We want to teach you how we think about: Direct response marketing. Customer research. Hooks & angles. Copywriting. Creative strategy. Meta advertising. AI creative production. Performance analysis. Our goal isn't to have you pushing buttons for us for the next three years. Our goal is to make you dangerous. Someone who can eventually look at an audience, understand what makes them buy, develop an angle, build the creative and analyze whether it worked. And we reward performance. There will be a competitive monthly base salary depending on your skill and experience. But that's only the starting point. On top of your base, you'll earn performance bonuses for winning creatives. We want incentives aligned: When Wunderwell grows because of your work, you should participate in that upside. The better you become → the better your creatives perform → the more responsibility you earn → the more money you can make. We're not interested in artificially capping an A-player. If you become extremely valuable to Wunderwell, we want this to become an extremely valuable position for you. We would rather overpay one great editor than underpay three average ones. Who we're looking for You probably fit if: - You already have a strong video editing portfolio - You've edited direct-response / DTC / e-commerce ads before - You understand that an ad's job is to sell, not win a design award - You're extremely comfortable with modern AI tools - You can create convincing AI video, B-roll, talking heads and animations - You're fast without becoming sloppy - You're reliable and communicate quickly - You take direct feedback without ego - You're curious about marketing beyond editing - You take ownership instead of waiting to be managed - You genuinely want to become exceptional at what you do Experience in supplements, health, wellness or parenting is a plus - but hunger and ability matter more. DO NOT APPLY IF: - You want a comfortable 9–5 where you finish your assigned edits and collect your paycheck. - You need someone to constantly tell you what to do. - You disappear when things get busy. - You take direct feedback personally. - You need three days for an edit that should take a few hours. - You care more about cinematic transitions than conversion. - You aren't interested in AI. - You aren't interested in understanding the numbers behind your creatives. - Or you're looking to do the minimum required. There are easier jobs. This isn't one of them. Why Wunderwell? Because you're joining early enough that your work can actually matter. We're ambitious. We're building quickly. We're constantly testing. And we want people around us who see that as an opportunity rather than pressure. You'll work closely with the people making the decisions. You'll see what happens to the creatives you make. You'll learn from real performance data. You'll get access to the tools you need. You'll be encouraged to experiment with AI. You'll have room to take ownership far beyond editing. And if you become one of the people who helps us turn Wunderwell into a major European brand, we want you to grow with it. We're not looking for someone to fill an editing seat. We're looking for someone who wants to earn their seat at the table. How to apply We're intentionally making the hiring process difficult. Portfolio → Short Interview → Paid Test Edit → Final Call We care much more about what you can actually do than what your CV says. One important thing: Start your application with I'M ALL IN FOR WUNDERWELL so we know you actually read the entire post. Applications without it will NOT be considered. When applying, send us: 1. Your 3 best performance ads Not your prettiest videos. Show us ads you believe actually sell. 2. Your best AI creative Show us what you can do with modern AI video tools. 3. One ad you personally think is brilliant It doesn't need to be yours. Tell us in 3–5 sentences why you think it works. 4. Tell us which AI tools you currently use For video, images, avatars, voice and audio. 5. How quickly can you deliver the first draft of a 30-second ad once you receive the brief and assets? 6. Your current monthly compensation expectation 7. And answer this question: Why do you want to become one of the best performance creatives in DTC? If your answer is basically "I need a remote job" - this probably isn't the right role. But if you want to spend the next few years becoming ridiculously good at performance marketing, work with people who expect a lot from you, get rewarded when your work wins, and help build something from an early stage: We want to hear from you!

title: Experienced Podcast Video Editor Needed

title: Backlink Outreach VA (Part-Time / Ongoing)

This is outreach work, not writing work. title: # Technical Recruiter – Marine / Shipyard Trades
description: # Technical Recruiter – Marine / Shipyard Trades **Part-Time | Remote | UK Company | Approx. 2 Days per Week Initially** We are a UK-based company supplying skilled technical personnel for projects aboard **cruise ships, superyachts, commercial vessels and within shipyards/dry docks**. We are looking for an experienced **Technical Recruiter** to join us on a part-time, remote basis. The successful candidate will initially work approximately **2 days per week**, with the potential for the role and hours to expand for the right person. ## The Role Your primary responsibility will be to review, screen and shortlist skilled tradespeople for marine and shipyard projects, ensuring candidates have the appropriate technical experience, qualifications and certifications before being selected for testing and potential mobilisation. You will recruit across technical trades including: * Welders / coded welders * Pipefitters and fabricators * Mechanical fitters / technicians * Electricians * Plumbers * HVAC and related mechanical trades * Other skilled marine and shipyard personnel ## Key Responsibilities You will be responsible for: * Reviewing incoming CVs and applications * Conducting initial candidate screening and telephone/video interviews * Assessing candidates' technical experience and suitability for specific projects * Reviewing welding qualifications, coding/certification and relevant trade credentials * Understanding the difference between candidates suitable for shipyard/dry-dock work and those suitable for mobilisation aboard operational vessels * Checking candidates' marine documentation and certification where required * Identifying candidates who should progress to practical trade/welding testing * Shortlisting and recommending suitable personnel to management * Maintaining accurate candidate records and recruitment pipelines * Communicating with candidates regarding documentation, testing, availability and potential mobilisation * Helping develop and maintain a reliable pool of qualified technical personnel for future projects ## Technical Knowledge Required NOTE This is **not a general recruitment or virtual assistant position**. We are specifically looking for someone who understands technical trades and can confidently assess whether a candidate's experience and qualifications are relevant. You should have good working knowledge of several of the following areas: **Welding & Fabrication** Understanding of welding processes and terminology such as TIG/GTAW, MIG/MAG/GMAW, SMAW/MMA, FCAW, welding positions, materials and coded/qualified welders. You should be comfortable reviewing welding qualifications and understanding whether a candidate's certification and experience are appropriate for the work being considered. **Mechanical / Electrical / Plumbing** Ability to understand CVs from mechanical fitters, pipefitters, electricians, plumbers and similar technical personnel and distinguish genuine relevant experience from general construction experience. **Marine / Shipyard Recruitment** Ideally, you will understand the documentation and certification that can be required when personnel work aboard vessels, cruise ships, yachts or within shipyards/dry docks. Experience dealing with areas such as STCW certification, seafarer medicals, passports/visas, seaman's books and vessel-specific requirements would be highly advantageous. You do not need to be a welder or engineer yourself, but you **must be technically confident enough to screen experienced tradespeople and ask the right questions**. ## Ideal Candidate We would particularly like to hear from candidates who have previously worked in: * Marine or maritime recruitment * Shipyard recruitment * Oil & gas / offshore recruitment * Engineering recruitment * Skilled trades recruitment * Welding/fabrication recruitment * Technical manpower or crewing agencies Previous experience recruiting Filipino skilled tradespeople for international projects would be a significant advantage. ## Working Arrangement * Fully remote position * Working for a UK-based company * Initially approximately **2 days per week**. Starting next month. * Potential to increase hours/responsibilities for the right candidate * Some availability during UK working hours will be required * Hourly rate: Negotiable depending on experience** We are more interested in finding someone with the **right technical knowledge and recruitment experience** than simply selecting the lowest hourly rate. ## How to Apply Please send your CV together with Linkedin page and a short introduction explaining your relevant recruitment experience. In your application, please specifically answer the following: 1. What experience do you have recruiting welders, mechanical trades or other skilled technical personnel? 2. Have you recruited personnel for marine, shipyard, offshore or vessel-based work? 3. What welding qualifications/certifications are you familiar with? 4. What documentation or certification would you normally check before mobilising a tradesperson to work aboard a vessel? 5. Which technical trades are you most experienced in recruiting? 6. What hourly rate are you seeking? 7. Are you available approximately 2 days per week initially? Applications that do not address these questions may not be considered. We are looking for someone who can become a trusted part of our recruitment process and, for the right candidate, there is potential for the position to develop into a larger ongoing role.

description: Dear applicant, We run a growing Shopify dropshipping operation and are scaling hard this year. We are looking for a Data & Reporting Specialist to join a new team. Which of these have you worked with, and for how long: Shopify, Facebook Ads Manager, Slack, Incogniton, Google Sheets? 2. Describe a time you spotted an error in data someone else produced. What did you do? 3. In a Google Sheet with daily ad spend and revenue per product, which numbers would you check first to see if something is off? Why? 4. What do you do when the workflow tells you one thing, but the data clearly says something else? 5. Are you available 4–10 hours a day, 7 days a week? Which hours (state your timezone)? 6. What internet speed and backup connection do you have? **Requirements:** - Experience with Facebook Ads Manager (must) - Experience with Shopify (must) - Strong written English and proactive communication (must) - Comfortable following written workflows and video training (must) - Confident in Google Sheets — filtering, cross-checking, spotting inconsistencies - Able to read data and explain what it means, not just record it - Experience with Slack - Experience with Incogniton is a plus If you do not meet these requirements, please do not apply — thank you. **Your responsibilities:** - Recording daily KPIs accurately and on time - **Verifying** the data: cross-checking numbers, catching mistakes, missing entries and outliers - **Reporting proactively**: a short daily update on what you saw, what changed, and anything that looks wrong - Raising delays or blockers immediately instead of waiting to be asked - Coordinating with team members in the same process - Working according to our strategy, workflows and schedule We provide full workflows and video training for every step of the process. We offer real career growth for team members who take ownership. If this sounds like you, apply with your answers to the questions above. Best regards, TWK
